event_narrative: Public reports a swift water rescue in the channel near the intersection of Raitt Street and Edinger Avenue in Santa Ana. Reports of 2 people swept away in the channel.

The Emergency Manager reported high water from Garner Creek flooded Persimmon Tree Road, resulting in its closure. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 10 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported high water from Garner Creek flooded Persimmon Tree Road, resulting in its closure. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 10 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported high water from Pitts Creek washed out Forrester Road. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 10 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding issues in the county including: Purvis Road washed out, Apple Valley Road home flooded, a bridge closed on Westmoreland, and the closure of Moss Farm Road. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 6 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Diamond Hill Church Road was closed due to flooding from nearby creeks and rivers. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 4 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Dixon Bridge Road was closed due to high water conditions on the North Oconee River. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the washout of Hulsey Mill Road due to high flow conditions from Mossy Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a portion of Barrett Mill Road was washed out due to high water conditions from Flat Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported that a bridge on Airport Road was completely washed away and destroyed. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Roy Powers Road was washed out due to high water conditions on Brasstown Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Carolina Springs Road was heavily damaged by flood waters, including a partial washout. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Major flooding was reported along Gulf Breeze Parkway in Gulf Breeze. A port of Da Lisa Road and the intersection of Garden Road and Commerce Road were closed near Bagdad. Flooding was also reported near the intersection of Raughton Road and Clearview Street near Garcon Point.
The Emergency Manager reported water on Main Street. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 3 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flash flooding at the intersection of Joseph E. Boone Boulevard and Vine Street. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flash flooding at Humphries Street SW, Cooper Street SW, McDaniel Street, SW, Smith Street, and at the intersection of University Avenue and Pryor Street SW. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flash flooding at the intersection of Delowe Drive and Arthur B. Langford Parkway. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a water rescue due to flash flooding in the 200 block of North Avenue NW. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a water rescue in the 1500 block of Orlando Street SW due to high water from a nearby creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flood water from Proctor Creek at the intersection of Troy Street NW and Joseph E Boone Drive NW. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flash flooding in the 2200 block of Verbana Street. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flood waters inundated apartments in the 1600 block of Battle Creek Village. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along the Flint River resulting in the closures of Upper Riverdale Road at Garden Walk Boulevard, Roxbury Drive, and Arrowhead Boulevard. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported significant flooding at the intersection of Old Rex Morrow Road and Reagan Chase due to high water conditions of Trammel Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Thompson Road was closed at two locations, and Hugh Stowers Road closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along Flat Creek in Dawsonville, resulting in the closure of Flat Creek Road, Jack Heard Road, and Maple Street South. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

A stream gauge and the public reported flash flooding developed across York County after 3 to 5 inches fell across the eastern part of the county. Public reported a tributary of Sugar Creek overflowed its banks and inundated roads and buildings in the vicinity of Regent Parkway and Heritage Blvd. A stream gauge on Tools Fork Creek northwest of Rock Hill exceeded its established flood stage, indicating partial flooding of Highway 5.

Media reported flash flooding across the South Yadkin River basin in western Iredell County after 4.5 to 6 inches of rain fell, with much of that falling in about a three hour period during the pre-dawn hours. Multiple roads were closed due to inundation, mainly from tributaries of the South Yadkin. A portion of a bridge collapsed in the far northwest part of the county. In addition, saturated soil resulted in a tree falling on and causing significant damage to a home in the Union Grove community. Finally, one person was killed when his vehicle hydroplaned on Highway 115.
A period of heavy rain, in addition on previous steady moderate to heavy rain, resulted in flooded roads across parts of Navarro Co that had to be barricaded. Other roads were impassable.

A flooded and impassable roadway was reported at Brookside Dr and Riverside Dr in Orangeburg. Observations from around the area indicated about 4 to 6 inches of rain fell over this region. Street flooding was also observed in a few other parts of the town of Orangeburg.
Numerous roads were flooded in and around Jacksonville. Some roads that were flooded were Huff Dr, Pony Farm Rd, Vandergrift Dr, Maplehurst Rd, and Walnut Dr.

A Miami Herald reporter and members of the public posted videos of significant flooding in the Biscayne Point, Normandy Isles, and North Beach neighborhoods of Miami Beach. Streets were impassable and several cars were stranded. Water also encroached on several homes. ||Rain gauges in the area measured between 3.6 and 4.7 inches of rain in 3 hours between 5:15 PM and 8:15 PM, with daily totals in the 4-6 inch range.
There were reports of two feet of water on Shore Drive. Several vehicles were stalled.

Stream gauges on the Rocky River above Irish Buffalo Creek and on Back Creek indicated flash flooding developed along tributaries of the river, including Irish Buffalo Creek and Dutch Buffalo Creek after 3.5 to 5.5 inches of rain fell across Cabarrus County, with much of that falling in about a three-hour period during the morning of the 12th. Multiple roads were inundated, including Stallings Rd, Poplar Tent Rd, Bowman-Berrier Rd, Mount Pleasant Rd, and Highway 200.

Fire dept reported flash flooding developed along Tanyard Creek after 4 to 5 inches of rain fell, with much of that falling in around three hours during the morning of the 12th. Reepsville road was inundated for several hours.

Stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along multiple streams in northern and central Rowan County after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across the area, with much of that falling in about a three-hour period during the morning. Second Creek overflowed its banks and inundated low lying areas near Cleveland. Tributaries of Second Creek, including Winthrow Creek likely flooded multiple roads south of Highway 70. Grants Creek also flooded near Salisbury.
High water was reported on several roads across the county.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed along creeks and small streams and in urban areas after 2 to 3 inches of rain fell, mostly in around three hours during the morning of the 12th. Multiple roads were closed and at least two motorists required rescue from stranded vehicles.

A stream gauge on Henry Fork exceeded its established flood stage after 3.5 to 5 inches of rain fell over Catawba County, with much of that falling during a three-hour period on the morning of the 12th. Several roads along the stream were inundated and closed.
Intersection of Airport Road and Mooretown Road was closed due to high water over the roadway.

A stream gauge on the Yadkin River near Patterson exceeded its established flood stage after 4 to 7 inches fell across the basin, with much of that falling in only 3 hours or so between midnight and daybreak on the 12th. Multiple roads and some homes were inundated in the Happy Valley community, especially between Highway 268 and the river. Additionally, a few mudslides developed in the Yadkin basin, including a large one that covered/closed Kirby Mountain Rd north of Patterson.

After 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across Appomattox county during the morning, an additional 1.75 to 2.25 inches of rain fell during the evening, most of it within a hour, as a line of slow-moving thunderstorms passed across the area. This caused numerous creeks, already running high from the earlier rainfall, to flood out of their banks. Notable among the flood reports was water about one foot deep running across Horseshoe Road. At least five water rescues were performed by emergency personnel, including one at North Creek Road where North Creek was observed flooding the roadway, and another at River Ridge Road at the Appomattox River. Additional rounds of rain of weaker intensity persisted through the late evening hours, maintaining the flooding conditions, though flash flooding ended by 11:00 pm.

Multiple personal weather stations observed 3 to 5 inches of rain during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding of Forbush Creek, including along Lace Knoll Road where is crosses over the Creek. Lace Knoll Road was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

Stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along numerous creeks throughout the Charlotte area after 3.5 to 4.5 inches of rain fell across much of the city, with the bulk of that falling in about a 3-hour period during the morning of the 12th. The most significant flooding occurred along the Sugar Creek and Little Sugar Creek basins, where several gauges reported moderate to even major flooding. Water from Sugar Creek inundated multiple buildings along Southern Pines Blvd and Red Oak Blvd. Little Sugar Creek overflowed and impacted several homes in the Parkstone neighborhood as well as several structures along Highway 51 in Pineville. On the opposite side of the city, significant flooding developed along Mallard Creek in the University City area, impacting homes on Dashiel Dr and Circle Dr. Irwin Creek also inundated Statesville Rd just north of Uptown. Steele Creek flooded in the Carowinds area, flooding several mobile homes along John Price Rd. Otherwise, multiple roads were inundated along Briar Creek and McMullen Creek in the east and southeast part of the city, and along Stewart Creek and Irwin Creek on the north side and near Uptown. Long Creek also flooded roads near Mountain Island Lake, while Clarks Creek overflowed and flooded multiple vehicles in the far north part of the city. Drainage flooding also developed along I-85N near Little Rock Rd, with multiple vehicles stranded and occupants rescued. Overall, 23 people were rescued from homes and 12 people from vehicles throughout the city.

Multiple reports of significant flooding received from the broadcast media, trained spotters, law enforcement, and NWS employees were received over the course of a day. Reports of significant street flooding and major, damaging rainfall in northern parts of the county, primarily in Miami Lakes, Country Club, Hialeah, Opa-Locka, and Miami Gardens where streets were impassable in many areas. Major flooding and impassable streets also occurred in downtown Miami and Brickell. Water entered structures in some of these areas, including Hialeah and Miami Gardens. Minor flooding was widespread county-wide. A number of stalled vehicles were reported as well. Rainfall amounts of 4 to almost 14 inches were measured across Miami-Dade County, with a little over 14 inches in Miramar, 8 to 10 inches near Hard Rock Stadium, and 5 to 9 inches in downtown Miami and Brickell.

Runoff from 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in about a one-hour time period caused flooding several inches deep to flow across the intersection of Wilkerson Road and Kentuck Road. The road was reported impassible until after the water receded.

Multiple personal weather stations observed 2 to 3 inches of rain during the early morning hours of November 12th across the upper Ararat River basin. This resulted in a rapid 8- foot rise above flood stage within a 3-hour period at the Ararat River. Extensive flooding of Riverside Park was observed during late morning as a result of this flooding.

Multiple personal weather stations observed that 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across eastern Yadkin County during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding of Forbush Creek, including along Hutchens Road where is crosses over the Creek. Hutchens Road was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

A stream gauge on Hunting Creek near Morganton indicated significant flash flooding developed along the stream after 4.5 to 6 inches of rain fell in the area, with a significant portion of that falling in the 2-3 hours prior to daybreak. Coal Chute Rd was inundated and several businesses between the river and East Fleming Dr were also flooded. Backwater effects along Fiddlers Run also resulted in flooding of Bethel Park. Additionally, spotter reported severe drainage flooding along Highway 64 at Chesterfield. Other non-specific road flooding reports were received from elsewhere in Morganton as well as in the Valdese area.

Between 5 and 8 inches of rain fell during the early morning hours, within an area with a shallow water table due to previous heavy rainfall. Showers moved onshore or developed along the coast and trained over areas south of Port Salerno, impacting Hobe Sound most significantly, and in particular Hobe Heights. Rapid inundation occurred, with standing flood waters exceeding a depth of 3 feet in portions of Hobe Heights and surrounding neighborhoods, where flood waters approached homes, overtopped culverts and creeks and caused dozens of roads to become fully or partially impassable. The flood waters were very slow to recede.

Several roads throughout Rockingham County were flooded and impassible as multiple rounds of heavy rain passed across the county. One round in Reidsville produced 1 to 1.25 inches within a 40 minute period, with rainfall rates at times of 2 to 3 inches per hour. Particularly affected was Scale Street in Reidsville.

Multiple personal weather stations observed 2 to 3 inches of rain during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding of Hogan Creek, including where the creek intersects Hogan Bridge Road, causing the bridge to be flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

Multiple personal weather stations observed 3 to 5 inches of rain during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding of Forbush Creek, including near the intersection of Griffin Road and Snider Road. Griffen Road was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

Several rounds of heavy rain passed across Rockingham County on the evening of November 11th. One round in passing across the community of Madison produced around 1 inch in less than an hour over saturated soil conditions, with rainfall rates at times of 2 to 3 inches per hour. Multiple streets within the community were flooded and impassible.

Multiple personal weather stations observed 3 to 5 inches of rain during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding of Forbush Creek, including along Union Cross Church Road where is crosses over the Creek. This road was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded. Residents along the creek were stranded inside their homes due to the flooding, and required rescue from the Yadkinville Fire Department.

Multiple personal weather stations observed that 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across eastern Yadkin County during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of it during a 90-minute period for some of these stations. This resulted in flash flooding along Mill Branch. Bloomtown Road crossing the Mill Branch was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

Multiple personal weather stations observed that 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across the upper Logan Creek basin during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of it during a 90-minute period. This resulted in flash flooding along Logan Creek. The Cornelius Road bridge crossing the creek was completely flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.

Spotters reported flash flooding of a couple of streams in southern Cleveland County after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell, with much of that falling in about a three hour period during the morning of the 12th. Logan Branch inundated a portion of Sulphur Springs Rd and Buffalo Creek overflowed onto Cleveland Ave.

City of Columbia Police reported the intersection of Whaley Street and Main Street flooded. Areas along Rocky Branch were flooded from the intersection of Blossom Street and Pickens Street. This also includes areas along Maxcy Gregg Park. The USGS stream gage at the intersection of Whaley Street and Main Street crested at 8.6 feet. Flood stage is 7.2 feet.

After 2 to 2.5 inches of rain fell during the morning across much of Buckingham County, a band of slow-moving thunderstorms moved across the county during the evening. Runoff from this heavy rain caused water to flow across the road near the intersection of Howardsville Road and Watoga Road.

After 2 to 2.5 inches of rain fell during the morning across much of Buckingham County, a band of slow-moving thunderstorms moved across the county during the evening. Runoff from this heavy rain caused water to flow across the road near the intersection of Twin Creek Road and West James Anderson Highway.

With 1.5 to 2 inches of rain having already fallen earlier in the day, a band of fast-moving thunderstorms producing heavy rain moved across the community of Blacksburg. Between 7:00 pm and 7:40 pm, a weather station in Blacksburg recorded about 1.25 inches of rain with this band. Runoff from the rainfall push Stroubles Creek out of its banks near the Duck Pond on the Virginia Tech University campus, flooding Duck Pond Drive. The road was impassible for several hours.

With about 2 inches of rain having already fallen earlier in the day across the Jacobs Creek watershed, a band of thunderstorms passed across the area during the evening. Multiple personal weather stations observed 1.25 to 1.5 inches of rain during a 45-minute period between 6:30 pm and 7:15 pm, falling over saturated soils. Runoff from this rain pushed Jacobs Creek out of its banks, which was then observed flowing across Red House Road. The road was impassible until the flood waters receded. An automobile became stranded in the floodwaters and had to be towed out.

Multiple reports of significant flooding received from the broadcast media, trained spotters, law enforcement, and NWS employees were received over the course of a day. Reports of significant street flooding and major, damaging rainfall in many neighborhoods in the following cities: Miramar, Pembroke Pines, Southwest Ranches, Weston, Davie, Fort Lauderdale, and Lauderhill. Standing water remained for several days, blocking off some neighborhoods. Water entered above grade structures in Fort Lauderdale and Lauderhill, as well as many near or at grade structures in Davie. At least minor flooding was noted across the remainder of the county. Rainfall amounts of 8 to almost 21 inches were measured across most of Broward County, with almost 21 inches in Pembroke Pines, and 12 to 18 inches in southwest Broward metro communities from Weston to Miramar.

Two to three inches of rain fell during the early morning hours of November 12th, about half of these amounts during a 90-minute period with the main convective band. This resulted in flash flooding along the Mitchell River, flooding over-passing bridges at several locations. Among other roads, Zephyr Mountain Park Road became flooded and impassible where it crosses over the river.

The Emergency Manager reported water flowing over White Road and other nearby roadways due to rising water from neighboring creeks. Several fields and pastures were also inundated. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding near the intersection of Edwards Street and Coombs Avenue. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred in the area, producing the flash flooding.

Several reports of flash flooding in Biscayne Park and North Miami were received. Roads were impassable in Biscayne Park with water entering crawlspaces and homes. Streets were also impassable at the intersection of Biscayne Boulevard and Sans Souci Boulevard in North Miami. Rain gauges in the area measured 3-4 inches of rain, most of it over the course of a couple of hours.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding along Ivey Drive, resulting in its closure. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred in the area, producing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding on Cut Thru Road due to high water conditions in Little Rocky Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, producing excessive runoff and resulting in the flash flooding.
More than a foot of water was rushing down Wagner Avenue. Evacuations were being initiated.
Major flash flooding of Nanticoke Creek was occurring. Families were being evacuated from 12 trailer homes near NY-26.
Flash flooding occurred along the Choconut Creek with flood waters passing through nearby neighborhoods and a mobile home park on Route 26.

A stream gauge on Mud Creek in Hendersonville indicated flash flooding occurred after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell across the area in around 24 hours. Several low lying spots along the creek were inundated. Additionally, Wash Creek flooded a parking lot and access road at the intersection of S Church St and S Main St.
Water rapidly rising in the area with one home flooded to the first floor.
Water was flooding the fairgrounds and roads along State Route 14.
Water was flowing across U.S. Route 6.
Water was flowing across North Rome Road.
Water was flowing over roads in the area.
Flash flooding of Wysox Creek was underway. One home in the area was flooded out.
Depot Street flooded and closed at this time.
Flash flooding was entering a house on State Route 23.
Multiple roads were flooded throughout the village. The East Branch Delaware was flooded and rising rapidly.
Several roads were closed due to high, flowing water.
Major flash flooding was occurring along North Rome Road. Homes were evacuated in the area.
Serious flash flooding occurred across State Route 187. The road was impassable due to floodwater damages.
Small streams and creeks were flooding the borough of Dallas.
Widespread flooding of creeks and streams throughout Endicott and Vestal, particularly along Vestal Road and Prentice Road.
Mountain Road flooded with considerable runoff ongoing. Water rushing over road and getting deeper.
Flooding was occurring along Caldwell Hill Road near Baldwin Street.
Numerous roads were flooded with rocks and debris also on the roadways.
Numerous roads flooded in the area with rocks and debris in many areas.
Local media reported significant street flooding in New Iberia. Some roadways were briefly closed with water half way up vehicles.

A stream gauge on the Catawba River at Lookout Shoals Dam indicated major flash flooding developed just upstream of the dam after 5 to 8 inches of rain fell throughout the Catawba basin, with the bulk of that falling in only a 3-hour period between midnight and sunrise on the 12th. Numerous homes were inundated and damaged, with numerous residents evacuated along the western shores of Lookout Shoals Lake. This was the second major flood event along this portion of the Catawba in less than two years (June 2019), and the second highest crest on record at Lookout Shoals (August 1940).
Several roads were flooded in and around Faison. Numerous fields around town were submerged. Nearby Highways 403 and 50 were flooded.
Water was reported to have been covering the roads in numerous locations around the county. The intersection of Carey and Hillandale Rd was closed due to high water.

A number of trees were reported down in roadways on Bald Rock Road. Significant amounts of ash and sediment were reported in roadway ditches that also overtopped the roadway in multiple locations. Timing is based on radar estimate. Location is also estimated. Damage is also estimated for debris and sediment removal, as we are unaware of any crop damage.
Water-covered roads were reported around the county. Some locations that were flooded were Old New Bern Rd, 10-Mile Ford Rd, and Greentown Rd. The time was estimated based on radar data.
Various roads were flooded in and around Greenville. Rural two lane roads across the county were also flooded, as well as one water covered bridge.

Heavy rain with measured amounts of 2.82 being reported in the vicinity of Newry, ME lead to localized flash flooding at the Sunday River Ski Resort. In addition to the heavy rain, melting man made snow contributed to rapid runoff. Heavy erosion and undermining caused damage to one of the base areas at Sunday River Resort.

Stream gauges reported flash flooding developed along the major headwater streams in Transylvania County after 4 to 5 inches of rain fell across much of the southern and western part of the county in around 24 hours. The Little River overflowed its banks and flooded Merrill Rd in the eastern part of the county. The French Broad River inundated multiple roads in the Rosman area, including Depot St, where some homes has to be evacuated, as well as Hannah Ford Rd, E Main St, and Highway 178. The Davidson River also overflowed its banks in the Pisgah Forest area, flooding portions of Davidson River Rd and Wilson Rd, and indicating backwater flooding of Turkey Creek which inundated Deavor Rd.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed along portions of the Catawba River and many of its tributaries across central McDowell County after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell in around 24 hours. In addition to around two dozen roads being inundated and closed, a water rescue occurred at an apartment complex in Old Fort when Mill Creek overflowed its banks. Private bridges were destroyed by intense stream flow along Second Broad River at Mimosa Dr and Clear Creek Rd (both in the Marion area) and along Peppers Creek Rd in North Cove. A culvert under Hidden Forest Drive was also washed out by a tributary of Limekiln Creek in Woodlawn. Additionally, a stream gauge on the Catawba River exceeded its established flood stage in the Pleasant Gardens community, indicating inundation of a campground off North Main St just north of Marion.
Flash flooding closed State Route 415 between Lakeside Drive and the intersection of State Route 29.
Major flash flooding was occurring in the vicinity of Winterdale Road which prevented emergency responders from reaching nearby residences.
Flash flooding led to evacuations of residences along Bluegrass Road.
Flash flooding occurred along Choconut Creek with the stream cresting around 11.8 feet. Roads and basements were flooded in the area.

Emergency manager reported major flash flooding developed throughout Alexander County after up to 9 inches of rain fell in 24 hours, with around half of that falling in a 3-hour period prior to daybreak on the 12th. The most significant flooding occurred along the South Yadkin River in the Hiddenite area. Multiple recreational vehicles and campers were swept down the river from a campground off Princess Ln. Five people, ages ranging from 1 to 76, drowned and 31 more people required rescue from rapidly rising flood water. Otherwise, most of the creeks and streams in the central and northeast part of the county overflowed onto at least one road, with more than 50 roads closed at some point during the event.

Emergency manager and stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along tributaries of the Catawba River, including Johns River and Lower Creek after 3 to 5 inches fell across the area in around 24 hours. Johns River inundated multiple roads, including Johns River Loop and Johns River Rd. A water rescue occurred on Johns River Loop. Lower Creek also flooded Antioch Rd near Highway 18. Pax Hill Rd and Hartland Rd also flooded in the Chesterfield community.

Emergency manager and stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along the Johns River and Yadkin River basins after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across much of Caldwell County in about 24 hours. Johns River flooded multiple roads in the Collettsville area, including Highway 90 and Valley View Circle. Water from the Yadkin inundated several roads in the Happy Valley community, including Yadkin River Rd and Indian Grave Rd.
Pennsylvania State Highway 239 is closed due to flooding between Ruckle Hill Road and Pond Hill Mountain Road.
A house was surrounded by water on State Route 187.
Severe flooding was occurring in several places along Laurel Creek and Roods Creek Road in the towns of Deposit and Tompkins. Road closures taking place.
Water flowing across NY Route 30 and Perch Lake Road. Floodwaters were pouring off the hills above the Pepacton Reservoir.
Multiple reports received of water flooding all along the Trout Creek area.
Several roadways were reported to be underwater across the Panama City area due to 2 to 3 inches of rain falling in 1 hour.

Heavy rain from Tropical Storm Zeta caused Whittier Creek to overflow its banks and completely wash out Nurse Road, making the road impassible. Water was estimated to be flowing about two feet over the bridge before it was destroyed.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations indicate that more than half of the rain fell within a 2-hour period as the center of the storm passed. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Ararat community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded. A few bridges were damaged or destroyed.

Two swift-water rescues were performed for the occupants of vehicles that became stranded where Hiatt Road passes across Stoney Creek. The road was flooded and impassible for several hours. This flooding was the result of heavy rain which occurred during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Dobson community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded. A few bridges were damaged or destroyed. Highway 601 was impassible due to flooding of Bear Creek, where one swift water rescue was performed for an automobile that became stranded in the flood waters. Fisher River Park was also closed due to flooding.

Several roads were observed flooded and closed in and around the community of Jonesville. Among them, over six inches of water from the nearby Yadkin River was observed flowing rapidly over Fabric Lane.

Training thunderstorms formed along a boundary left in the wake of Tropical Storm Zeta, producing 2.5-4 inches of rain in a three to four hour period. Rainfall rates were observed to be one to two inches per hour. The Campbell County 911 Center reported that at least seven roads within the central part of the county were flooded and impassable. This included Yellow Branch rising out of its banks near the intersection of Morman Mill Road and Patterson Road.

Persistent heavy rainfall from Hurricane Delta caused flash flooding in portions of Catahoula Parish especially in a corridor from near Jonesville to near Sicily Island. Fifteen homes in Jonesville took on floodwaters, and several roadways were either flooded over or washed out between Harrisonburg and Sicily Island.

A tributary of Daniels Creek overflowed its banks and flooded onto Oakland Drive, making it impassible until the water receded. The flooding was the result of up to two inches of rain inside a two hour window, with one to 1.5 inch per hour rainfall rates per nearby personal weather station observations.

Bassett Branch overflowed its banks and flooded onto Meadowood Trail, making it impassible until the water receded. The flooding was the result of up to two inches of rain inside a two hour window, with one to 1.5 inch per hour rainfall rates per nearby personal weather station observations.

Multiple weather stations in the southeastern portion of Franklin County recorded between two to locally 3.5 inches of rainfall inside a three hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour were observed in some locations. This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways in the Snow Creek area, making them impassible until the water receded. This includes Muddy Fork Road flooded by Reed Creek and Sutton Hollow Road closed due to flooding of Crawford Creek and Snow Creek. Fawndale Road and portions of the Virgil Goode Highway were also reported flooded and impassible for a few hours.

Multiple privately-owned weather stations indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain fell during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Soils were already very moist due to rounds of rain that passed across the region earlier in the night. Runoff from the rain caused Cranberry Creek to overflow its banks across a bridge on Double Springs Church Road, making the bridge impassible for several hours.
North Olmsted Police conducted a water rescue along the Rocky River at Cedar Point Road and Valley Parkway in North Olmsted as fast moving hood-deep water surrounded the motorist.

Privately-owned weather stations across northern Ashe County indicate that 1.5 to slightly over 2 inches of rain fell across soils already very moist from rainfall earlier in the past 24 hours. This caused flooding of Helton Creek, overflowing across a bridge along Jim Duvall Road.

Significant flooding occurred in the Sea Pines neighborhood of Lantana resulting from a combination of heavy rainfall of the previous days plus 4-5 inches of rain on the night and early morning of October 24th and 25th. Numerous calls were received from residents stranded in their homes, some who had water in their homes up to their knees. Streets were impassable across the entire neighborhood. Extensive flooding took place along Cub Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as two to three inches of rain fell across the basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a one hour period, on top of an additional one to two inches that fell during the previous evening for a total of nearly five inches in 24 hours. Virtually all of Cub Creek Park was flooded, and the bridge on South Bridge Street that crosses the creek was completely over-topped by the flooded creek. Elsewhere, the dam of a 3.5 acre pond collapsed at around 1:40 pm EST, sending flood water that washed out at 20 foot section of Woodfield Way just downstream. Concern for the bridge on Industrial Park Road that crosses the creek about one mile downstream prompted evacuations of multiple businesses and apartments that would be cut off if the that bridge too was washed out, though it did not. Country Club Extension Road along Little Cub Creek was flooded and closed, as was Westover Road, where storage buildings and nearby residences were also flooded.

Extensive flooding took place along Moravian Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period. This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours. Newspaper reports indicate that nearly all of Moravian Creek was out of its banks, causing flooding Wilkes Community College's lower campus. School Street further downstream was also closed by the flood waters.
Around two inches of rain during a 2-hour period caused flooding of Powder Mill Creek onto both School Board Road, while flooding of Doe run closed both Doe Run Road and Ashpone Road.

Numerous businesses along Wilkesboro Boulevard from the Yadkin River bridge to Memorial Park were flooded when the Yadkin River swiftly rose out of its banks, the result of 4 to 5 inches or rain within a 24-hour period both preceding and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations observed 2-3 inches of rain within a 1-hour period just before the onset of flooding. Flash flooding ended as the river crested during mid-afternoon, and roads were reopened during the evening once the river receded. Among the businesses flooded were Extreme Collision Auto Body, which had to move several vehicles to prevent them from being damaged by flood waters. Flood waters completely inundated Memorial Park as well as the Yadkin River Greenway.

The Reddies River at Wilkesboro (REDN7) crested at 11.79 feet (6760 cfs), which was between a 5- and 10-year Annual Return Interval per USGS StreamStats. These rises were the result of 3-5 inches of rainfall within a 24-hour period, much of which fell within a 2-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The rapid rises resulted in the precautionary evacuation of residents from the Rose Glen Manor assisted living facility, though flooding did not enter the buildings. Employees of other nearby businesses were evacuated as well out of precaution.
Water was reported over Hwy. 123 west of Western Grove.

Widespread flooding took place along Fishing Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period. This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours. Newspaper reports indicate that Fishing Creek Arbor Road at Fishing Creek was washed out when the culvert running beneath the road failed. Further downstream, flood waters from the creek carried away several dozen propane gas storage tanks. It is unclear how many tanks were recovered and still functioning. In addition, high water rescues were conducted for cars that became stranded in the flood waters. One rescue was conducted on Highway 115 near the intersection with Speedway Road, and the other was on Speedway Road near the Fishing Creek Road intersection.

Moravian Creek quickly rose out of its banks during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, the result of three to five inches of rain within a 24-hour period. This caused several roads intersecting the creek to be flooded and closed until the flood water receded, including Germantown Road and Falls Road near the Moravian Falls waterfall.

Heavy rain across central and western Wilkes County due to the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta caused rapid river rises along the Yadkin River. The Yadkin River quickly rose out of its banks, flooding multiple roads in the Roaring River and Ronda communities, including Red, White and Blue Road, Roaring River Road and Clingman Road.

Multiple weather stations in the vicinity of the Blue Ridge in Carroll County indicate that between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain fell inside a two-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta at rates of one to two inches per hour in spots. This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways, making them impassible until the water receded, including across Spring Bud Road and Route 52 as Paul's Creek rose out of its banks.

Training bands of heavy showers redeveloped across coastal areas of Martin County during the morning of October 2 and persisted into the early afternoon. Rain totals of 5 to 8 inches fell across the same area impacted by 6 to 10 inches only a day earlier. Many of the same areas which experienced flash flooding were again inundated with rapidly rising water, exceeding 3 feet in some areas. High water resulted in the closing of dozens of roadways. Flood waters approached many homes and intruded into several homes resulting in damage. Drainage canals and creeks overflowed and high water from the Savannas Preserve flowed into surrounding areas. The flood waters were very slow to recede.

Multiple data sources across all of Patrick County, including trained spotters and personal automated weather stations, indicate that between two and locally three inches of rain fell during a two-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta from roughly 9 am to 11 am EDT. Rainfall rates were observed at one to two inches per hour in spots. This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways, some up to 12 inches deep in the vicinity of Buffalo Creek, making them impassible until the water receded. This included Egg Farm Road where it intersected Grassy Branch Creek, as water was estimated to be at least eight inches deep over the roadway.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Elkin community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded, including Commerce Street, Pleasant Hill Road, and Memorial Park Drive. A stream gauge on the French Broad River near Marshall indicated flash flooding developed along the river in the town of Marshall after widespread heavy rainfall occurred throughout the basin over 24 hours, with a good bit of that falling in just a few hours during the afternoon of the 17th. Although the rivers rapid rise leveled off during the late evening as heavy rainfall came to an end, runoff working its way downstream through the basin resulted in moderate flooding persisting along the river until around sunrise on the 18th, while the river didnt return to its banks until late morning. This was the worst flooding that developed along this portion of the French Broad River since Hurricane Ivan in September 2004.

The Hackensack River at River Vale exceeded its minor flood stage of 5.5 feet at 11:30pm EDT. The river then continued to rise quickly, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.5 feet) by 12:15am EDT September 2nd and major flood stage (8.0 feet) by 12:30am EDT. The river then crested at a height of 11.05 feet at 4:00am EDT September 2nd. After falling through much of the morning, the river experienced a secondary crest of 10.73 feet at 3:45pm EDT September 2nd. The river did not fall back below flood stage until 11:45am EDT on September 3rd.||The crest of 11.05 feet is the third highest on record at this location behind crests of 12.26 feet in August 2011 and 12.19 feet in April 2007.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain resulted in major flash flooding across southern Roswell and southern Chaves County. Heavy rainfall had fallen in the area the previous evening, and an additional 3 to 5 inches of rain during the morning of May 31st exacerbated the flash flooding. Numerous locations along U.S. Highway 285 from Lake Arthur northward into Roswell had upwards of 2 feet of water along the travel corridor while low water crossings had upwards of 4 feet of water which overfilled the banks. Multiple reports of flooding across fields, ditches, yards, and vehicles were reported. Several side roads were unpassable and had to be barricaded. A breached arroyo near the Roswell Airport also forced the closure of roads around the airport for about a week. Damages are estimated.

Several people were stranded along the highway and were waiting on top of their vehicles to be rescued. Several water rescues had to be conducted at U.S. Highway 285 and Orchard Park Road. The East Verde River near Childs (Gauge EVDA3) rose from 10 to 12.4 feet in less than 30 minutes at 930 AM on September 1. It dropped below 12 feet about 3 hours later. At 830 PM, it rose to 13.8 feet. The water dropped back to around 11.6 feet by 900 AM on September 2.

Heavy rain over the Little Colorado River Basin and tributaries created a surge of water at the river gauge (LCCA3) on the Little Colorado River near Cameron. The water rose from 1.8 feet to 5.43 feet on the gauge in less than 15 minutes at 1245 AM on 2 September. The water was still above 4.7 feet at 945 AM.

The stream gauge on Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City rose from 17.6 feet to 20.8 feet in less than half an hour at 430 PM on 1 September. The gauge went down to 18.4 feet then rose again to 23.7 feet in less than half an hour at 900 PM on 1 September. The water rose a third time to 22 feet in less than half a hour at 3:00 AM on 2 September. The water receded below 18 feet by 800 AM on 2 September.

An upper level low pressure system parked off the coast of northern Baja California spread considerable deeper moisture north and into Imperial County on January 20th. The deep moisture combined with modest instability to produce widespread showers, some of which were moderate. Embedded isolated thunderstorms resulted in locally heavy rain that caused an episode of flash flooding in eastern Imperial County just north of Interstate 8 during the morning hours. At 0953PST local law enforcement reported flash flooding along Ogilby Road north of Interstate 8 and roughly 4 miles northwest of the town of Felicity. The flash flooding resulted in debris flowing across the highway as well as the closure of Ogilby Road. There were no reports of accidents due to the flash flooding. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect at the time of the flash flooding.

Flash flooding of Champion Creek prompted the closure of Highway 994.

Considerable flash flooding occurred in Murray and the nearby surrounding area. Numerous roads were flooded, including main thoroughfares such as U.S. Highway 641 and Highway 80. The figures for Calloway County outside Murray include: at least 91 locations with road or culvert damage and an unspecified number of flooded residences. At the peak of the flooding, water was over Highways 181 around Elkton and Guthrie, Highway 475, Highway 106, Highway 104 at Old Trenton, Highway 102 near Allensville, and at least ten county roads. Kickapoo Creek spilled out of its banks and flooded State Route 10 just west of Lincoln. A minor car accident occurred due to hydroplaning: however, no injuries were reported.
Widespread flash flooding across Shelby County with observed rainfall amounts of 4-6 inches in less than six hours. Many roads impassible.
Several streets were flooded and impassable with at least one vehicle stalled in high water.
Water was reported over the road closing it to traffic.

Heavy rainfall in the Hondo area caused widespread flooding of roads and low water crossings. The Lincoln County emergency manager estimated that the Rio Ruidoso rose 4 to 6 feet quickly while Alamo Canyon Road south of U.S. Highway 70 was completely inundated. One individual was in their truck at Alamo Canyon Road and became stuck in the low water crossing when the flood waters inundated it. The individual then either tried to escape or the flood waters pulled them out of their truck. Tragically, they drowned, and their body was found the next day. Damages are estimated for the loss of the truck.
Flat Mary Road in the community of Mary and Cave Branch Road near the community of Bethany were said to be impassable due to flooding.
Portions of Highway 45 were flooded north of Bonanza.
Flood water caused minor damage to twenty homes in Ozark, and damaged portions of several roads in southwestern Franklin County.
Portions of several roads in and around Vian were flooded.
Portions of W Redwood Avenue were flooded.
Portions of several county roads were flooded and closed. Flood water eroded portions of these roads, as well as a new tin horn.
Portions of a county road and a large tin horn were eroded by flood waters.
Heavy rainfall of 4-6 inches resulted in numerous roads flooded across the county, several of which were closed.
Gwinn Road was flooded and closed.
Water covered Highway 67 and Front Street in Donaldson.
Water was flowing across the eastbound lanes of I-72 southeast of Berlin.
Several roads in both Danville and Tilton were flooded.
Illinois Route 17 was closed between Lacon and Sparland due to water flowing across the road.
A culvert was washed out on Illinois Route 29 near Sparland, which swept a vehicle off the road. No injuries were reported.
Approximately 6 inches to one foot of flowing water was reported across Route 2 on the north side of Hebron.
Flash flooding on Columbus Street in Albertville. At least 6 inches of water over the roadway. Report relayed via social media.
Intersection of Highway 75 and Highway 35 in Rainsville has between 1 and 1.5 feet of water covering the roadway.
Multiple roads closed due to high water, including 2400 Rd to 2800 Rd.
Several city streets were reported flooded with at lease one vehicle stalled in high water.
State Highway 37 at Clear Creek was closed due to flooding.
Route Y at Hollis Branch was closed due to flooding.

The main street in Paradise is impassable with water over the roads. They have begun to evacuate the community. There was a water rescue for a family of 4 just west of Paradise. Many other county roads in the vicinity were also covered with water and impasable.
Numerous roads are covered with water making travel across the county extremely difficult.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Colorado City. There were multiple low water crossing rescues that occurred around Colorado City. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Snyder. There were reports of flooded streets in downtown Snyder. Some streets were blocked or impassable. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

The public reported water over the roadway at the intersection of Corinth Road and Millard Farmer Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain accumulated quickly, causing the flash flooding.
Several roadways flooded. Several cars stalled in waters. Intersection of Rossville Blvd and Central Avenue was closed.
Several flooded roadways in downtown Chattanooga.
Twitter report showed flash flooding on Bill Evans Road south of Gila, NM.
Fire official reported some sink holes and a couple of cars swept away in La Union. Radar estimated about 1 inch of rain in less than an hour.
Portions of 6 city streets were under water, with around 3 feet of water over the roads at one point.
About a foot of water over roadways in Kingfisher.
Car stranded in one to two feet of water near center of town.
A water rescue was performed successfully on Clear Creek. No injuries were reported.
High water was reported over several roads with flooding occurring along Turkey Creek. Between 3 and 4 inches of rain were recorded during the day.
State Highway 76 at Buffalo Creek was closed due to flooding. Water was reported to have risen very rapidly.

Pictures posted on social media showed water from Long Branch flowing across Prestonsburg Street in West Liberty, making it impassable. It had also surrounding a neighboring home. This was confirmed by the 911 dispatch as well.
Fire officials reported stranded vehicles and flooded roads along I-27 and HWY 217. Several other reports came in from the public of stranded vehicles as well.
Several inches of mud, rocks, and debris flowed over Baker Creek Road that closed the road. This was a burn scar area and the first of two road closing slide events.

The Emergency Manager reported Benson Lake Road closed at Mt. Moriah Road due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Puckett Road at Pumpkinvine Creek is flooded. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the quick rise of the creek.

The Emergency Manager reported Sleepy Hollow Road at Brownsville Road was closed due to water over the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a road washed out near Line Creek Road and Blanton Mill Road due to high water on the Flint River and Flat Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
Over 5 inches of rainfall was observed.
Major flooding occurred in Dermott with two feet of water covering highways.
A portion of Causeyville Road was under water.
Water was over Highway 37 in northern Covington County.
Water was across some of the roads in Stringer.
Multiple neighborhoods in town were reported to be surrounded by water making travel extremely difficult.
Several roadways were flooded in the Kingsport vicinity.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Odessa. There were reports of flash flooding across portions of Odessa on social media. There were pictures of water up to the top steps of home porches on Hancock Avenue. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Northbound lanes on highway 177 underwater.
Water nearly into houses, flooded yards and streets.
Stalled vehicles in deep water.
Two cars stalled out and road closed at 33rd and Kelly.
State Highway C was closed at Indian Creek due to flooding.
State Highway AA at a tributary of Buffalo Creek was closed at a low water crossing due to flooding.
State highway 413 was closed due to flooding of a low water area.
Several washouts along Highway 37 south of Rockland including one along King Lane found in NWS storm survey.
Flooding along Trapper Creek Road with excessive runoff from Squaw Creek and Little Squaw Creek drainages. Several inches of rocks, mud and debris on the roadway.
Significant flash flooding occurred across a gravel road, and water was overtopping a small bridge along a paved road in the area of S 2950 E and Heglar Canyon Road west northwest of Heglar.
Heavy rain caused the intersection to flooded at Hillcrest and Grelot Roads.
The Emergency Manager reported water from Mud Creek was covering Honeysuckle Lane. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water from Lick Log Creek covering Garmon Road and Hunters Mill Drive. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water from Mud Creek covering the roadway near the intersection of Mudd Creek Road and McGarity Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Winn Road was impassable between Bobby Austin Road and South Paulding High School due to high water from a Sweetwater Creek tributary. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
Heavy rainfall resulted in street flooding throughout the city of Cleveland.
Flash flooding occurred around Taylorsville. Approximately a foot of water was across the roadway at the intersection of Pine and Front Streets. Part of County Road 21 was also underwater.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in northern Austin. A video on Twitter showed up to six inches of water on roadways at the intersection of Shoal Creek Blvd. and Hancock Blvd. along Shoal Creek.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing several roads in and around Kenedy.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Odessa. There were pictures of flooding across the intersection of 8th Street and Muskingum Avenue. The water was high enough to move a dumpster into the middle of the intersection. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Odessa. There was a video of a car floating down Tom Green Avenue with water several feet deep across the residential area. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Odessa. There were pictures of water up to the side of cars and trucks along Walnut Street. A few vehicles were submerged up to the hood. The water was at least two to three feet deep. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Stalled cars in the roadway.
Multiple cars stalled out.
Street flooding reported across town.
Flooding reported in several spots around the city.
State highway V at a tributary of the James River was closed due to flooding.
State highway CC at Spring Creek was closed due to flooding.
State Highway A at Spring Creek in Hurley was closed due to flooding.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey found evidence of high water along several stretches of Arbon Valley Road. Road and Bridge crews called out to clear off extensive debris caused by the flash flooding on the roadway.
A NWS storm survey found flooding had occurred on Highway 36 with damage to culverts. Idaho Transportation Department was cleaning up debris.

The US Forest Service reported Trapper Creek Road washed out in the area of FS Road 538 to Trout Creek Pass. A 12 foot deep gully was running down the center of the road. This was due to excessive runoff from the burned canyon walls from the Badger Fire burn scar.
Street flooding reported on South Coulter near Hollywood Road construction zones.
There were reports of water over roadways.
Parts of Knob Lick Road were under water. The time was estimated by the dispatcher.

Flooding occurred east of the Interstate exchange.
