Several roads were reported flooded near Randleman, including Fox Street and Poplar Street.
Flash flooding was reported in the 4900 block of Edgar Road.
Flash flooding was reported near South Cutchin Street, where several homes were evacuated due to rising water from the heavy rain.

Airport Road and Highway 35 near the Interstate 59 interchange flooded with water rising rapidly. Water reported to be to the steps of tractor trailers at this time. Airport Road closed. One fatality occurred here when a womans car was swept off the roadway due to flooding from Dye Branch which feeds into Big Wills Creek.
KY-11 near the Three Forks Historical Center is experiencing ongoing flooding.
East Main Street is flooding.
The Clay County dispatch reported a brief road closure, between 5 and 6pm, on KY-472 along Bray Creek due to water flowing over the road.

Numerous streets are flooded and impassable in Lincoln. The fire department also had to barricade roads to keep people from driving into the flooded areas. A resident also reported flooding to their basement.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Odessa. As many as 27 swift water rescues were made across Odessa due to prolific flooding across the area. There were several pictures that showed abandoned cars engulfed in the flood waters. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding near Colorado City. There were pictures and video from a spotter of flash flooding ongoing along the Colorado River north northwest of Colorado City. The water was several feet deep and flowing quickly. The water was well over the banks. No damage was reported.
At least 3 cars stalled at Lindsey/Elm street intersection. Water up to 2 feet.
Main and Peters streets flooded with manhole covers dislodged.
State Highway 95 at Bryant Creek was closed due to flooding.
Streams out of their banks and flooding yards around Mount Carmel. A vehicle was reported to be stranded.
There was a rapid rise in water over East Harris Road.
The fire department advised that water was in a home on the 5000 block of Gotts Hydro Road. The cost of property damage is unknown.
Water was over the Cumberland Parkway eastbound at exit 14.
Social media report received of a truck trapped in high water in the Harlingen area. Water depth was estimated to be around 3 feet.
Social media report received of several flooded streets with 2 to 3 feet of water depth near Miller Jordan Middle School in San Benito.
Several high water rescues were reported due to cars stranded in high waters.
Water ran over Pine Street and Heidel Road.
Water covered roads in Columbia.
Water flowed across streets in Oak Grove.
Water was over roads in Magee.

Widespread flash flooding across much of Bowie County and the Texas side of Texarkana resulted in the closure of numerous roads. A few water rescues were also needed from stranded vehicles. Water entered several structures throughout the county as well.
Water rescues had to be performed in the northeast part of the county. Ohio street north of interstate 70 was impassable. Also, multiple homes had four or more feet of water in the basements.
Stinking Creek was out of its banks and flooding roadways.
A slow moving thunderstorm produced 10 to 16 inches of rain over the Hampshire - Fannett area which flooded numerous homes, businesses, vehicles, and streets.
Numerous roads flooded and closed around and between Jasper and Browndell including state highways. Several homes were also flooded in Jasper.
Numerous streets were flooded around Lafayette with cars stranded at several intersections.
Feeder roads and the FM 1093 exit along State Highway 99 were closed due to flooding.
Numerous impassable roads due to flooding.
Williams Silvers Parkway, the east bound lanes of Canal Road, and Jubilee Point Road were all flooded in the Orange Beach area.
County Road 95 between County Road 20 and Fitzpatrick Lane was flooded.

Public report received of flood waters reaching up over the top of car wheel wells in the Weslaco area. Emergency managers also reported water depth of up to 3 feet in spots during this event, mostly in the area just south of Interstate Highway 2 between Westgate and Airport Boulevard.

Local emergency management coordinator and on-site law enforcement/fire and rescue reported water entering properties on the east side of Los Fresnos in poorly draining locations where 3 inches fell in a 2 to 3 hour period.

Several roads were flooded and impassable in southwest Rutherford County, including areas around Rockvale where water rescues were conducted from vehicles, Armstrong Valley near Yeargan Road, and Barfield Road along the Stones River.
Several roads were flooded and closed across Hickman County including Brushy Road near Arnold Road and Highway 100 West.

Flash flooding affected far northern Cannon County, with several roads flooded and closed and water rescues conducted. Roads that were flooded included Gassaway Road, Ashford Hollow Road, and Marshall Creek Road. A water rescue was conducted for a person stranded in a flooded vehicle in the 700 block of Asford Hollow Road, and two other water rescues were performed from vehicles trapped in the 700 block of Marshall Creek Road.
Posts from social media indicated numerous streets in and west of Iota flooded and impassable after several inches of rain.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Midland County. There were several roads under water across western Midland County, including Farm to Market Road 1788. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
An underpass was flooded along Interstate 69 South near East Mount Houston Rd, resulting in at least one stalled vehicle.
Photos on social media showed flooding over Bethlehem Church Road.
Portions of Highway 64 near White Oak Creek, west of Ozark, were flooded.
Edgemont creek was flowing over Pleasant Valley Road.
Holmes Run was out of its banks and flowing onto nearby trails and roads.
Law enforcement reports high water rescues ongoing in Abilene. Also, a flooded home was reported at the 1200 block of Westmoreland St.
A few roads were flooded across Sparta including Skyline Drive and Hickory Valley Road. Southeast of Sparta, two to three feet of water covered Lost Creek Road.
Several roads were flooded across Cookeville.
Numerous roads were flooded and closed across the county, including I-40 at mile marker 178, South Bear Creek, Hogan Road at Porter Road, Double Branch Road, and Highway 48 N at R Owen Road.
Several roads were flooded in Jamestown and across Fentress County.

Numerous roads were flooded across Clay County, including Wet Mill Creek Road, Pitcock Lane, Kyle Street at West Lake Avenue, Williamson Street, Poor House Road, Free Hill River Road, Arcott Road, Turkey Creek Road, New Hope Road, Finus Cherry Road, Trace Creek Road, Leonard Road, Luther Pedigo Road, and Mack Bean Road.
Several roads were flooded across southern Cheatham County, including West Kingston Springs Road, and Highway 70 at Pinnacle Hill Road.
Numerous roads were flooded and closed across Mount Juliet, including Belinda Parkway which was flooded and impassable.

Major flash flooding affected Mount Juliet, with most roadways flooded and closed, numerous water rescues conducted from vehicles and homes, and many homes and businesses flooded. Homes were flooded on Creedwood Drive and West Division Street with people rescued. The Valley Center Mall shopping center on Mount Juliet Road at Old Lebanon Dirt Road was also flooded.
A bridge over Cedar Creek on Woodridge Place near Clemmons Road was damaged by flood waters and closed.

Training thunderstorms over several hours across central Bailey County caused flash flooding mostly along Farm to Market Road 746 west of Texas Highway 214. The next morning water was still over Farm to Market Road 746.
A female was rescued after her car became stuck in high water near the Verizon Building at 590 Union Avenue.
Flooding occurred at the intersection of Shady Lane and Delafield Road in Fox Chapel.
Search and rescue was deployed in Beatyville to get people to safety due to ongoing flooding.
Dispatch reported that a road east of Booneville was impassable due to water flowing over it.

Thunderstorms moved very slowly across Lake Charles and the surrounding area while back building during the late morning to mid afternoon of the 17th. One rain gage recorded near 22 inches of rain in South Lake Charles during the event, but a large swath received 10 inches or more. Most streets were flooded and impassable. Numerous vehicles were flooded and some were swept off the roads into ditches and and bayous. One person drown when their car floated into a ditch. Numerous homes and businesses were flooded in South Lake Charles some of which were still being repaired from Hurricanes Laura and Delta. Some schools and churches in the area also flooded.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Cars were stranded in flood waters from Olmos Creek in northern San Antonio.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. The San Antonio Fire Department performed a water rescue at Old O'Connor Rd. and Lookout Rd. in northeastern San Antonio.
Vehicles were flooded in Sweeny due to heavy rain.
Images on social media showed high water from East Fork Creek over the County House Road Bridge.
The Cedar Flat Curtis Bridge flooded.
Kentucky 90, Summer Shade Road, one mile west of the Cumberland/Metcalf County Line was closed due to flooding.
Kentucky 90 was closed due to flooding around Marrowbone.
Numerous roads in and around McAlester were flooded, and several vehicles were stranded in high water.
There was a swift water rescue near the 8900 Block of Jones Road in Libertytown.
MD-75 at Coppermine Road was closed due to high water.
High water was blocking several lanes of the George Washington Parkway between Slaters Lane and Bashford Lane.
MD 194 at Cash Smith Road was closed due to high water.
A swift water rescue took place in the 9900 Block of Daysville Road at Cabbage Run.

Major flash flooding affected northern Williamson County, with many roadways flooded and closed, many homes and businesses flooded, and numerous water rescues conducted from vehicles and homes. Roads were flooded and closed and homes were flooded around Harpeth River Drive and Granny White Pike at Belle Rive Drive in Brentwood, the Fieldstone Farms and the Meadowgreen Acres subdivisions on Hillsboro Road in Franklin. A river gauge on the Little Harpeth River at Granny White Pike crested at 16.20 feet at 135 am CDT.
Several roads were flooded and closed across the county, including Ash Lane near the Jackson County 911/EMA office in Gainesboro.
A portion of Doc Webb Road was flooded.
Broadcast media reported cars stranded at Saddle Creek and Leavenworth. Water dpeth up to the top of the tires.
In the town of Pennsboro, more than a foot of water covered the roadway along the southbound portion of Route 74.
In the town of Toll Gate, numerous homes, campers, and vehicles were submerged underwater.
A horse trailer was swept into the water along Dotson Run in Greenwood, becoming banked up against a bridge.
Water was reported as being over the road on KY-52 between mile markers 2 and 3 in western Lee County.
Multiple areas of flash flooding reported.
Cars were under about three feet of water at Russellville and Interstate 165. Cost of damage unknown.
Approximately three feet of water was over the road near the intersection of Three Springs Road and Smallhouse Road.
Happy Valley Road had two feet of water over it.
Several roads in the county were flooded.
Social media report received of streets flooded in the San Cristobal Subdivision in Edinburg. Water depth was estimated to be 2 to 3 feet in some spots.
Several reports of roads flooded and closed across Williamson County including Spring Hill.
Several streets were flooded in Starkville.
Flash flooding was reported on Pointers Road.

Major and historic flash flooding affected southern and eastern Davidson County, with the worst flooding affecting areas along and near Sevenmile Creek and Mill Creek in south Nashville. Hundreds of homes and businesses were flooded, numerous roadways were flooded and closed including I-24, I-40, and I-440, and over 130 water rescues were conducted from people stranded in flooded vehicles and homes. Homes and businesses that were flooded included a hotel at 95 Wallace Road near I-24 at Harding Place, the South Brooke Apartments on Linbar Drive, many homes around Edmondson Pike at Blackman Road, the Walmart on Nolensville Pike at Harding Place with vehicles in the parking lot submerged up to their windows, a home on Truxton Court in Donelson, and the Kroger on Old Hickory Blvd in Hermitage which also had cars stalled in flood waters in the parking lot. Residents were trapped and rescued from the second stories of homes on Paragon Mills Road, and the attics of homes on Currey Road and also on Suter Drive near Edmondson Pike. Other people were rescued clinging to trees or in flood waters in the 400 block of Hogan Road, on Milner Drive, and in the 400 block of Harding Place. Interstate 24 near Antioch Pike was submerged with many vehicles stranded and around one dozen drivers rescued, and Interstate 40 and Interstate 440 were also flooded in a few areas. Other roads that were flooded and impassable included Rosa Parks Blvd near the Farmers Market, Highway 70 near White Bridge Road, Dodson Chapel Road, Tulip Grove Road, and Chandler Road. A total of 5 people were killed, 3 of which were swept away from a homeless camp along Sevenmile Creek near Edmondson Pike at Nolensville Pike. Another man drowned when he left his submerged vehicle and was swept away near the Nashboro Village Golf Course at Nashboro Blvd at Flintlock Court, and another man drowned in his vehicle behind the Walmart near Harding Place at Nolensville Pike.
Flash flooding washed away portions of Old Mill Creek Road near Nunnelly and destroyed two bridges on Old Hadley School Road near Bon Aqua.
A few roads in Spring Hill were closed due to high water, including Tom Lunn Road at Port Royal Road and Rice Road at Derryberry Lane.
Several roads were flooded across the county.
Flash flooding occurred along Highway 14.
Water covered Ira Hudson Road.

Two occupied vehicles were swept away by floodwaters. One vehicle was swept away on Bowman Collins Road and the other on Mandy Road. They required swift-water rescues. These roads suffered culvert washouts. There were multiple road closures across the county due to flooding including Chester Street which was flooded with 2 to 3 feet of water near the uptown area of Jackson. Culverts were also washed out on White Fern Road and Meadon Malesus Road.
The basement of a home at 2 Moffatt Lane in Chester was reported flooded. Radar estimated rainfall amounts in the area were greater than 3 inches over the previous hour.
Roads impassable and underwater with multiple roads closed due to flooding around the town of Harrison, including Frank E. Rodgers Boulevard.
Elm Road was flooded and impassable.
Glendale Road was flooded near Highway 69 just northwest of Savannah. Road was impassable.
Highway AA was closed at a low water area due to flooding.
Buffalo Creek reached moderate flood stage with waters still rising. Water was beginning to impact parts of Highway 42 around the bridge.
Excessive rainfall along the Little Lost Creek basin caused flash flooding in Seneca. Numerous roads became impassable to motorists.
Over five inches of rain was estimated to have fallen over far southeast Burleigh County. This heavy rain damaged roads and culverts.
Flash flooding occurred across the City of Anderson along Beaver and Indian Creeks. Waters rose rapidly causing the creeks to rise out of their banks and make roads impassable from high water.
The low water crossing on Highway CC at Elkhorn Creek was flooded and impassable due to flooding.
Highway 76 was closed due to flooding of a low water area.
The low water bridge on Highway U at Mikes Creek was flooded and impassable.
Several roads flooded in Houston. Some rescues occurred in Houston.
The low water crossing on Highway A was closed at South Indian Creek was flooded and impassable.
The low water crossing on Highway E at Big Sugar Creek was flooded and impassable.
Law enforcement reported that 482nd Street had water running over it and it was in the process of being closed and barricaded.

Over six inches of rain fell over parts of northeast LaMoure County, with unconfirmed reports of ten inches near Marion. This led to flooding in the city of Marion, with water flowing over roads and up to homes. County roads were also flooded, with water flowing over causing extensive damage.
Over five inches of rain fell over southeastern Grand County. Flood waters washed out 75th Street near Freda, which is east of the community of Raleigh.
Emergency management reported flash flooding including the flooding of the basement of Eldon City Hall and street and highway flooding in and around the town of Eldon.
A trained spotter relayed that multiple creeks were out of banks with and estimated 6 inch depth of water flowing across highway 16. Spotter was uncertain when flooding began.

Numerous local and county roads closed due to high water. A couple were rescued by boat from the roof of their vehicle on State Road 43. Additional water rescues were done across Owen and Monroe counties. 1500 Fish Creek road was completely flooded with water rapidly flowing across the road. White Road along Raccoon Creek was destroyed by flood waters. Across the county roads have suffered severe damage, 23 culverts have been washed out and 2 bridges have significant damage. In all, over 30 Owen County roads are closed. A local emergency disaster declaration was created later in the day.
Sand bags were deployed to help hold back flash flooding in Prairieton. Numerous roads were closed across southern Vigo county due to water flows.
Highway CC at Lock Creek was flooded and impassable.
County Road 410 North between County Road 1000 East and State Road 46 was washed out by rapidly flowing water destroying a pipe. Water was noted to be flowing over the road over the time.
Highway 86 at Shoal Creek was flooded and impassable.
Water was reported over the road at Highway 43 and Iris Road making it impassable to traffic.
State Road 32 closed due to water flowing over the road near the Montgomery Fountain county line. Additional roads closed across the area.
Numerous water rescues were performed during the early morning hours of June 19th. Many county and state roads were under water as a result of locations receiving more than 7 inches of rain.

A 31 year old male was swept away in a vehicle in floodwaters from clear creek near the intersection of College Avenue and Dodds Street. Another person of unknown age and sex was also in the vehicle at the time but was able to escape with only minor injuries. Numerous videos and pictures showed standing water along portions of the downtown including Walnut Street. Many businesses in the area remained shut down for a week to clean up issues related to the flood waters. Water rushed into a nursing home which required the building to evacuate.
Numerous roads were noticed to be closed later in the day by NWS employee. Roads were closed due to rapidly rising floodwaters earlier in the night.
Rapidly flowing water over State Road 244 in southern Rush county. A section of County Road 1000 South was washed out by flood waters.
Water rescues performed in northern Morgan county. Rapidly rising waters also got into several homes across the county.
A house along State Road 135 South had rapidly rising flood waters enter the building. Damage was noted to several bridges across the rural portions of the county.

Dozens of roads closed due to rapidly rising waters including State Roads 235, 135, and 268. A water rescue was conducted to help a trapped semi driver who drove through rapidly flowing flood waters. Two other motorists were rescued after driving into high water.
Campo Road flooded between Avocado Rd and Via Mercado. Three vehicles were stuck in the water.
Twitter picture of a car halfway under water.

Nearly 3 inches of rain fell from a thunderstorm inside of a 1 hour period of time in the Big Island area, including along Camden Road. Rainfall rates were observed to be as high as 5 inches per hour at times during the event. Runoff from this rainfall caused Camden Road to become flooded by several inches of water and impassible. Water was also reported by law enforcement entering a basement of a home. FLASH (Flooded Locations and Simulated Hydrographs Project) estimated that 1-hour rainfall was about 2.5 times that of Flash Flood guidance and that this was a 25 to 50-year event per FLASH 1-Hour ARI estimates.

Over four inches of rain was measured over various parts of southwest Kidder County, with radar estimates of over six inches. In the city of Steele, many roads were under water. Over rural portions of the county affected by the heavy rain, multiple gravel road and culvert washouts occurred.

Over five inches of rain was measured over parts of west-central into northeast Emmons County, with over seven inches indicated on radar, leading to flash flooding. In Hazelton, streets and yards flooded. Near Braddock, a mail delivery vehicle was swept away in flood waters, along with another vehicle. Multiple rural roads were heavily damaged.

Up to five inches of rain fell in the Williston area as multiple rounds of thunderstorms passed through. This led to widespread street flooding, with water affecting many homes. In addition, multiple vehicles were damaged by the flood waters. This includes a combination of parked vehicles and ones where the driver entered the flood waters.

Heavy rain, falling at rates of 2 to locally 5 inches per hour, caused the railroad underpass along Business Highway 220 to be flooded by several feet of standing water. The underpass was reopened after the water receded.
Runoff from heavy rain caused by a thunderstorm was observed flowing across Stone Mountain Road at M. P. Drive. No damage was reported and the road was reopened after the flood waters receded.

Runoff from heavy rain caused by a thunderstorm resulted in several inches of flowing water across S. Henry Street near the Adams Mart. No damage was reported and the road was passable after the flood waters receded.

Between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain fell within a 90-minute period across the community of Boonsboro, at times falling at rates of 4 to 5 inches per hour. This is roughly a 10-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. This rainfall caused flooding across Walnut Hollow Road at Indered Farm Road. The road was reopened and passable after the water receded. No damage was reported.

Monsoon moisture increasing from the south brought thunderstorms across northern Arizona. Heavy Rain in Utah produced flash flooding in the Paria River that flows into Arizona and the gauge near Lees Ferry rose from 4.4 feet to 6.3 feet at 4:30 AM MST.

Rainfall of between 2.5 and 3 inches fell within a 90-minute period near the community of Keeling, at times falling at rates of 4 to 5 inches per hour. This is estimated to be a 10- to 25-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency Estimates. The heavy rain caused a tributary of Birch Creek to overflow its banks across Richmond Highway, temporarily closing the highway until the water receded. No damage to the road was reported.

Water was observed flowing several inches deep across River Ridge Road as Plain Run Branch overflowed its banks. Doppler radar indicated that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain fell in the area during a 3-hour period from a slow-moving thunderstorm. This amount was between a 10- and 25-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates.
Kickapoo Creek reached record levels, resulting in the flooding of several homes in Lawndale. The basement walls of one house collapsed, destroying the structure.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Lamesa. There was a video of at least a foot of flowing water over roads in Lamesa. The damage estimate in Lamesa due to a thunderstorm downburst plus flooding was around ten million dollars.

Evacuations of several homes along Lost Creek in the City of Seneca occurred as the creek rose rapidly out of its banks. Water was reported in basements and some businesses. No injuries were reported.
The bridge at the intersection of Martin and Elder Roads was reported as underwater as Carver Creek flowed out of its banks. .
Bethel Road south of Kentucky Road was washed out from heavy rainfall and flooding.

Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of rain fell from a slow-moving thunderstorm across the Blackwater Creek watershed during a 90-minute period. The Town of Stratton suffered major impact due to flash flooding.
The Town of Windham suffered major impact due to flash flooding. Wheeler Road was closed as a six foot culvert washed away. Other damage in the town were to ditches and drainage culverts.

Significant flash flooding was reported across southern portions of Nashville. Numerous roads were flooded and closed including Sawyer Brown Road at the railroad underpass, Old Hickory Blvd at Health Park Drive, I-24 West at I-40, Charlotte Avenue at I-40 East, and Hogan Road at Regent Drive. In addition, Richland Creek in Belle Meade at Harding Place reached moderate flood stage with considerable flooding reported along the creek.

Report received via Broadcast Media of water completely covering lanes and shoulder on I-2/US-83 Eastbound near Mercedes. Lanes were closed as a result. Multiple water rescues eventually were needed. Video was also received via social media of water rising up to homes in the Mercedes area.
An NWS Employee reported water up to two feet deep resulting in stalled vehicles on the westbound Frontage Road near Rio Grande Valley Premium Outlets near Mercedes.
A Co-Op Observer reported 5.8 inches of rain occurring between 10:30 AM and 2:00 PM, along with minor flooding in the Port Mansfield area. One house also experienced flooding.
Highway Y was flooded and impassable at Cowskin Creek.

A local apple orchard owner reported that 'a massive amount of flood water', overflowed the Bitterroot irrigation canal after heavy rain. This flood water carved 18 ditches through about 3 rows of his orchard. In addition, hail shredded some leaves of trees and strong winds toppled a 20-year old pine tree. After assessing the damage he felt there would be no crop of apples in 2021.
Runoff from a heavy rain event over the Coal Hollow Fire Burn Scar flowed over railroad tracks and onto the south shoulder of U.S. Highway 6.

Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding on Harris Wash. The flooding occurred later as peak flow worked around from Alvy Wash into Harris Wash. Also, the Escalante River gauge near Escalante indicated a 702 CFS flood wave, with a time above 300 CFS from 1845 MDT to 2015 MDT.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 23 CFS to 1450 CFS with the primary flood wave. The time above 1000 CFS was from 2315 MDT to 0130 MDT.
Flooding was reported at Main and Mill Streets.
Multiple roads in the area had flooding issues.
A water rescue was needed along Delaware Road for a car stranded in flood water.

Multiple reports of flash flooding in and around the Village of Fonda. A small creek north of Fonda overflowed its banks causing 6 to 8 inches of water and mud to flow down Broadway (Route 30A) to Main Street (Route 5), causing multiple roads to be closed. Road shoulders were washed out on Old Johnson Road. The Interstate 90 off-ramps were closed at Exit 28 in the village of Fultonville due to flooding.

Widespread roadway flooding occurred in Valley Township, Coatesville and South Coatesville. There were numerous water rescues. Minor flooding occurred along the West Branch of the Brandywine Creek in and around Coatesville and South Coatesville.
A water rescue took place at the intersection of South Union Avenue and Park Place in Yeadon.
Minor flooding occurred along Frankford Creek.
Flash flooding was observed along KY1428 in the city of Allen. One lane of the road was impassable.
A family had to be rescued from their mobile home by boat due to flooding. Several vehicles were damaged.
Flash flooding was reported on Genesee Road in Sardinia.
Washout reported on White Oak Drive in Barnstead.
Major road washout and undermining along Lake Shore Rd in Gilford.
Several roads were closed due to flooding, and approximately 20 swift water rescues occurred.
The Town of Grafton suffered major impact due to flash flooding. Damage was concentrated along portions of Kidder Hill Road and Hinkley Brook Road.

The Town of Townshend suffered major impact due to flash flooding. At least two roads were closed with many other roads damaged. Creeks and streams were out of their banks with many back roads impassable. Culverts were overwhelmed and washed out some roads. Twelve individuals were reported isolated individuals due to main road washouts. Two individuals needed to be evacuated from their homes. Some residential damage was also reported.
Severe street flooding was reported.

Heavy rained washed out NH Route 124 by the town garage. Maple Lane was completely washed out and needed a temporary bridge due to approximately 25 residents being stranded. The first round of rainfall came around 8 PM EDT dropping close to 3 inches. This was followed by a second round of heavy rain shortly before midnight. The area recorded 5.5 over a 12 hour period.

There was a significant amount of flood damage to the northern portion of the Town of Nassau. Several roads were closed, including Burden Lake Road and Nassau-Averill Park Road. Route 66 was closed due to debris over the road at Pike's Pond.
A road construction project on Edgewood Drive over a creek was washed out due to flooding. A portion of East Street was also closed.
County Road 500 was flooded and impassable at Prairie Creek.
Flooding in town forced an ambulance to detour to reach its destination.
SE 601 Road was flooded and impassable at Coon Creek.
Highway Y was flooded and impassable at Cowskin Creek.
Excessive rainfall caused flooding across the city of Bolivar. Some homes were flooded or had sewage water in their basements. Numerous roads were also flooded and impassable.
Portions of E 146th Street S were flooded near S Division Street. Three people were rescued from their flooded homes.
Portions of E 121st Street S were flooded near S Memorial Drive.
Flooding was reported at the intersection of Gibson Street and N York Street.
Numerous roads were flooded in and around Morgantown.
Numerous roads were reported to be flooded in Westover.
Heavy rain led to several buildings being flooded on Bennington's South Street.

Flooding caused a culvert to fail and washed out a bridge at Hinesburg Road and Melchen Road in Brattlesboro, VT. A vehicle drove into the washed out section of road and overturned, but there were no injuries. Akley Road was also closed due to flooding.
Multiple roads were damaged due to flooding in West Brattleboro.
A section of Swamp Road was reported flooded and impassable.
North Street was closed between Burke Avenue and New Road in Pittsfield due to flooding.

Larimer County Sheriff reported flash flooding near Glen Haven. An estimated 1.2 inches of rain fell in one hour. The areas around Steamside Drive and Fishermans Lane just north of Glen Haven were most impacted by floodwaters from Miller Fork.
Widespread roadway flooding occurred in South Philadelphia. There were a few water rescues.
Widespread roadway flooding occurred in Camden and in Pennsauken Township with numerous water rescues reported.
Several streets in Carlisle experienced flash flooding. Cost of damage is unknown.
A vehicle got stuck in flood waters covering North Maple Street. Cost of damage is unknown.
One vehicle swept off the roadway on box canyon road with 10 to 12 other vehicles potentially stranded.
Flooding on Varner road near Bermuda Dunes.
Buckhorn and Mill Rd sustained washouts from flash flooding.
Mountain Rd and Cheney Rd in Newbury sustained significant flooding and washouts.
Multiple streets and intersections were under high water across the southern portions of Corpus Christi. Several cars became stranded in the high water.
FM 70 between Chapman Ranch and Bishop was closed due to flooding along with Weber Road to the southwest of Corpus Christi.

High water occurred at multiple intersections along Crosstown Expressway, along Highway 44 between Robstown and Corpus Christi. Leopard Street and North Padre Island Drive was closed. Several cars became stranded in the water.
Highway closures occurred due to high water along Highway 77 from Robstown to Calallen and along Interstate 37 from Calallen to Annaville.

The Town of Putney suffered major impact due to flash flooding. Numerous roads were closed throughout the town with Putney Mountain, Holland Hill, Pine Banks and River Road the hardest hit. A culvert collapsed on Putney Mountain Road with additional areas along the road washed out. A large section of River Road was washed away. Approximately 300 individuals were reported isolated individuals due to main road washouts. The Putney General Store on Kimball Hill reported damage due to flooding.
Significant damage with multiple road washouts. Scott Pond Road was completely washed away where the causeway crossed over a pond. This road damage caused 12 homes to be isolated.

Two rounds of heavy rain impacted Keene on the evening of the 17th. The first round came around 9 PM causing some localized flash flooding. Shortly after midnight another round of heavy rainfall moved over the area resulting in another surge of floodwaters into the city. In all, over 80 residential basements flooded along with several businesses. A large sinkhole developed on Roxbury Street with severe damage. There were at least 2 evacuations, one on Wetmore Street and another at Boston Place.

The Town of Westminster suffered major impact due to flash flooding. Roads around the town were disintegrated making them impassable along with at least one culvert washed away. There were reports of mudslides and standing water on other roads around the town. One home off Henwood Hill Road is uninhabitable when rock and gravel and debris was deposited against the foundation and flood water gouged a new riverbed next to the house, where a large culvert had been. Farther up the road, severe washouts resulted in one of two cases of cars to end up in a massive ditch. An out-of-state driver suffered a concussion after ending up in a gouged-out ditch along a portion of Orchard Hill Road.
In Worcester, flash flood waters were up to car windshields on Dale Street.
In Worcester, five cars were stuck in flood waters at Dewey Street and Parker Street.
Highway O was flooded and impassable at a low water area.
Roads between Highway 65 and Highway H along EE were flooded and impassable.
Several streets were flooded in town including along Highway 60 and Main Street.
Highway P was flooded and impassable at Lindley Creek.
Route O was closed and impassable at Rule Creek.
Several streets reported flooded near Highway 21 and Dummyline Rd.
A vehicle driven into a flooded intersection, was washed off the road and into a ditch, where the driver needed to be rescued.

Various reports of flooding in Miami Beach reported via an off duty NWS meteorologist and the public via social media. Water was reported to exceed curbs on Collins Avenue, significant street flooding occurring with water above curbs and halfway up vehicle tires, reports of water entering buildings at Collins Avenue and 41st Street, and water halfway up vehicle tires near 86th Street and Harding Avenue.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported up to 2.5 feet of water on streets in Enoch, as well as water breaching into homes. The water was deepest near Homestead Boulevard. Several homes were flooded.
There were numerous roads flooded in the town of Lenox. All available firefighters were called in by the Lenox Fire Department.
There was a report of flowing water moving across Housatonic Street.
There was report of flowing water and debris from a nearby stream moving across Walker Street.
Law enforcement reported Werden Road flooded near an egg farm.
Law enforcement reported Leonhart Road in Becket flooded.
West Center Road was flooded with some rocks and debris left behind.
West Center Road was flooded with some rocks and debris left behind.
Flooding conditions were reported on State Route 22 south of Boston Corners Road in the town of Ancram.
Route 9W was closed due to flooding between Glasco Turnpike and Belevedere Lane.
Heavy rain produced multiple debris flows over CO-125 between mile markers 10 and 15. The road was closed and some travelers were stranded.
Heavy rain produced localized flash flooding.
Flash flooding along Tonahutu Creek forced the shut down of Grand Lake's hydro plant.
Pump Station Road was made impassable due to water over the road.
Debris flows blocked roadways at the top of Chestnut Stand Road and Sweet Lick Road near Irvine.

Flashing flooding issues were reported along Blaines Branch just off of Hwy 52 past the intersection with Robinson Hollow Road. Roughly 2 feet of water was over the road and some of the black top was removed. The road had to be closed due to the flooding and damage to the road surface. A video was also shared with the NWS Jackson, KY weather office by the Lee County EM of a culvert being washed away.

Radar estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rainfall at the mouth of Box Canyon which caused flash flooding at the entrance of Box Canyon Road and along Painted Canyon Road. There were a couple vehicles involved with the flooding which caused a road closure. Located south of I-10 and north of Highway 111.
Caltrans reports boulders in the roadway near Vista Point on SR 74.
Road closures were reported due to flooding with vehicles stranded in the streets.
Multiple washouts on local roads in Milton. Roads include Mason Rd, Teneriffe Rd, and Morgan Dr.
Numerous roads were closed or washed out due to high water across the northwest part of the county, including Crymes Road, Kings Road, and Falls Road.
Danforth Corners Road in Hillsboro flooded and impassable.
FM 774 east of Refugio was closed due to flooding.
Interstate 37 closed due to flooding between Mathis and Edroy. Several roads closed in the communities of Mathis, Odem, and Sinton. SH 359 underpass in Mathis closed due to flooding.
FM 1069 and Highway 35 near Aransas Pass was closed due to flooding.
Multiple roads were closed due to flooding around Ingleside.
State Highway 361 on Mustang Island had water covering the road.
The Town of Drummerston suffered major impact due to flash flooding. Approximately 20 individuals were reported isolated individuals due to main road washouts.

The Town of Arlington suffered minor impact from flash flooding. Many roads were flooded and closed around the town. Residential damages were reported by emergency management. Vermont Route 313 was closed due to flooding near the Sandgate Intersection.
Law Enforcement reported that a portion of Roxbury Street in Keene was washed out due to flash flooding.

Multiple roads washed out. Scott Pond Road, Warren Hill Rd, Royalston Rd, Sandy Hollow Rd, Rhododendron Rd, Old Coach Road, Lower Templeton Tpke. Nearby rain gages reported between 4 to 6 inches of rainfall, with the heaviest rain shortly after midnight.
Idaho Transportation Department reported water running across Idaho Highwy 37 between Lawery Lane and Cow Canyon Road.
A NWS survey found evidence of an extensive mud slide along and across Highway 75 North of Clayton.
Heavy rains caused several rock and mud slides along Trail Creek Road for several days.
Five roads in Eudora were closed due to flooding.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Depression Ida caused flash flooding along Zion Ridge Road.
Route V was closed and impassable due to flooding at Weaubleau Creek.
Highway A was flooded and impassable near a headwater tributary of Indian Creek.
Highway 86 was flooded and impassable between Harrison Avenue and Highway M.
Flooding was reported at low water areas along Tower Road.
Highway YY was flooded and impassable at North Deer Creek.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in several instances of flash flooding across southern Choctaw County. Roads were flooded in the Bethsalem area as well as French Camp.

A vehicle was trapped in flood waters on Woodland Drive in Plainsboro Township, requiring a water rescue. Another water rescue took place on Dey Road. Plainsboro Pond overflowed, closing Maple Avenue.
Heavy rain over the Ether Hollow Fire Burn Scar produced a debris flow that moved across Quiet Meadows Lane on the outskirt of Mapleton.
Law enforcement officials reported a debris flow moved through the Pinnacles and Promised Land Resort areas.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sunglow Canyon.
A debris flow was reported into the Elk Ridge area.
Hildale Fire Department dispatch personnel reported water flowing over three street crossings. The streets were closed due to the flows.
A few roads were closed due to flooding in Squirrel Hill, with vehicles stranded.
US Route 44 was closed due to flash flooding between Banghall and 9 Partners Lane in Washington.
Eight to ten roads were closed due to flooding around Prattsville.
Heavy rain caused localized flash flooding in Erie. Standing water stranded vehicles at the Intersection of Highway 7 and Mountain View Blvd. A couple of basements also flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 14 near Mile Markers 87-89. The area had to be blocked off until the floodwaters receded.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 125, with mud and debris flows crossing the roadway. The highway was closed temporarily to clear off the debris. The U.S. Forest Service reported flooding and some damage on Cabin Creek and Buffalo Creek Roads.
A car was stalled in floodwaters on McKinley Street.
Cars were stalled in flood waters near Ogden Avenue and Western Avenue.
A car was stalled in flood waters at an underpass near Ashland Avenue and Kinzie Street.
Multiple photos and videos shared on social media showed flooding of underpasses along Lake Shore Drive.

Between roughly 403 and 418 pm, several homes along Geneva Ave in Irvine were damaged by flood waters. Several more homes had water flowing into them. A few water rescues were needed in this area as well.

Damage and washed out section of concrete sidewalk as embankment gave way to flooding along Country Club Drive and Avenue 42. Water covered roadway on Jefferson Street. Photos shared by emergency management. Rain of 0.70 inch per hour observed.
High Street was closed due to flooding.
Market Street was flooded and closed.
Stranded vehicles in high water were reported on West Hundred Road and Jefferson Davis Highway. One water rescue was performed.
Car was stranded due to high water.
Osborne Road at Old Stage Road was closed due to high water.
Chester Road at Perrymont Road was closed due to high water.
Nearly 70 percent of all roads in Petersburg were closed due to flooding at the height of the event.

The Town of Newport sustained significant flooding to properties and businesses along NH Route 103 in the area of 48 John Stark Highway. Flood waters were 1 to 2 feet deep throughout a business plaza which sustained significant damages. The confluence of the Sugar River and its South Branch occurs just west of the impacted areas. The nearest river gage is located approximately 10 river miles to the west at an elevation of 500ft higher. The river did not reach flood stage at Claremont, but did show a notable increase in discharge from about 350cfs in the afternoon of the 29th, to a crest over 5,000cfs in the early morning hours of the 30th.
Numerous roads washed out and flooded in and around Loudon. Washouts were reported on Bumfagon Rd, Storrs Dr, Hollow Route Rd, and Gilmanton Rd where significant damage occurred.
State Highway 35 was closed due to flooding.
Multiple roads around San Diego had water covering the roadways.
Flash flooding was reported along United States Highway 301 near Ward Boulevard.
East Market street was reported closed between 9th Street and North Malta Street due to flash flooding.
Flash flooding was reported along Progressive Church Road. A portion of the road was washout as well.

The Town of Athens suffered minor impact due to flash flooding. Seven roads in the town suffered significant damage. One town culvert was washed out. There was also damage to the town office parking lot. Approximately 10 individuals were reported isolated individuals due to main road washouts.

Several clusters of thunderstorms with heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across northern Shelby County. Several roads were impassable along the Jefferson/Shelby county line with rain amounts estimated near 2 inches in one hour.
Erosion along several local roads, primarily shoulders and pavement damage. Majority of the damage occurred in the evening.

Jaffrey airport reported 6.9 in 18 hours, measuring 6 to 8 inches of rain in 24 hours. More than 15 roads were washed out, one of which lost a major culvert. Damage figures were estimated over $1 million mainly for damage to roads and bridges. There was a voluntary evacuation for 39 homes on Letourneau Drive off Nutting Road after a bridge was flooded by a small stream.

Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in flash flooding across Jones County. The intersection of Hines Road and Service Road was flooded. Several streets in Laurel were flooded including 5th Street, 16th Avenue and Jefferson Street at Leontyne Boulevard.
Stellers and Cook Hill Roads were flooded and impassable due to heavy rainfall.
A portion of Highway 37 was flooding and impassable due to heavy rainfall.
Spencer Drive in Meadview was flooded and covered with mud.
At least three roads were closed, at least one home was inundated, and major flooding occurred inside the park, impacting several campground cabins.
Two feet of water flooded Temple Bar Road.
Two to three feet of water flooded DW Ranch Road from 1225 to 1330, and again from 1425 to 1600.
The Virgin stream gauge on the Virgin River at Virgin spiked from 108 CFS to 2180 CFS, a rise of over 3 feet.

Zion National Park dispatch personnel reported numerous slot canyons experienced flooding, including Pine Creek and Spry Canyon. The Zion automated weather station recorded 1.29 inches of rain in one hour. In addition, the East Fork Virgin stream gauge on the East Fort Virgin River near Springdale recorded a peak flow of 2790 CFS.
Several vehicles were stuck in high water in the area of both Thompson Run Road and Rodi Road.
Widespread roadway flooding occurred in East Whiteland Township, including Conestoga Road, North Bacton Hill Road and Planebrook Road.
Minor flooding occurred along the East Branch of the Brandywine Creek between West Bradford Township and East Bradford Township.
Law enforcement reported flooding of streets along the Housatonic River in New Milford.
Law enforcement reported numerous streets flooded in Watertown. Some creeks and streams have also overflowed their banks.
Heavy rainfall washed out County Roads 43 and 44H, along with several residential driveways and roads that crossed Buckhorn Creek north of Stringtown Gulch Road.
Localized flash flooding occurred over Highway 14 near Mile Marker 80.
Public reported two cars stranded in flood waters along I80 in a low spot.
Water was flowing across the road on Town Line Road at Lower Mountain Road.
Water and debris was flowing over Blackman Road.
High water was over Rives Road.
Water was covering the intersection of Woods Edge Road and Ruffin Mill Road.
Boydton Plank Road at Franklin Street was closed due to high water.
Cattail Road at Barnetts Road was closed due to high water.
Old Town Farm road washed out due to the heavy rain. A dozen homes were cut off from emergency access due to the road closure.
Clinton Rd, NH 31, was washed out from the Great Brook due to the heavy rains.
Numerous roads were flooded in and around Princeton.
Flash flooding was reported along Highway 421 near Washington Avenue and Wilmington Avenue.
Cars were reported flooded in downtown Princeton.
Two cars stalled in flood waters in the 6000 block of Fairview Church Road.
Flash flooding was reported near the intersection of Old Glenola Road and Tabacco Road.
The Town of Brookline suffered minor impact due to flash flooding. Numerous driveways were washed away along with damage to roads throughout the town.
Media reported Old Town Road in Peterborough washed out on both sides of the road.

Acworth was the hardest hit community during the flash flooding on July 29th. Localized rainfall amounts on July 29th approached or exceeded 4.5 inches in less than six hours. Reports from FEMA and State Officials list 75% of the town's 29 roads were damaged. Multiple bridges were damaged and destroyed. Reports on damages ranged from approximately 2 to 7 million dollars. Most damage was on Crane Brook Road and Charlestown Road at Luther Hill Road. Local officials claim damage was the worst since the 2005 floods.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Rolling Oaks Dr. was flooded at Yorks Creek near Wimberley.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Huntress Ln. was flooded west of Scenic Loop at Leon Creek west of Leon Springs.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Toutant Beauregard Rd. was flooded at Balcones Creek south of Boerne.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Old Fredericksburg Rd. was flooded north of Lost Creek Gap near Leon Springs.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Little Arkansas Rd. was flooded at the Blanco River southeast of Wimberley.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Spring Branch Rd. at Rittimann Rd. was flooded by the Spring Branch.
Thunderstorms dumped around 2 inches of rain over Green Bay during the evening hours. This caused several roads to be closed due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Geer Canyon in the Calwood burn area.
The driver of a stalled car was rescued from flood water on Woodland Drive.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Manalapan Township and in Englishtown. Numerous roads in Manalapan Township were closed including Spotswood-Englishtown Road, Wilson Avenue, Sobechko Road, Union Hill Road and Conmack Lane. Main Street in Englishtown was closed due to flooding.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Cranbury Township. Numerous roadways were inundated and there were several water rescues. Brainerd Lake overflowed its banks, closing Main Street. A water rescue took place on Old Trenton Road.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in East Windsor Township and in Hightstown. Numerous roads were closed due to flooding. Water rescues took place along Hankins Road near Woodland Drive, and at the intersection of Mercer Street and Airport Road in East Windsor Township. US Route 130 was closed to the south of Princeton-Hightstown Road in East Windsor Township. Franklin Street was closed to the east of North Main Street in Hightstown.

The Millstone River overflowed its banks in West Windsor Township, inundating several roads. Grovers Mill Pond overflowed its banks in West Windsor Township, flooding several roads and damaging nearby buildings.
A portion of East Starbuck Lane was washed away due to flash flooding in the Town of Fort Ann.
Water was observed over the roadway on Drifting Ridge Road and Tori Trace in the Town of Fort Edward.
U.S. Route 4 was impassable at Black House Road in the Town of Fort Edward due to flash flooding.
Portions of S 209th E Avenue were flooded with up to five feet of water. A vehicle was driven into the flood water, and the driver had to be rescued.
Water and debris flowed over Aztec Road and Bacobi Road near Shinarump Drive.
Water flowed over Stockton Hill Road.
Water flowed over Gordon Drive.
Main Street was flooded with water and debris.
Half an inch of rain in 15 minutes caused flooding of Dogwood Street between Minneola Road and Spyrock Avenue.
Water, rocks, and mud flooded the intersection of Old Fort Irwin Road and Old Highway 58.

Report received of minor street flooding in and around Burlington, CO. Another report of 1.4 inches of storm total rain was received via social media with photo of a rain gauge at one location. This heavy rain produced enough rain for water to reach the running boards on a jeep (estimated 4-6 inches deep).
A house reportedly was inundated with water up to the first floor.
There was a report of an entire road being impassable near Route 41 and Lambert Road.
Carson County also reported that a car was swept off the road and stranded in the ditch on Highway 207 1 mile north of Panhandle.
Minor flooding occurred along the Bush Kill in Middle Smithfield Township.
Minor flooding occurred along the Brodhead Creek near East Stroudsburg.
Tobyhanna Creek overflowed its banks near Blakeslee.
Minor flooding occurred along the Pohopoco Creek at Kresgeville.
Public reported street flooding and a stranded vehicle.

County comms reported flash flooding developed from a combination of poor drainage and overflowing small streams after 4 to 7 inches of rain fell in the Green Creek area in just a couple of hours. Multiple roads were inundated and closed. A driveway was also washed out, necessitating rescue of a resident.
Philmont Avenue was closed near Pine Road in Lower Moreland Township due to flooding.
A water rescue took place on the Hollow Road ramp to the Schuylkill Expressway in Lower Merion Township.
PA Route 447 was closed near PA Route 191 to the north of Analomink due to flooding.

A water rescue took place on US Route 202 near the US Route 30 Bypass in West Whiteland Township. Valley Road was under water at Valley Creek. Several vehicles were trapped in flood waters on the Lincoln Highway near the Pottstown Pike in West Whiteland Township. Rocks and debris were washed onto Cockerham Lane by flood waters.
Public reported via mPing river/creek overflowing; cropland/yard/basement flooding.
Additional reports of widespread flooding were received with stranded vehicles in other portions of Lockport.
A state of emergency was issued that included a travel ban due to widespread flooding in Niagara County.
RT-140 road washed out at Halls Hill Rd due to the heavy rain.

Flash riverine flooding occurred on the evening of the 29th in Alstead. Flood waters upstream in Acworth along the Cold River resulted in a washout of the Route 123A road near Kelley Road. River levels from the USGS Cold River at Alstead gage reported an all time peak flow of 11.46 feet and a flow of 10,500cfs, cresting at 11 PM on the 29th. The period of record is relatively short dating back to 2009, but significant damage occurred in the Cold River basin with an estimated 50 to 75 year flood event based on USGS data.
A group of 23 kayakers had to be rescued due to flash flooding on Shoal Creek near Iron City, but no one was injured.
Rabbit Trail Road was closed due to flooding and a culvert being washed out.
A low water bridge was flooded and impassable at Bishop Chapel Road near Sweet Home Road.
Two vehicles that drove into flood waters were swept away into a creek on Mockerson Road at Day Road. No injuries were reported.
The Town of Jamaica suffered minor impact due to flash flooding. There were many reports of damage to roads, bridges and culverts across town. A portion of River Road was reported to have collapsed.

In Lempster, the town lost access to 15 roads. 24 culverts were damaged or destroyed, and the recovery effort was further exacerbated by the closure of State Route 12 also caused by flash flooding. Rainfall estimates were between 3 and 5 inches on the evening of the 29th.
The town of Langdon lost emergency access to 18 residents and closed three roads due to road washouts caused by the heavy rain.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding and led to Vandiford Thomas Road to be closed near Taylor Road.
Mount Herman Church Road was closed near North Carolina Highway 91 due to flash flooding.

An NWS Employee was reporting very heavy rainfall which was causing urban flooding, resulting in vehicles close enough to getting stuck. It was very difficult to see road with wipers on full speed. This was occurring along Southland Blvd from Knickerbocker Rd to Southwest Blvd.
An amateur radio operator reported that Sul Ross Rd at the Red Arroyo was impassable and emergency vehicles was blocking the entrance.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Cypress Cove Rd. was flooded by Rebecca Creek northeast of Spring Branch.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Heuermann Rd was flooded north of Babcock Rd. south of Leon Springs.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. FM 335 was flooded near the Nueces River north of Barksdale.
U.S. Route 4 and Lock Road in the Town of Fort Edward was impassable due to flash flooding. The inside of Turning Point Wesleyan Church on U.S. Route 4 was also flooded.
Portions of O'Brien Road and Anthony Road in the Town of Fort Edward were washed out due to flash flooding.
Pleasant Valley Road was closed due to mud and debris left behind by flash flooding.
Flowing water and debris was reported across County Route 36 or Clauverwie Road in Middleburgh.

Gorge Creek overflowed its banks due to debris blocking a culvert, which sent water flowing across Main Street at Wells Avenue. There was water and electrical damage at the Middleburgh High School. Strub Lane was also filled with mud and debris. In addition, basement flooding was also occurring within the village.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in both the main canyon and in tributaries feeding the canyon from the east.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sulphur Creek, with water running 6-12 inches high. Also flash flooding occurred in the Fremont River and Grand Wash.
Urban flash flooding was reported in Cedar City. A video received via social media showing water flowing down streets near the Ashdown Subdivision.
Flash flooding caused mud and rock slides along Highway 168 near Aspendell, blocking the road and causing several vehicles to be stuck.
Lillyhill Drive was flooded six to eight inches deep near Bailey Avenue.
Flash flooding in Cold Creek washed out the shoulders of some roads.
One foot of water flowed over the intersection of Boulder Highway and Sunset.
Hidden Valley Road was closed at the Muddy River crossing due to flooding.
Water flowed over Interstate 15 near Moapa, causing traffic to be diverted.
Several roads in and around Independence, especially those near Whiskey creek had water over them and were closed during the flooding.
Multiple roads in the northwest part of the county were closed due to unsafe driving conditions and water over the road.
A water rescue took place on North Gulph Road in King of Prussia.
A water rescue took place on DeKalb Street in Bridgeport. US Route 202 was closed in Bridgeport due to flooding.
Moderate flooding occurred along Valley Creek near Valley Forge.
A water rescue took place at the intersection of Paper Mill Road and Harston Lane in Flourtown.
A water rescue took place on Ashmead Road in Cheltenham.
Minor flooding occurred along the Wissahickon Creek in Philadelphia.
Pump Station Road was closed from Highway 93 to Back Road due to flooding.
Water and debris flowed over Stockton Hill Road.
Antares Road was closed after flooding carved a foot deep rut into the road.
Flooding at 14th St and Veterans Dr in Traverse City.

Three water rescues took place in West Chester. One was at the intersection of East Gay Street and Montgomery Avenue, another was at the intersection of South Bolmar Street and Union Street, and a final one was at the intersection of Union Street and South Franklin Street.

A water rescue took place at the intersection of Sugartown Road and Morris Road in Radnor Township. Also, there was widespread roadway flooding in Radnor Township with multiple vehicles trapped in the flood waters. There was a rockslide on Strafford Avenue near Lancaster Avenue.
Route 425 was reported to be closed between Lower and Upper Mountain Roads.
Multiple roads washed out including South Street, Quarry Rd, West Hill Rd, Prospect Rd, and Brook Rd. Perkins Pond dam was overtopping near Monadnock St and Sand Dam.

The Town of Rockingham suffered significant damage to roads and infrastructure due to flash flooding. Numerous roads were closed around town including Ski Bowl, Leach, Rockingham Hill, Hartley Hill, Pleasant Valley, Paradise, Hall Bridge, Corey Hill and Darby Hill. Residential damage was also reported. The Laurel Avenue-Hyde Hill neighborhood in Bellows Falls was blocked by flood debris, sending several feet of water into the area, leaving behind lots of mud.
The Los Fresnos Police Department reported more than 10 streets in the city were experiencing flooding. Floodwaters were rising over curbs and spilling into sidewalks at the time of the report.

North Branch of the Sugar River caused flooding in Goshen. Route 10 closed from Route 31 to Grandview Road with water reported over the road. A campground had to evacuate 25 people due to rising flood waters.

Very intense rainfall led to brief flash flooding across portions of Avon and Plainfield. Several roads had water over the curb while also rapidly flowing. Avon High school was partially flooded after the roof began to leak. 2 reports of rainfall over 4 inches were received with the rainfall occurring over a period of less than 2 hours.
In Chester, flash flooding caused a portion of Skyline Trail to be washed out.
In Belchertown, a portion of River Street, near the Swift River, was flooded and impassable, with people being evacuated.
Flash flooding was observed with water covering yards and flowing beneath mobile homes in the Old Dock community.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in several instances of flash flooding across portions of Kemper County.

Heavy rainfall from Tropical Depression Ida resulted in several instance of flash flooding in the city of Columbus. Hospital Drive was flooded with water backed up into an apartment complex. Portions of 4th Street were also flooded with water entering a home.
Blodgett Road in the Town of Fort Edward was impassable due to flash flooding.
A culvert collapse occurred on U.S. Route 4 in the Town of Fort Edward.
Route 278 and Route 7 were flooded with 2-3 feet of moving water at the intersection. There were reports that Route 278 was impassable and closed.
Flash flooding occurred in a tributary of Shoal Creek. An abandoned pickup truck was observed submerged in the water.
A Capitol Reef National Park official shared a video of flash flooding in Sulphur Creek.
The Overton Wash flooded Highway 169 about two feet deep.
Short Creek flooded and closed several bridges and low water crossings in Colorado City. One vehicle was rescued.
A pickup truck tried to cross a flooded intersection on Queens Bay Road and got swept downstream.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to East Austin Peak Road, and Knight Creek Road was closed from Hackberry Road to milepost 4.6 due to flooding.
Antares Road was closed from Highway 66 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding.
Vehicles were trapped in flood waters in Stroud Township. PA Route 447 was closed to the south of Analomink due to flooding.
Vehicles were trapped in flood waters in Smithfield Township. Little Sambo Creek was out of its banks, flooding some nearby properties in Smithfield Township.
Runoff from locally heavy rain caused a rock slide to occur southeast of Lake City. Debris from the slide went onto U.S. Highway 61.
Heavy rain resulted in numerous roadways, yards, and ditches to be flooded across Roswell. Damages are estimated.
A trained spotter near Cuba reported flash flooding due to heavy rainfall. Extent of damages are unknown.
River Road and Dunham Road in the Town of Sunderland was flooded and impassable.
The Town of Wardsboro suffered minor impact due to flash flooding. Damage occurred across two culverts, undermined pavement and numerous roads.

Numerous water rescues occurred due to flooded streets with vehicles stranded. Some residents were evacuated due to water entering buildings. Water was a foot deep at the Presbyterian Church. Multiple roads were closed in Rockport and Fulton, including Market Street, Champions Drive at Royal Oaks Drive, and FM 2165 from Business 35 to Linden.
Brownsville Police reported that about 30 streets in the city were experiencing flooding. Floodwaters were deep enough to prevent cars from traveling through.

Reports received via social media of flooding along Frontage Road near the Sunrise Mall in Brownsville, with floodwaters reaching up to the headlights of cars. Additional flooding was also noted on FM 802/Ruben Torres Boulevard.
Reports received via public of resacas (oxbow lakes) near Valley International Country Club were overflowing onto parts of FM 802.
Public reports received via social media showed several streets near UTRGV Brownsville Campus were flooded, and portions of the campus were without power due to lightning strikes and/or flooding.
There were several reports of roads flooded or washed out in the Brunswick area, including Moonlawn Road.
Police reported that numerous roadways were flooded and impassable in Glen Cove.
All lanes were closed on the Bronx River Parkway between the Sprain Brook Parkway in Bronxville and Exit 22 in White Plains due to flooding.
Flash flooding was observed at the intersection of Kings Hwy at 10th Street. The road was impassable at this location due to deep water.
Flash flooding reported with numerous streets flooded across town.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding near Fort Davis. Highway 118 between Fort Davis and Alpine was washed out with water over the road. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
In the Millers Falls section of Montague, several streets were closed due to flooding. Federal Street had 3 feet of water in the road. Flood waters were entering a business.
In Deerfield, flash flood waters caused a portion of Conway Road to wash out.
Roadway flooding occurred along the I-10 Frontage Road and in areas surrounding the Memorial City Mall. Multiple cars were stalled as a result of the floodwaters.
Woodard Road in the Town of Fort Edward was closed due to flash flooding.
Hunter Road between Williams Road and Moore Road in the Town of Fort Edward was washed out due to flash flooding.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding along the Escalante River and Calf Creek.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise of 397 CFS, or about 1.5 feet.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a 3 foot rise, with peak flows of 1800 CFS.

Several reports of flash flooding in and around Escalante, including Birch Creek. Storm spotters reported logs and trees floating in the Escalante River just north of Escalante. Time of event coincident with time of first report.
There were at least four swift water rescues, and numerous roads were closed.
Waist deep water flowed over the intersection of Bank Street and Calle Castano.
Hackberry Road was closed from Main Street to Route 66 due to flooding.
Oatman Highway was closed due to flooding.
The intersection of Oatman Highway and Route 66 was flooded.
Signal Road was closed from Highway 93 to Alamo Road due to flooding.

Heavy rain was reported in the are with some estimates of 1-2 inches of rainfall. Law Enforcement reported several inches of water over US Highway 50 at mile marker 9. They also reported several inches of water across SR-488, 487, and US-6.

A quick 2.5 inches of rain in thunderstorms lead to flash flooding of the underpass at the intersection of Maple Road and South Easton Street. Flash flooding also blocked all lanes of traffic along southbound I-75 near 11 mile road.

A quick 1.75 to 2.5 inches of rain in thunderstorms lead to flash flooding on roadways.|Cars were stranded in flood waters at Davison and John C Lodge Freeways. All lanes of traffic along I-75 were flooded in the area of Holbrooke Avenue and 11 Mile Road. Flooding also caused several road closures along M-39 between Joy Road and Rotunda Drive.
Runoff from higher desert terrain and rain falling on an urbanized landscape led to flash flooding across western portions of Rock Springs.

The Town of Newfane suffered a lot of damage due to flooding, especially near the center of town. The WW Building Supply business along Vermont Route 30 reported damage due to flooding. Some residential damage was also reported across the town. A swift water rescue team assessed a housing development and decided to let people shelter in place as that was a safer alternative than moving them across the flooded waters.
Reports received via social media of water rising halfway up wheels on vehicles as well as a few stalled cars in Olmito Estates.

Pictures received via social media of flooding estimated at 2 to 3 feet of water depth at Old Alice Road and Price Road in Brownsville, with water nearing gas pumps and buildings. This location is a flood-prone area which has seen several similar events since 2010.
There were several reports of roads flooded or washed out in the Eagle Mills area, including Garfield Road, Creek Road, and Dater Hill Road.
There were several reports of roads flooded and washed out in the Poestenkill area, including Plank Road, Snyders Corner Road, and Blue Factory Road.

Several clusters of thunderstorms with heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across southern Jefferson County. Several roads were impassable in the Cahaba Heights areas and an observer reported 2.25 inches of rain in one hour.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. There was water over the road on Cielo Vista Dr. south of Vista Mountain Dr. Rainfall in the area was over 2.5 inches in one hour.
Several homes near Heath Road and Dhaka View flooded. There were reports of 1 to 2 feet of water in a few of the residences.
Numerous vehicles were stranded in high water in the area of Red Toad Road and Principio Road.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Jamesburg. Homes and businesses were severely damaged by the flood waters. Many roads were inundated and numerous water rescues took place. Some of the worst of the flooding occurred along Forsgate Drive in the area of Railroad Avenue. Homes near Manalapan Brook were evacuated.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in South Brunswick Township. US Route 130 was closed between Georges Road and Deans Rhode Hall Road. A water rescue took place on Ridge Road. US Route 1 was closed at Raymond Road. Herrod Boulevard was closed with vehicles stranded in the flood waters, requiring several water rescues.

Heavy rainfall over portions of the Mullen Burn Scar with estimated rainfall of two to three inches. Subsequent mudslide and debris flow led to a road washout near Highway 230. The Woods Landing Resort also had nearby stream rise out of its bank with water on area campgrounds and a few inches of water were reported in the resort kitchen.
Spotter reported one inch of rainfall in thirty minutes along with pea size hail.
Received video from Wyoming Game and Fish Biologist of flash flooding along Lake Creek in the Mullen Burn Scar.
The Dollar General store was flooded in the Village of Argyle.

Heavy rains caused several road closures due to high water in the Bangor and Brewer areas. Canterbury and Church Roads were flooded in Brewer. An exit on Interstate 395 was closed due to a dirt washout across the road. In Bangor...Perry Road was closed at the Route 202 overpass due to street flooding.

Video received showed significant flows through a normally dry wash just south of Tropic, including a mature fully grown tree floating beneath an underpass along Bryce Highway. In addition, Bryce Canyon National Park officials reported the closure of the Queens Garden Trail, Navajo Loop, and the road to Bryce Point due to flooding.
Video received showed 2 to 3 feet deep water flowing down a street in Hildale, eroding a portion of the road.

Capitol Reef National Park rangers report 4 to 5 inches of water flowing across Scenic Drive at the first wash crossing. Water 6 to 7 inches deep was reported at the State Route 24 bridge crossing the Grand Wash. Waterfalls were also observed in the park, and debris was flowing down the Fremont River.
Flash flooding washed out the main access road to Old Irontown from State Route 56. Emergency managers stated the road was closed until repaired.
Water and debris flowed across State Route 21.

Beaver County dispatch and emergency management personnel reported street flooding in Milford with water 3 feet deep. In addition, debris from flooding was reported on State Route 21 near Milford. The Milford automated weather station recorded 1.10 inches of rain in one hour.
Pinewood and Lakeview Drive were both closed due to flooding, with over 2 feet of running water at the intersection.
Heavy rain near Weston Pass caused localized flash flooding along State Highway 9 in southern Park County. An SUV got stuck in the flood waters but no injuries were reported.

Substantial flooding was reported on the northwest portion of the East Troublesome burn area which caused localized flash flooding along State Highway 125. The highway was closed north of Granby to the Jackson county line to clear mud and debris from the roadway.
Debris flows associated with flash flooding damaged several forest service roads.
Heavy rain caused water to cover the roadway at Highway 98 and Pine Street.
Flash flooding in Orange Beach with knee high water in some locations. Water also approached homes in the area.
Heavy rain produced localized flash flooding along Kinney Creek. There was some damage to the road. The floodwaters also impacted nearby properties.
Heavy rain and runoff from higher desert landscape produced flash flooding in sections of Rock Springs that had seen similar conditions on July 28.

Mud and rock were observed flowing across switchback portions of Casper Mountain Road leading up the north face of the mountain. The mud and rock were the result of very heavy rain. One observer noted a 24-hour rainfall total of 2.15 inches along Garden Creek just to the west of the switchbacks.
Emergency management and trained spotters reported numerous flooded roads and basements around Kemmerer and Diamondville.

Trained spotters near Jaconita reported flash flooding in the area from heavy rain. The spotters' truck became stuck in the flood waters and mud flow, but no injuries were reported. Damages are estimated for water damage to the truck.

Approximately $1 Million in road damages reported town wide in Peterborogh. Old Town Farm Rd and Old Jaffrey Rd received significant damage. Old Town Farm Road is a dead end and had 18 homes isolated by the road washouts.
Two feet of flood water was reported covering the intersection of 3rd Street at Crutcher Road in East Nashville.
Charlotte Pike at American Road was flooded and impassable.

An off-duty NWS employee reported 2 to 3 feet of water flooding multiple roads in north Brownsville, including Morrison at Stagecoach; a neighborhood between Alton Gloor and east Morrison Blvd.; and a section along Dennet Road east of the Woods' End neighborhood. Several cars had water above their wheels, stalled in the floodwaters. This area had last seen similar flooding on June 19 and 20, 2018.
Per public reports, numerous portions of a Frontage Road in Mercedes were flooded.

Several inches of moving water was reported flowing over Route 43 in several locations between West Sand Lake and Averill Park. Route 66 was washed out as well north of Averill Park. Several other roads were closed or washed out in the Town of Sand Lake, including Holcomb Road, Burden Lake Road, Old Best Road, and Taborton Road.
One lane of Columbia Turnpike was reported closed. In addition, rocks and debris were washed onto some roads in the East Greenbush area.

Rainfall amounts quickly totaled 3 to 5 inches over northern and western Milwaukee County after repeated rounds of heavy rain. Reports of water over Interstate 41 near Wauwatosa, and water completely covering the roads along the Root River Parkway near Cleveland and Oklahoma Streets in West Allis.
In Eastford, a section of Pilfershire Road was washed out. Rainfall totals by early evening included 4.95 inches in Pomfret, 4.75 inches in 2.5 hours in Ashford, and 3.42 inches in Woodstock.
In Pomfret, a portion of Route 244 was partially washed out. Rainfall totals by early evening included 4.95 inches in Pomfret, 4.75 inches in 2.5 hours in Ashford, and 3.42 inches in Woodstock.

In the Warrenville portion of Ashford, flash flooding closed Route 44 over the Mt. Hope River between Route 74 and Route 89. Rainfall totals by early evening included 4.95 inches in Pomfret, 4.75 inches in 2.5 hours in Ashford, and 3.42 inches in Woodstock.
Water covered the road along a portion of County Route 49 in the Town of Argyle.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in portions of the park, including the Narrows, Kolob Canyons, and Telephone Canyon.
The manager of Veyo Pool Resort reported a 7 foot rise on the Santa Clara River. Campsites were evacuated near the river.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding across Scenic Drive in multiple locations, including Grand Wash and across State Route 24, closing the road. A muddy debris flow was also reported in Sulphur Creek.
A Zion Nation Park ranger reported significant flash flooding occurred on Taylor Creek at the north end of the Kolob Canyon area of the park during the night.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported 5 inches of debris, mud, and gravel overflowing the Scenic Drive by the Capitol Gorge area. High-flowing water was also reported in a usually dry wash at the end of the Scenic Drive. Scenic Drive was closed beyond Grand Wash.

Washington County dispatch officials reported water over the road on State Route 17 near Toquerville, briefly closing the road. The bridge where water crossed the road is above full grown trees in the creek below, indicating a significant rise in water level.
Several roads across Terre Haute were closed either due to standing water or water flowing over the road. There was a report of water several inches deep in a house, but no details on the location.
Three feet of water completely covered the road at Commercial Boulevard near Swisshelm Park.
The Carrizozo airport measured 3.95 inches of rain in a short period of time which resulted in flash flooding in the area. Extent of damages is unknown.
Moderate flooding occurred along Cobbs Creek in Philadelphia.
Minor flooding occurred along the Pennypack Creek in Northeast Philadelphia.
Heavy rain caused numerous roads to be flooded in the Foley community with at least a foot of water reported on one of the roads.
Heavy rain caused several roads to be flooded in the Gulf Shores area.

Heavy rain caused water to cover the road along the Foley Beach Express at Doc McDuffie Road. In addition, the nearby river gauge for Wolf Creek rose almost 9 feet in just a couple hours time, resulting in flooding of other roads as well.
Barricades were requested to put out on Joe Sevario Road due to significant street flooding.
