Driver of car that stalled out in deep flood water had to be rescued on La Rochelle road east of highway 929. Significant street flooding occurred on many nearby streets.
Media reports high water on street in the French Quarter at Rampart Street.
Highway 127 was flooded and impassable.
Highway 127 was flooded.
The intersection of Highway 190 and Cow Creek Road was impassable due to mud and water. Flooding also damaged a water main, cutting off water service to nearby homes.
State Line Road was flooded east of Death Valley Junction.
Water one to two feet deep flowed over the intersection of Highway 190 and Beatty Road.

A water rescue took place at the intersection of US Route 202 and North Valley Road in Tredyffrin Township. Another water rescue took place at the intersection of Old Eagle School Road and Wallace Drive. A third water rescue took place at the intersection of Duportail Road and Mill Road in Tredyffrin Township.

Heavy rain across eastern Quay County resulted in flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 469. Local law enforcement reported that the roadway became impassable and the road was closed. There are no known impacts.
Public reports received of water covering North Border Avenue near Weslaco High School.
Local emergency managers reported standing water at the Intersection of Wilson Road and Frontage Road in Harlingen.

An official with the local Council of Government reported several feet of water on property next to her house, with over six inches of water inside her home north of La Joya. Total event rainfall exceeded 10 inches in this area over the course of several hours; additional flooding was also experienced in the area.
There were several reports of roads flooded or washed out in the town of Schodack.

Several roads were closed or washed out due to flooding in the eastern portion of Sand Lake, including Holcomb Road, North Nassau Road, and Burden Lake Road. A parking lot was washed out at a restaurant on Crooked Lake.

Flooding with reports of road closures and damage was reported across Richmond, Sullivan and Rutland Townships and in Mansfield Borough. No water rescues were reported. PA-549 was closed near Scouten Road. Sherman and North Academy Streets in Mansfield was closed.
County Road MM was reported underwater where it intersects the Sheboygan River. Nearby on MM closer to highway J, two vehicles stuck in flood waters in the ditch.
Spotter posted social media report via Twitter of a stranded vehicle under water and roadway flooded along Circle Street in the Cayce, SC community.
Public report of nearly impassable roadway due to flooding at 12th Street and Old Wire Road.
Idaho Transportation Department reported multiple mudslides and rock falls along US 93 between Evans and McKim Creek roads.
Several inches of mud, rocks and debris moved across Baker Creek road that closed the road. The cause was heavy rain over a burn scar area.
Idaho Transportation Department reported a mudslide and running water across Idaho Route 75 between East Fork Rd and Malm Gulch Rd completely blocking the highway.
Heavy rain from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in flash flooding along Highway 145 on the south side of Quitman.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Depression Ida resulted in flash flooding across Clay County, including in the city of West Point.
County Farm Road was washed out in the Town of Argyle due to flash flooding.
A culvert was plugged and caused flooding into a well on East Lake Road in the Town of Argyle.
Moore Road was closed in the Town of Argyle due to flash flooding.

A nearly stationary thunderstorm developed over the city of Tuscaloosa and produced rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches in a short period of time. Several locations along McFarland Blvd were under water and impassable.
The Iron County Emergency Manager reported flooding in Parowan. Floodwaters moved protective concrete barriers for the power plant and pushed them into the power plant building.

Video received showed deep and swift moving water flowing westward down Center Street and 700 E in Paragonah. Flows originated from Red Creek, which empties into Paragonah from the east. Radar estimated up to 2.15 inches of rain upstream over the Red Creek drainage.
A weather spotter reported water running down streets in Tropic.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 27 CFS to 493 CFS in 15 minutes, a rise of 1.5 feet.
A 100 foot stretch of Oliver road was flooded near the Harding Street exit of Interstate 70. Additional roads were closed due to water flowing over them across the downtown area.
Heavy rains washed out a section of State Road 32 in far eastern Fountain county along the border with Montgomery county.
Flooding of low-lying roads all over the county. Several roads were closed through the overnight hours.
Water was noted to be flowing over several city roads in Frankfort with other reports of rural roads with deep standing water.
A vehicle was stuck in rising water on Station Street.
McLaughlin Run came out of its banks, causing four homes to be evacuated on Baldwin Street and McLaughlin Run Road.

An estimated quarter of one inch of rain in under one hour on the Luna burn scar resulted in flash flooding in the area and areas downstream. This resulted in building damage along Luna Creek in Luna Canyon. The number of buildings damaged and to what extent is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.

Several roads were closed across the northeast part of Franklin County due to flash flooding, including Liberty Pike and Whitcomb Road, Kunkel Road north of Whitcomb Road and Farm Hill Road between Mud Road and Liberty Pike. An old bridge from the early 1900s was washed out.
Water was flowing across a roadway and carrying debris. A few roads washout were also reported across central Franklin County.
Water is 9 inches high and moving into a home. Vehicles reported stalled.
Two vehicles stranded. Water continues to rise.
Roads were flooded all around the Belden area.
Severe flooding on the Vestal Parkway. Vehicles trapped in rushing water.
Numerous homes were flooded in the Van Zyverden area.
A storm produced 5 inches of rain along Coal Creek, followed by flash flooding.
Portions of State Route 725 were impassable due to more than one foot of water running over the roadway. High water was also reported on Sugar Valley Drive and near Dillman Road.
Flooding reported by local 911 Call Center; flooding on Turner Valley Road.
Flooding in commercial building.
Washington Blvd was closed due to flooding; vehicle was underwater.
A few flooded roadways in Arnold and New Kensington, this includes North Street and Constitution Blvd.

Heavy rain led to the rapid rise of the Rio Felix near Hagerman with the gauge on Wiggins Lane measuring a maximum crest of 11.4 feet. The Chaves County emergency manager reported significant flash flooding across all low water crossings near the Rio Felix. Rapidly flowing water resulted in damage to a bridge on Morgan Road. The flash flooding also forced the closure of several Hagerman roads, including Cherokee Road, Lincoln Avenue, and Shoshoni Road. Damages are estimated for the structural damage to the bridge as well as an unknown amount of damage to nearby homes and businesses along the Rio Felix.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on several drainages in the Park.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding on US-23 near Valley Hills Road and Industrial Avenue, resulting in its closure. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of Swift Street between Industrial Drive and Whitesville Street due to high water from Oseligee Creek. Radar estimates indicate that |3 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Hamilton Road was closed at Old Chipley Road and Hagler Road due to flash flooding. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

After several hours of steady rainfall through the day on the 17th, a band of heavy rain passing across the Town of Boone produced between 1.8 and 2.6 inches of rain in less than an 1-hour period, falling at rates of 4 to locally 6 inches per hour at times. Runoff from this rain caused rapid rises along Winkler Creek and Hodges Creek, with quickly overflowed their banks and flooded over 3 feet deep in spots across the Boone Mall shopping complex. No injuries were reported, however several cars were observed flooded, a few of which had water up to the windows.

Heavy rain resulted in significant flash flooding near Apache Creek. The fast moving flood waters rushed through at least one home and overtopped an earthen dam. A metal tank was swept downstream, and a truck in the Apache Creek was submerged in the water. Damages are estimated.
Several roads and highways had running water in and around Bethany.
Flooding occurred on the Vestal Parkway. Water flowing across the road with parking lots taking on deep water.
Multiple underpasses were flooded in La Junta.
A few to several inches of water accumulating and flowing in areas surrounding the National Weather Service Pueblo Forecast Office building. This included sidewalks, parking lot, and yard.
Several streets in Winona were flooded. A portion of Scotland Shortcut Road south of town was washed out.

The public reported water flowing over the roadway near Mount Berry Square Mall and Armuchee Connector. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Willie Robinson Road washed out due to high flow on Latham Creek. Radar estimates indicate 2 to 3 inches of rain quickly fell on already wet soils from rain that occurred in the preceding few days. This quickly accumulating rainfall resulted in the flash flooding.

A state official reported a road closure due to flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 53 and Calhoun Avenue. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.
Highway 304 at Chalk Cliffs was washed out.
Flooding along County Road 28 south of Parkdale.
Road closed due to flooding. Other intersections Abriendo and Lake, Santa Fe and Mesa also flowing with 6-7 inches of water.

A slow-moving thunderstorm produced a radar-estimated 3.5 inches or rain during a 90-minute period along Beaverdam Road, which fell at rates as high as 5 inches per hour at times. This would be roughly a 100-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. Runoff from this heavy rain, possibly combined with a poor drainage issue, caused one lane of Beaverdam Road to buckle. Numerous stones at least six inches in diameter were also washed across Beaverdam Road and Moody Boulevard.

An estimated two inches of rain fell within an hour from a slow-moving thunderstorm across the Dry Creek drainage basin, between a 10- and 25-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. The rain was estimated to be falling at rates of three to four inches per hour per KFCX Doppler radar, and caused Dry Creek to overflow its banks and flow across Camp Road several inches deep. No damage to the road was reported.
Water was rushing over Harry L. Drive.
Three vehicles were reported to be stuck in flowing water above the wheels.
Several cars were reported to be stranded in water.
A few rounds of heavy rain caused flash flooding across numerous roads in various parts of Covington County. A video showed water flowing across a portion of McDonald Chapel Road south of Collins.

A stream gauge on Granite Creek (northeast of downtown Prescott--GRCA3) reported a 6.7 foot rise with a peak flow of 3,558 CFS. At least five roads were closed in Prescott due to flooding between 2:50 and 3:50 PM. Several roads were also closed in Wilhoit due to flooding. Two cars were stuck in flowing washes near Chino Valley/Paulden. Water was beginning to move the vehicles so Law Enforcement was called to the scene.
County Road 32 in Hollywood had 4 to 6 inches of slowing water reported covering the roadway.
College Road is under at least 6 inches of moving water in several locations.
Bridge on Nix Ridge Road is under 2 feet of water.
Route 66 and Greensburg Road was flooded due to high flow from Poke Run.

Multiple areas flooded in the Finleyville/Library area. A water rescue was due near Lobb's Run Road. Trax Farms in Finleyville had some flooded. Basements flooded in Peters/Union township. Piney Fork Road closed and flood at Greenman's Tunnel. Floodwaters closed Railroad Street and Airport Road as creeks spilled their banks.
Street flooding has been reported in the city of Brookville.

Trained spotters near Chacon reported 30 to 45 minutes of heavy rain across the Luna burn scar resulted in significant flash flooding in the area as well as three to twelve inches of mud and debris. The rapidly moving water also displaced boulders that blocked a residential driveway. Damages are a rough estimate.

Multiple sources reported flooding around Eldorado as an intense thunderstorm produced rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour. A CoCoRaHS observer in Eldorado reported 2.03 inches of rain with 1.1 inches of that falling in just 45 minutes. The heavy rainfall flooded arroyos around Eldorado. A couple residents also reported that their yards had been flooded while another resident reported that the flood waters entered their garage. Damages are estimated for the flooded garage.

Doraville Police reported the exit ramps Buford Highway to and from I-285 shut down due to high water. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager and several media outlets reported flash flooding in the Cleveland area, including but not limited to Campbell Street, Thomas Road at Georgia 115 West, South Main Street, Quillian Street, Cooley Woods at Mountain Meadows, and Ricky West at Mossy Acres. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 8 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager and several Media relayed reports of flash flooding in the city of Helen. Widespread flooding of Edelweiss Strasse and Bruken Strasse occurred due to high water on the Chattahoochee River. Water inundated the patio of a restaurant and caused damage to a bridge by the Chamber of Commerce. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 8 inches of rain occurred over the area during the storm.

Widespread flooding was reported across La Union due to over 7 inches of rain over the previous 3 days from just north of Domenici Highway through La Union. The Dona Ana County Emergency Manager ordered evacuations of La Union due to the flooding and possible dam breach of an earthen dam to the west of town.

Highway 70 was closed due to water running across the road at mile marker 174 as well as across the White Sands Missile Range Headquarters Road. The center median eroded due to the running water. A spotter reported 4.67 inches of rain in the 24 hour period ending at 6pm on 8/14.
Heavy rain southwest of Conchas resulted in flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 104. No damages were known.

Strong thunderstorms near Encinoso produced an estimated 1.5 to 2 inches of rainfall. This resulted in severe flooding along New Mexico State Road 246 which forced the closure of the roadway from mile marker 18 to mile marker 36. Damages are estimated for the washed out roadway.
Route 220 was flooded and possibly washed away.

Heavy rain in Belen resulted in significant flash flooding across the town. Over two inches of rain breached the Belen Highline Canal which caused flooding along Main Street. An unknown amount of homes and businesses were damaged from the water. The New Mexico Governor signed an executive order declaring a State of Emergency in Valencia County due to the flooding. Damages are estimated.
A tree was reported to be blocking a culvert causing the road to flood.
Streets were flooded, and vehicles were stranded.
Flooding reported at the intersection of Church and 6th Avenue in Decatur.
Flooding reported at the intersection of Woodall Road and Highway 20.
Debris and mudflow were noted into Middle Creek and along county roads 440 and 442.
A culvert washout with road damage was reported on Leigh Street.
A vehicle was stranded in floodwaters in Tupelo.
Railroad tracks have been washed out in addition to several bridges with water over them. Most area roads have at least 6 inches of water over them throughout Phil Campbell.
Part of College Street has been washed away.
Multiple areas flooded in Greensburg, roads included: Cemetery road and Hwy 119, Mt. Pleasant Road and Pellis Road, and Slate Run Road.
Reports of homes and businesses flooded.
Water was several inches deep and completely covering 13th Street South in Northwood.

A thunderstorm producing rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 14 in the Cedar Crest area southward into Pinon Ridge. A trained spotter in Cedar Crest also reported that arroyos in the area were full and storm drains were becoming overwhelmed. Extent of damages is unknown.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge rose 3.3 feet, with an increase in flow from 4 CFS to 1790 CFS.
Flash flooding carried debris across Old U.S. Highway 91 through Kanarraville.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a peak flow of 865 CFS.
The North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale spiked from 26 CFS to 1560 CFS in just 15 minutes, corresponding to a rise of 4 feet.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Grand Wash, Capitol Gorge, and Pleasant Creek were all closed due to flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager and several media outlets reported flash flooding over several roads in Sautee Nacoochee, including, but not limited to, Mauldin Road at Asbestos Road, Bean Creek at Gold Valley Road, Asbestos Road and Chastain Road. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Broadcast Media reported significant flooding along I-85 near Jimmy Carter Boulevard. Parts of the interstate were shut down due to high water over the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 2.5 inches quickly fell over the area, causing the flash flooding.
The Rio Penasco River came out of it's banks from just east of Mayhill into Chaves County with widespread flooding across the area.
High water observed on North Peters Road in Knoxville.
Vehicles stalled in high water on Middlebrook Pike in Knoxville.
Two people were rescued from a car stalled on a flooded roadway.

Wolf Creek overflowed its banks in several areas causing widespread flooding to the area. Creek debris, tree debris, mud and silt were deposited into the large drainage pipe and surrounding catch basins, as well as the roads. Washouts occurred along several portions of Fuller Road. The pavement from the intersection of Fuller down Grant was destroyed. Homes were flooded and evacuations took place.
Roads were reported to be flooded and washed out.
Trained spotter reports water over the intersection of Woodlawn and 2nd Street at least 6 inches deep. Report via social media.
Streets were flooded and vehicles stranded.
Highway 12 was closed at Big Branch Creek for water and debris over the road.
Streets were flooded and vehicles were stranded.
Flash flooding occurred over Highway 12, with the road closed.
A bridge on Beech Ridge Road was damaged by flash flooding.

Runoff from several inches of rain caused Sycamore Creek to rise out of its banks and flow across Sycamore Creek Road near the intersection of Woodlawn Church Road. At around 9:40 pm EST, the rainfall triggered at least one debris flow nearby. The flooding left large amounts of debris along the bridge crossing the creek and across the roadway. Structural damage to the road was also observed and required repair.

Thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in southeast Phillips County. Local law enforcement reported several roads were flooded southeast of Holyoke. Rainfall measurements from 4 to 9 inches were reported. Several houses had water rise up to the front doors. Significant flash flooding was observed 6 miles east of Holyoke on U.S. Highway 6. Widespread flooding of roads, ditches, and fields was reported. At least one road crossing Frenchman Creek was impassable. Frenchman Creek and other streams had significant flooding as well.

Law enforcement reported that water was flowing over County Road 84 and Reservation Road 101 around Pojoaque which forced the closure of the roadways. Water was also reported to be flowing across New Mexico State Road 503 in Nambe, but it was not closed. No damages are known.
Off duty National Weather Service Employee reports multiple cars stranded in flood waters near Pueblo Riverwalk and Santa Fe Avenue.
Off duty National Weather Service meteorologist reports underpass flooded and impassable at the entrance to Pueblo Memorial Airport.
Off duty National Weather Service meteorologist reports substantial underpass flooding along U.S. Highway 50 south of Pueblo Memorial Airport.
Flooding along U.S. Highway 50 between Colorado Highway 47 and areas south of Pueblo Depot. Reported by Colorado Department of Transportation.

Law enforcement reports multiple areas of significant flash flooding in the vicinity of the intersection of U.S. Highway 50 and Colorado Highway 47. This includes 4 feet of standing water and roads washed out.
Water was several inches deep flowing over Yarrow Avenue near the intersection of 410th Street.

Water two to three feet deep flowing up to the road on south end of town as well as approaching a residence. Three to six inches of water flowing over road. Report via social media courtesy of KAAL TV.
Water several inches deep flowing over the road near the intersection of Ulmus Avenue and 410th Street east of Kensett.

Four people died due to flooding at the Oakwood Plaza apartment complex on Irvington Avenue in Elizabeth. All four people were found in one apartment and included a 74 year old woman, her 71 year old husband, their 38 year old son, and a 33 year old neighbor.
Big Cottonwood Canyon Road was closed due to flash flooding carrying debris and rocks across the roadway.
UDOT reported two flash floods the Trail Mountain Fire burn scar flowed across state Route 31 between milepost 40 and milepost 44.
Photos from broadcast media indicated water and mud over a roadway in Kanab.

Flash flooding was reported on Coal Creek. The Coal Creek near Cedar City gauge rose from 8 CFS to 1160 CFS overnight. Several homes within the Flying L Ranches subdivision outside of Cedar City were damaged by floodwaters.

Flash flooding produced significant trail damage in Bryce Canyon National Park. Park officials reported the Wall Street section of Navajo Loop, the Bryce Connector Trail, and Peekaboo Loop were closed were closed due to the damage.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out and impassible due to flash flooding south of Sandy Ranch at Dog Water Wash.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Burr Trail, Strike Valley, and Halls Creek Road were all impassible due to flash flooding.
Several roads were closed due to high water or fast moving water in the Stoney Creek area northeast of Elizabethton.
Video depicted fast moving water on a homeowners property on Grindstaff Hollow Road near Sadie.
Social media image showed a residential backyard completely covered in water.
Flash flooding was reported along Highway 111 near Van Smith Road.
Several streets were reported flooded near Dudley.
The sewage treatment plant in Polo was flooded.
Standing water was reported up to the bumpers of cars in Jamaica.
Water was flowing across several roads in the Garrison area.
Several roads reported to be flooded in the area.
Several roads were flooded.
Road 421 was overtopped for hundreds of yards.
Water overtopped County road 442.
Several roads near the Conway community were flooded, with one home almost flooded in the area.
Several roads in and near Durant were flooded and inaccessible, and floodwaters neared several homes in town.
A few roads in Lexington were flooded. Many of the vehicles at a car lot in town were submerged, and its office building was flooded.
Standing water was reported up to the bumpers of cars in Flushing.
NY 303 was closed due to flooding between Spruce Street and Orangeburg Road in Orangeburg.
Water rescue with water coming into vehicle.
Ellwood Avenue was closed near North Hamilton Street due to flash flooding.
Monument Avenue near Kent Road was closed due to flash flooding.
Road was closed due to flash flooding.
Two swift water rescues were reported along the 4000 Block of West Broad Street.
High water was reported on Hull Street Road near Bellson Park Drive.
Spotter reported fast moving water on Pemberton Road near Interstate 64.
High water was reported at the intersection of East River Road and Dupuy Avenue.
High water was reported along Whitehead Road.
Law enforcement indicates that flash flooding continues across eastern parts of the Pueblo area, though not as significant as earlier in the night.
Flash flooding was reported on the Bountiful Bench, with water flowing through a home.
A dike collapse due to heavy rainfall led to a large amount of debris across Old U.S. Highway 91, with the road being closed.
Zion National Park officials reported the Kolob Canyons section of the Park was closed due to significant mud and rock slides from overnight flash flooding.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding of the East Fork of the Virgin River. The flood wave started near the East Fork of the Virgin River near Glendale, which rose from 16 CFS to 544 CFS, corresponding to a 3 foot rise. The flood wave grew downstream from additional heavy rain, where the East Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale rose from 45 CFS to 2410 CFS, corresponding to a 6 foot rise.
The Escalante River near Escalante gauge indicated an increase in flow of 1440 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 5 feet.

Heavy rain near Capitan in Lincoln County resulted in the rapid rise of the Magado Creek near the Capitan Fairgrounds. The Magado Creek rose an estimated ten feet which caused the flooding of a low water crossing in the area and temporarily trapping two unoccupied vehicles. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Damages are estimated for the damage to the two vehicles.

Radar estimates and local mesonet/CoCoRaHS stations confirmed a corridor of rainfall amounts from 4 to over 7 inches across this Flash Flood Warning area. The highest measured rainfall amount was 7.13 inches, recorded by a mesonet station located six miles east-southeast of Oxford, with most of this rain falling between 8-11 p.m. CDT. A resident located six miles north-northwest of Orleans reported that School Creek flooded and covered at least one gravel road during the early morning hours...with water getting within 50 feet of his home. The initially-issued Flash Flood Warning was replaced by an Areal Flood Warning that lasted several more hours, as water gradually receded through the morning.
Several roads were underwater in and around Harrisonville, namely Highway 291 near Home Farm Road and 283rd Road near Kauffman Road.
Trained spotter reported 6 to 8 inches of moving water across the intersection of Highway 31 and Lacon Road.
A construction crane along I-29 near Amazonia started tipping over due to erosion from rapid running water on a nearby creek.
Water rescues occurred at Highway 136 and Highway 65 in Princeton.
Water was rushing down Reynolds Road and Harry L. Drive.
Several roads flooded in the area, including Mount Upton and South New Berlin. State Route 8 inundated in several places.
A road was flooded and covered with mud and debris.
Numerous roads were reported as washed out in the area, including State Route 8.
A bridge was flooded. Hay bales were blocking the creek underpass. The local fire department was flooded out.
Route 54 was severely flooded.
Three to five inches of rain resulted in flash flooding across much of western Lewis County. Numerous culverts and roads were washed out or damaged due to the flowing water.

Significant flooding occurred across the county, with numerous streets and roads flooded. Multiple roads were washed out as well. Subsequent erosion to the banks along Big Sand Creek and Beasley Creek caused trees to fall into the creek beds. Seven homes and two businesses were impacted by floodwaters. The dam at Gee Lake failed after the lake became overfilled from runoff floodwaters, causing downstream flooding in Leflore County. Over eight inches of rain fell at the Greenwood Leflore Regional Airport.

US Highway 49 from north of Ruleville to north of Drew was closed in both directions due to flooding. Over 50 public roads in Drew and surrounding areas were flooded, some of which had to be closed. Fields in northern portions of the county were also flooded. Many homes were threatened by rising floodwaters, but only 13 were impacted by flooding. Vehicles parked at a car repair shop were flooded.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in the flooding of several streets across the city of Meridian.
There was bridge flooding south of Greene.
Tracy Creek is flooding near Tracy Creek Rd, and Richtmeyer Rd.
Flash flooding over several roads is occurring in the towns of Fenton, Colesville and Chenango.
Widespread flash flooding occurring in the Morningside Drive neighborhood. Several water rescues underway. Considerable damage reported to streets and storm drain infrastructure.

The Catron County emergency manager reported that heavy rain in Old Horse Springs resulted in flash flooding across the area. A local resident measured 3.5 inches of rain in just 45 minutes. This resulted in multiple barns and homes in the area flooded as well as the local fire department. The emergency manager also reported that several county roads had been washed away. Damages are estimated.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Scenic Drive was closed at Grand Wash due to a large amount of mud across the road, deposited by flash flooding, making it impassible. Rangers also estimated Pleasant Creek and Sheets Gulch had 6-8 feet of flooding overnight, and Burro, Cottonwood, and 5 mile Washes had 2 to 4 feet of flooding overnight.

Zion National Park dispatch officials reported a rockslide due to excessive rainfall along the Scenic Drive north of the Visitor Center. A portion of the road was damaged due to the slide, and was closed as a result. In addition, the river gauge on the North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale had a sharp rise and peaked at 1690 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 3 feet.
The Emergency Manager reported a pond dam failed, washing out Richard Pullen Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
Several roadways were flooded near Waterville and Cleveland.

The Passaic River at Dundee Dam in Clifton rose above its minor flood stage of 4.5 feet at 10:15pm EDT and crested at a height of 4.98 feet at 12:45am EDT September 2nd. The river then fell back below flood stage at 3:45am EDT on September 2nd. Flooding from the Passaic River resulted in three fatalities. A 70 year old man died when his car became stranded in 6 feet of water at the intersection of Passaic Avenue and Lackawana Place in Passaic.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced torrential rain and flash flooding across portions of western Grundy County. Vegetation was flattened near many creeks and channels due to the fast moving flood waters. Along Armstrong Run, water went over the Indian Trail Road bridge. Damage occurred to the bridge approaches and pavement was missing. A nearby shed was destroyed and a utility pole was toppled. Further northeast, the Kinsman Road bridge over Armstrong Run was also damaged. Significant damage occurred to vegetation including entire trees removed. Damage also occurred to the Dupont Road bridge over Armstrong Run where the approaches suffered significant scouring. Vegetation was flattened and a nearby fence was knocked over with evidence of 1 to 2 feet of flowing water. The Dupont Road bridge over Hog Run was damaged with the approaches washed out. Vegetation was flattened in many locations near Hog Run between Omalley and Grand Ridge Roads. Water rescues were performed during the peak of the flooding near Kinsman and Dupont Roads where at least three vehicles were stuck in flood waters. Rainfall of 6.19 inches was reported during a 3 hour period, four miles northwest of Verona. Rainfall of 4.58 inches was reported during a 4 hour period, three miles east of Seneca. The damage amount was estimated in consultation with local emergency management officials.
Report of water over I-68 Bridge near Cheat Lake.
Several roads were flooded in Sugar Creek Township. Engle Mill, Cornstalk, and Cook Roads all had washouts and were impassable.
Flash flooding was reported along Lower Hillside Drive.
Vehicles became stuck in rising water on Roxanna New Burlington Road.
A culvert was washed on on U.S. Route 62 near Northview Drive.

A strong thunderstorm produced an estimated 1 inch of heavy rainfall in a short period of time on the Ute Park burn scar. This resulted in rapid runoff with emergency personnel reporting a six foot wall of water that flowed through Ute Park with a three foot rise of water in Cimarron. This damaged many roads in the area and trapped numerous residents within their homes. No injuries or fatalities resulted from the flash flooding. Damages are estimated.

Doppler radar estimated that two to locally as much as four inches of rain from a series of thunderstorms fell across upper Moores Fork Creek basin (1.85 miles^2 per USGS Stream Stats), all within about a 2-hour period of time. For this duration, most locations within this area experienced between a 5- and a 10-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. If indeed four inches of rain fell, that would be around a 100-year rainfall event at the 2-hour duration. Runoff from this rainfall caused Moores Fork Creek to rise out of its banks, flooding several inches deep across Kitty Hawk Lane and potentially other locations. No damage was reported.
Flint Town Rd. is washed out. Flooding occurring in nearby home.
Homes are flooded and water rescues are underway.
One to three feet of water and mud over county road 162.
County roads 110 and 111 were washed out.
Extensive road damage was observed. A 7 foot wall of water developed due to a culvert plugging up. County roads 271, 261, and 265 all remained closed throughout the night.
An observer reported 3 feet of rocks, mud, and water flooded into a ranch basement and nearly moved a second home off its foundation near the Crawford Mountains.

Heavy rain over the Museum Fire scar (2019) produce significant flooding down Spruce Wash and into north central Flagstaff and down into the Rio de Flag on the south and southeast Flagstaff. The flood water first entered developed area around 1245 PM with trees, logs, and other debris 60-70 feet wide over topping a road about 2.5 - 3 feet deep. The flood waters were over 9 feet deep in some channeled areas through the forest. Many roads were flooded and closed. The flood barriers were overtopped in some places.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out at Bullfrog Creek Crossing near Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, resulting in a 5-foot drop-off, making the road impassible.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash, with 6 to 8 inches of rapidly flowing water.

The Emergency Manager reported water flowing over a portion of Fish Creek Road was up to the mailboxes. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported high water closed the roadway near the intersection of Judkin Mill Road and Johnson Lake Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a partial wash out of Morgan Valley Road at Hillside Drive due to flash flooding in the area. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported high water near Collard Valley Road and Fish Creek Road that submerged vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
Several streets flooded in Indianola.
Water flowed across Old Richburg Road.
Multiple cars were stuck in running water in Marshall.
Several roads across Saline County were overrun with running water.
MODOT reported that HWY 18 was closed due to flooding.
Several spots along HWY A and B east and west of Rich Hill were flooded due to heavy rain.

Multiple reports of flooded areas, including Pike Street and Howard Street. Fairmont Bowl Center had water inside, 2 to 3 inches deep. The rain was so heavy on Kirckway Drive, in Fairmont, that it caused Coal Run Creek to overflow. The water came over the barrier and caused a sink hole.
High water resulted in the closure of numerous roads across Warren County, including Columbia Road between U.S. Route 42 and Glosser Road.
Widespread flooding of streets and poor drainage areas within the Village of Hancock. A State of Emergency was declared.
Multiple roads were flooded in the county including several with washed out culverts.
Multiple roads were flooded in the county, including one that was washed out.

A few rounds of heavy rain across the county resulted in flooding across twenty-six roads scattered across the county, and four sinkholes developed in the city of Monticello. A church and a home in in New Hebron were flooded. The Lawrence County EMA in Monticello measured 6.25 inches of rain over the span of a few hours.
River Road and Route 46 are closed due to flash flooding.

Training thunderstorms dropped 2 to 3.5 inches of rain across the community of Blacksburg, with much of this rain falling within a 60-minute period. This caused flash flooding along Stroubles Creek, with rushing water at least a foot deep flowing across Duck Pond Drive and Plantation Road, causing both roads to be impassible. Smithfield Road and Oak Lane were also covered by flowing water. All roads were reopened after the flood waters receded.
Portions of Randolph Road was closed due to high water.
The fire department reported water deep enough that vehicles could not pass through on Mt Pleasant street and West Burlington Avenue.
Emergency management reported that Highway 61 in Burlington was impassable and 3 vehicles were stranded.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek and the Fremont River, along with muddy conditions on Scenic Drive. The initial flood wave through Sulphur Creek contained black boulders.
County dispatch reported Kingston Canyon was underwater with rock and debris over a portion of state Route 62.
A debris flow moved across a road in Timber Canyon.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in Enoch and Cedar City, with up to 300 homes damaged by flood waters. Water rescues were performed, and cars were swept off the road. Interstate 15 was closed during the event. Numerous roads were eroded by floodwaters, and Fiddlers Canyon was reported underwater.

Runoff from heavy rains caused flash flooding to occur near Melvina. A creek out of its banks sent water over both lanes of County Road J, a mud and rock slide covered a portion of County Road X and the Little La Crosse River went out its banks spreading water and debris across State Highway 27.

The Emergency Manager reported vehicles were trapped in floodwaters in the parking lot of the Polk County Medical Center. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a road washed out near the intersection of Culp Lake Road and Johnson Lake Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported a flooded roadway near Bellview Road and Anderson Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported a culvert washed out on David Price Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
The Paria River gauge at Lees Ferry showed a 4 foot rise between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM MST. The Paria River drainage originates in Utah and flows into the Colorado River near Lees Ferry.
The East Verde River near Childs (EVDA3) had a 2.9 foot rise between 0800 and 0845 MST.
The Tonto Creek stream gauge above Gun Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.1 foot rise between 0845 and 1000 AM MST.
The water was flowing 4.85 feet deep (normally dry) in Munds Canyon under Interstate 17 and about 25 feet wide. The estimated flow was 900 CFS.
Emerald Isle Public Works closed Reed Drive between East and West Sea View Drive due to high water.
Entrance to Wildwood neighborhood cover with up to 3 feet of water. Road not passable due to high water.

Strong thunderstorms that moved southwest through Socorro County brought heavy rain with reports of one to two inches. This resulted in widespread flooding across central Socorro County. The La Joya area was especially impacted with additional damage to the La Joya Acequia. A large section of the concrete ditch system north of La Joya was severely damaged, and several ditches and drains were filled with silt. All of the arroyos in the La Joya area flooded which washed away several of the arroyo banks and caused additional damage. The Rio Puerco River created to 17.75 feet Friday evening which was its highest level since 2013. Homes in the Contreras area were surrounded by flood water. Damages are estimated.
After several rounds of rain caused flash flooding water rescues were taking place in and around Amazonia.
Several roads were closed in the Idaho area due to high water. Rising water forced some evacuations from a few homes.
Several roads, along with a few houses were flooded between Ridgebury and Columbia Crossroads.
Roads were flooded in the area.
Road flooding was observed in several locations.
Water was surrounding homes near Gillett. Evacuation of residents was underway.
Northbound MS Highway 35 was flooded in several locations.
Floodwaters entered a home along MS Highway 14.
Roads were washed out in the Mauricio Canyon area.
Roads were washed out at County Road J and 40, east of Campo with approximately 3 feet of water.
Highway 160 was closed due to flash flooding and debris flows. Severe under cutting of the roadway.
County Road 80 was flooded near its intersection with County Road 19 and also near its intersection with County Road 78.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Masonville. Minor flooding was observed at the Masonville Post Office. There was a debris jam at the bridge. Black Creek Road in the Retreat was washed out in the storm. Both sides of the road were eroded by water flow making the it impassable. Big Bear Road was washed out from the paved road to the gate of nearby property. A recently installed culvert was washed out, and the road was impassable.

Training showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rain that flooded many roads in far northern Sunflower County. US Highway 49 was closed between Rome and Parchman, and at least one vehicle stalled on the flooded highway. A few homes flooded in Rome.

Training showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rain that flooded numerous roads and approximately 200 homes in and between the areas of Rosedale, Shelby, Mound Bayou, and Merigold. A neighborhood flooded in Rosedale, and several streets in town were flooded significantly. In Mound Bayou, some residents had to be evacuated from flooded homes. The COOP Observer 2 miles southwest of Shelby measured 11.96 inches of rain during a 6 to 7 hour period that morning.
A few of the roads in town were flooded.
Highway 51 in Coldwater was flooded with over 6 inches of water covering all four lanes.
Water was reported up to the top of a car tire on the corner of Nagle Avenue and Dyckman Street due to flooding in Washington Heights.

Flash flooding in Charlestown caused a road washouts, one on Route 12 between Almar St and Bowen Crossing. Another washout occurred on Scenic Hill Rd at Wheeler Rand Rd. The washouts were the result of overland runoff and not from any river or creek. At least six roads were closed in Charlestown, Pecor Road, Lamb Road, Meany Road, South Hemlock and Hackett Swamp. Nearby rain gages reported between 1.88-2.57 between 730 PM and midnight.
In Tooele, 37 homes were flooded. Additionally, multiple roads were closed due to flooding.

Runoff from locally heavy rains caused flash flooding to occur across the northern portions of Vernon County. Coon Creek went out of its banks causing extensive damage to the baseball field in Coon Valley. Water got into the basements of some homes as well.
The Emergency Manager reported a washed out roadway at JLG Road and Hutto Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose from 7.17 to 10.22 feet in 45 minutes.

Pictures on social media show at least 10 inches of water flowing in Dinnebito Wash near Hardrock. The water had been flowing for at least 2 hours. Road going into Hardrock were not passible due to the water flowing over the roadways.
Granite Creek (GRWA3) below Watson Lake rose 2.2 feet to 3.97 feet in one hour and 44 minutes. Water crested at 7:20 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge (BCMA3) near Montezuma Castle National Monument rose from 1.0 to 3.03 feet in 65 minutes. It crested at 11:13 PM MST.

Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in flash flooding in the city of Hattiesburg. Water covered the roadway at the intersection of Highway 49 and West Pine Street as well as at North 28th Avenue and Sims Road.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in flash flooding that washed out a culvert on Ora Williamson Road.
More than 3 feet of water along Back Road, near the Ocracoke Coffee Company. The road was impassable due to deep water. Videos were posted on social media.
Merrimon Road flooded just before Merrimon Church. Water was acrdoss the road in five places outside of Jonaquins subdivision.
Cape Point Campground was 100% flooded. Significant amounts of water on some areas near Cape Point.
Significant ponding of water along South Point Road.

Parts of Highway 12 flooded in the typical spots including Pea Island section of the seashore in what is called the Canal Zone. Flooding along the roads and roadside ditches in all the villages and in some locations between the villages. Staff described the roadway flooding as very dangerous.
Interstate 29 was closed between mile marker 84 and mile marker 92 due to water running over the road.
Portions of Highway J were overflowing with water.
Several streets around Lake Village were flooded.
Ten roads in the mainly downtown area of Grenada were flooded, and floodwaters entered a home along Shelby Chapel Road southwest of town.
Flooding in the 600 block of Main street in Lamar.

Flash flooding occurred across the southern sections of La Crosse due to runoff from locally heavy rains. A portion of County Road NN was washed out south of Saint Joseph, a mudslide occurred along State Highway 33 in Shelby and boulders were washed into the U.S. Highway 14/61 and State Highway 35 split on the south side of La Crosse.
The Verde River near Clarkdale rose over 17 feet in 58 minutes (VDCA3). The water crested at 19.49 feet at 942 PM MST.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose just over 10 feet in 4 hours (VAVA3). The water crested at 14.23 at 9:30 AM MST.
Emergency Management reported a 4 foot rise on Black Canyon Creek at 8:08 PM MST. This creek is downsteam from parts of the Tiger Fire (2021).
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida resulted in several instances of flash flooding on roadways in the city of Magee.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Ida caused a washout on Smith County Road 559.
Ocracoke Campground 75% under water.
About a foot of water was rapidly flowing across State Route 73.
Several roads and houses were flooded in the Mound Bayou area.
North Chester Avenue was flooded. Sylvia Street was flooded and some homes along this same road were flooded.
Three plush inches of water on county road 21 with damage to roads 2 and 6.
There were flooded streets.
Numerous roads were closed due to flooding in Jersey City.
Numerous roads were closed due to flooding in Kearny.
Severe local flooding was reported just north of the train station in the town of Kearny. Water rescues were performed on Schuyler Avenue to assist motorists trapped in flood waters.
Cars were reported stranded in flood waters in Jersey City.
All lanes were closed due to flooding on the US 1&9 truck route northbound at the New Jersey Turnpike in Newark.

Heavy rainfall across southern and central New Hampshire on August 1 caused flash flooding due to already saturated ground conditions from a record wet July. In West Unity, a weather observer measured at 2.57 between 730 PM and midnight. Rapid runoff caused several roads to sustain damage such as undermining of pavement to a complete washout. West Unity Road was the hardest hit with a large sinkhole estimated at 10 feet.
A vehicle was stuck in water on Washington Road near the Dairy Queen. Flooding along Saw Mill Run by the Parkway West ramp.
A trained spotter in Fence Lake reported that County Road 35D had been washed out due to heavy rain in the area. Damages are estimated.
Over a dozen motorists were rescued by the NYPD on the Major Deegan Expressway at W. 179th Street in Morris Heights due to flooding.
The southbound Hutchinson River Parkway was closed due to flooding at Exit 13 in White Plains.
Numerous roads across Dekalb County were submerged, with some water rescues in Clarksdale.
Significant flooding inundated the 157th Street subway station in Washington Heights.
High water reported on US19 at Bell Run.
Harlem River Drive was closed southbound in Washington Heights in the area of Exit 23 due to flooding.
The Whitestone Expressway was closed at 22nd Road in Flushing due to flooding.
The lobby of a building in Flushing was flooded with a few inches of flood water. The office on the ground floor was pumping out floodwater.
Roberts and Pierce Creek Roads were flooded and covered with debris. Roads were impassable.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced torrential rain and flash flooding across portions of eastern La Salle County including in Seneca. Vegetation was flattened near many creeks and channels due to the fast moving flood waters. Along Hog Run, vegetation was flattened near North 21st Road with debris near the road. Along North 2350th Road near Armstrong Run, flood waters flowed over the roadway with debris in the channel. North La Salle Road was flooded, just south of Dupont Road with debris piled on the side of the road along with erosion in the channel. There was substantial deposition of sediment from a nearby sand and gravel facility across Dupont Road near Deadly Run. A substantial stretch of Dupont Road was flooded with extensive mud marking on pavement, east of Route 170 near a marina. Just west of Route 170, the east abutment to the River Road bridge over a small creek was washed out. A local highway department staff member was driving over this area when the washout occurred. His truck became stuck on remaining pavement on either side of the washout. The driver needed to be rescued and refused medical treatment. Scouring occurred on both sides of the creek with vegetation collapsed or partially collapsed. Homes on Timmons Lane were flooded with one home suffering a basement wall collapse. During the evening of the 6th, a north to south low-level boundary set up along the Interstate 65 corridor that became the focus for back-building thunderstorms and heavy rainfall. Over the course of just a few hours, a wide swath of 6-10 inches of rain occurred. Numerous roads became submerged and impassable. Countless water rescues were performed as travelers either became trapped by or drove into flood waters. Flood water several feet deep impacted parts of neighborhoods and townhomes. Several businesses were damaged by flooding. Extreme runoff also caused creeks and other waterways to rapidly swell. A Flash Flood Watch had already been in place for a few days, highlighting the potential for flooding rainfall. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for Jefferson County, including the city of Birmingham, early in the evening. At least four rounds of thunderstorms occurred, with ongoing and forecast impacts pushing the event to the highest level of flash flooding, a Flash Flood Emergency. Scanner traffic became nonstop with public calls for help and first responder needs for mutual aid and resources. Even after the rain subsided later in the evening, flooding persisted for several more hours.

During the evening of the 6th, a north to south low-level boundary set up along the Interstate 65 corridor that became the focus for back-building thunderstorms and heavy rainfall. Over the course of just a few hours, a wide swath of 6-10 inches of rain occurred. Numerous roads became submerged and impassable. Countless water rescues were performed as travelers either became trapped by or drove into flood waters. Flood water several feet deep impacted parts of neighborhoods and townhomes. Several businesses were damaged by flooding. Extreme runoff also caused creeks and other waterways to rapidly swell. There was at least one report of a partial landslide in Pelham, sending dirt, rocks, and pine trees onto the road. A Flash Flood Watch had already been in place for a few days, highlighting the potential for flooding rainfall. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for north Shelby County early in the evening. At least four rounds of thunderstorms occurred, with ongoing and forecast impacts pushing the event to the highest level of flash flooding, a Flash Flood Emergency. Scanner traffic became nonstop with public calls for help and first responder needs for mutual aid and resources. Even after the rain subsided later in the evening hours,|flooding persisted for several more hours. Two deaths occurred when a vehicle was swept off the roadway and into a creek.

Stream gauges indicated significant flash flooding developed for the second day in a row near the upper reaches of the French Broad River after 3 to 6 inches of rain fell in the headwaters in just a few hours. This was on top of the 6-12 inches that fell durimg the morning of the 16th. Flooding was slightly worse in the Rosman and Balsam Grove area than what was observed on the 16th, with the stream gauge at Rosman reaching its second highest level on record (4 October 1964). Multiple structures along the river were once again inundated, including on Depot St, Highway 178, Main St, and Chestnut St in Rosman. Flash flooding again developed along the Davidson River in the Pisgah Forest area, overflowing portions of Davidson River Rd and Deavor Rd and inundating several businesses near the intersection of Highways 64 and 276.

An historic, devastating flash flood struck the city of Waverly along the Trace Creek river basin. A fast-moving flood wave traveling westward down Trace Creek caused flood waters to rise several feet in roughly a 10 minute timespan between 1000am to 1010am CDT, flooding hundreds of homes, businesses, and churches, some of which were washed off their foundations. News reports and information from the Tennessee Emergency Management Agency indicated a total of 523 homes were impacted by the flooding, with 272 totally destroyed, 168 with major damage, 31 with minor damage, and 20 affected. 44 businesses and 8 public facilities were also damaged, including the Waverly Elementary School and Waverly Junior High School which will have to be torn down are rebuilt in a different location. Dozens of cars were also washed away and deposited long distances downstream, and many of the roadway bridges than spanned Trace Creek were knocked off their pilings and heavily damaged. TEMA reported damage to roads and schools alone totaled $31,844,911, with an additional estimated $60-70 million in damage to homes and businesses. 19 people were killed in Waverly, along with 1 other who died in Hurricane Mills, making this the deadliest flash flood in Middle Tennessee history.

Stream gauges indicated and an NWS flood survey confirmed significant flash flooding developed near the upper reaches of the French Broad River after as much as a foot of rain fell in the headwaters in less than six hours. Multiple structures along the river were inundated in the town of Rosman, including on Depot St, Highway 178, Main St, and Chestnut St. This was the worst flooding along this portion of the French Broad in almost 30 years, while the stream gauge at Rosman registered its 4th-highest level on record. (Continuous observations at that site date back to 1935). Newspaper reported significant flash flooding also occurred upstream of Rosman along the North Fork of the French Broad in the Balsam Grove community, where vehicles were swept downstream and multiple structures were damaged or destroyed. In addition, flash flooding developed along the Davidson River in Pisgah Forest, briefly inundating portions of Davidson River Rd and Deavor Rd.

Emergency management and stream gauges reported catastrophic flash flooding developed within the Pigeon River watershed after 6 to 8 inches of rain fell in just a few hours across the northern slopes of the Balsams. This was on top of 5 to 10 inches that fell over the Shining Rock Wilderness during the morning of the 16th, resulting in 36-hour totals of more than a foot. Flash flooding initially developed along the West Fork and especially the East Fork of the Pigeon River. Water from the latter stream, swept downstream through the Cruso community causing widespread damage. Six people were killed in Cruso, four of them in a campground along the East Fork, where numerous recreational vehicles and automobiles were swept away. Water from the two forks of the river rushed downstream to the main channel of the Pigeon, causing major flooding along the stream in Canton and Clyde for the first time since Tropical Cyclone Ivan in September 2004. Numerous buildings in downtown Canton were inundated. In total, around 700 homes were impacted by flooding, with a couple of hundred of those destroyed. Numerous vehicles were also swept away or otherwise damaged and hundreds of people were rescued. Dozens of roads were flooded, with many roads and bridges damaged or destroyed.

Several roads were flooded in the Capitol View, Music Row, and Midtown areas of Nashville including West End Avenue, Chet Atkins Place, 10th Avenue North, Nelson Merry Street, and Exit 1 on I-440 West. Streets were also flooded across the Vanderbilt University campus, including 24th Avenue South and 25th Avenue South outside the parking garage.

Stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along the Swannanoa River after 6 to 10 inches of rain fell within the headwaters in around 24 hours, with much of that falling in just a few hours during the afternoon of the 17th. In Black Mountain, significant flooding of Veterans Park and some roads surrounding the park was observed. Flooding developed downstream to Biltmore Village in Asheville, where multiple roads and the first floors of some buildings were inundated. The rise of the Swannanoa contributed to rapid rises on the French Broad River downstream of the confluence of the two streams, with multiple roads inundated on the west side of downtown. Flooding actually worsened in the Biltmore Village area after heavy rainfall and flash flooding ended.

A couple of stream gauges along Little Sugar Creek in Uptown Charlotte exceeded their established flood stages after a couple of inches of rain fell in around an hour. Cullman Ave was overtopped as was the Freedom Park greenway and parking lots at the Carolinas Medical Center. The intersection of North Tryon Street and Atando Ave was also inundated by a tributary of Derita Creek. Additionally, media reported W Morehead St becoming impassable due to flooding along Irwin Creek.

Flooded roads throughout the Beulah area. Multiple residents were having a hard time accessing their driveways, especially in low lying areas.
Numerous reports of flooding in Trinidad with several county roads washed out or partially washed out. Purgatoire river went out of its banks along Highway 12 west of Trinidad.
Flowing water up to the curb, at Troy and Highway 47.
Flooding of fields, and road side ditches.
High water flowing across State Highway 109, with car stranded.

Following 2 to 4 inches of rain in 1 to 2 hours over the Sand Tank Wash watershed, catastrophic flooding occurred in the small town of Gila Bend with feet of water, mud, and debris moving through town. Storm surveys were completed by NWS Phoenix, Maricopa County Department of Emergency Management (MCDEM), American Red Cross, and Flood Control District of Maricopa County (FCDMC). FCDMC gages on Sand Tank Wash, Bender Wash, and in the Maricopa Mountains measured rainfall amounts around 3 to 4 inches in 1 to 2 hours for an annual exceedance probability of 0.1%. FCDMC found the most significant floodwaters were within Sand Tank Wash, with lesser flows in Bender and Scott Avenue Washes. The NWS Phoenix survey found evidence of out of bank flooding in Sand Tank Wash 1 to 3 miles south of Interstate-8 (I-8) with 2 to 6 feet of water and sizable debris. The streamflow gage on Sand Tank Wash at I-8 reached alarm stage at 0157MST, bank full at 0341MST, and flood stage at 0352MST. The gage crested at 7.69 feet with 5000 cfs of flow at 0408MST. The floodwaters and debris that moved through town caused flood damage to at least 140 homes and 25 businesses. Most structures impacted were between the Gila Bend Canal and Main Street and then along Pima Street. During the flooding, Maricopa County Sheriff's Office rescued at least 30 individuals from their roofs along with others pulled from stranded vehicles. Photos after the water receded showed the canal was eroded and breached where Sand Tank Wash flows over it. Photos also showed 2 to 5 foot water lines both on the outside and inside of many of the structures, piles of debris, damaged property and vehicles, and erosion. Of the homes MCDEM assessed, 21 were deemed uninhabitable after the flooding. Unfortunately there were 2 direct fatalities with this event. One made a heroic effort to save a stranded motorist before they themselves were swept away in their own vehicle. The other was swept away in one of the flooded washes. Additionally, many farm animals were killed. Besides the fatalities, no other injuries were reported. A state of emergency was declared for this event.
Flooding along Main street, in Canon City.
A culvert was washed out from the heavy rainfall.

Severe flash, and rapid onset river flooding destroyed many parts of the Village of Cameron, including residences, businesses and infrastructure.

Severe flash, and rapid onset river flooding destroyed many parts of the Town of Woodhull, including residences, businesses and infrastructure.

Heavy rain of 2 to 2.5 fell in less than 2 hours between the Pinaleno Mountains and Highway 70 west of Safford. This caused flash flooding of roads in the Pima area and significant rises in Cottonwood Wash. A large SUV which was attempting to cross the wash and carrying two adults and four children was swept away in the floodwaters. A four-year old girl drown during the rescue attempt. Her body was found four days later downstream in the Gila River near Eden.

Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2.5 fell in less than 1 hour in the Douglas area causing flash flooding of streets and caused the closure of Washington Ave where several homes were flooded and a block wall was knocked down by flood waters. West of town, Kings Highway just north of State Route 80 was closed due to flooding.

One to two inches of rain fell in less than 1 hour northeast of the Tucson International Airport causing flash flooding of area roads. One swift water rescue was conducted for a vehicle stalled in a wash.

A Tonto National Forest service member shared photos from a forest service road near Pinal Peak showing evidence of a flash flood with debris across the road, including boulders/rocks and tree branches strewn across the road. In coordination with the WFO Phoenix Senior Service Hydrologist, it would have taken at least 6 inches of flowing water to move the debris in the photos. There were no reports of damage or injuries.

Heavy rain of 2.5 in less than 90 minutes occurred near the headwaters of Rincon Creek. Flash flooding occurred downstream in the Rincon Ranch Estates area. Camino Loma Alta became flooded and impassible.

Around 2.5 of rain in less than 1 hour was measured near the headwaters of Sabino Creek in the Bighorn burn scar and caused a two-foot rise in the stream that crosses trails in the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area. Six hikers had to be rescued after becoming trapped by the high flows.

One inch of rain in less than 90 minutes caused rapid rises in Josephine Canyon. Two teenagers swimming near a waterfall were swept downstream by a rapid rise in the water level. One teenager drowned and another escaped the floodwaters while sustaining minor injuries and was later rescued.
Two USGS river gauges on Granite Creek measured a 4 foot rise due to heavy rain fall in the area.
The Verde River in Camp Verde had a 5.6 foot rise on the river gauge at 445 PM MST.

A thunderstorm with heavy rain produced runoff 4 feet deep near Ryal Trail at Salt Mine Road. This caused the collapse of a dirt berm on the east side of Salt Mine Road when the drainage pipe was overwhelmed.

The Thunderbird Road underpass at Interstate-17 became impassable with 2 to 3 feet of standing water after over 1 inch of rain fell in roughly one hour. One vehicle stalled in the flood water and had to be towed out. The road was eventually closed. No injuries reported.

Officials with Joshua Tree National Park reported several inches of swiftly moving water flowing over Indian Cove Road, making the road impassable. Timing was estimated using radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 2.5 in less than 1 hour at the headwaters of Tanque Verde Creek caused a 1 foot rise in water levels at Tanque Verde Loop Road, resulting in its closure.
An SUV stalled out in the underpass at Marconi Drive due to high water.
A member of the public reported roads to be impassable due to water 1 foot deep flowing over roadways.
A member of the public reported several roads to be impassible due to high water.
A member of the public reported flood waters covering the road and encroaching on homes.

Between 1 and 1.5 of rain fell in less than 1 hour in central Tucson causing widespread street flooding with water flowing across roads 1 to 2 feet deep. Swift water rescues occurred near the intersections of Grant and Tucson and Silverlake and Euclid with vehicles stranded at Mabel and 7th Ave. and the Orange Grove/I-10 underpass. A house was flooded near Speedway and Country Club.

Between 1 and 1.5 of rain fell in less than 1 hour south and west of the Tucson Mountains to near Three Points causing widespread street flooding and street closures due to water flowing across roads 1 to 2 feet deep. A vehicle was stranded in flood waters at the intersection of Snyder Hill and Sandario. Several dirt roads were washed out in the Three Points area.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour in the Sunsites area caused flash flooding and the closure of Birch Rd. near Highway 191.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour south of San Simon caused flash flooding of roadways and resulted in the closing of Coyote Song Rd.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour north of Willcox caused flash flooding of roadways and the closure of Hardy Rd.

A large area of 1 to 2 of rain fell in less than 90 minutes in southeast Pima County and caused extensive flash flooding from southeast Tucson and Vail southwest to Sahuarita and Green Valley. In the Vail area, three to four feet of water washed out East Andrada Rd at the Santa Rita Wash and a car was swept downstream 300 yards, but the occupants escaped unharmed. Many roads in Saguaro National Park East were also flooded or closed. In southeast Tucson, a person was rescued from a sandbar in the Pantano Wash near Harrison Rd. and farther south, Sahuarita and Wilmot Rds. were closed. In Sahuarita a woman was rescued from her vehicle at Beta Street and the Interstate 19 Frontage Rd. In Green Valley, several roads were closed and homes were flooded in the Casa de Abrego neighborhood east of I-19.
Two to four inches of rain in two hours fell over the higher terrain north of Safford and Pima. Flash flooding caused multiple road washouts of Safford-Bryce and Bryce-Eden Rds.
One hour rainfall of 0.5 to 1 on ground saturated from rain the previous day caused flash flooding northeast of Ryan Field and the closure of Snyder Hill Rd west of San Joaquin Rd.
Two inches of rain in 2 hours north of Three Points caused flooding of roadways west of Picture Rocks. A vehicle was stranded in floodwaters on Tucker Road at the Blanco Wash.
Heavy rain dislodged rocks that fell on Highway 89 between Flagstaff and Sedona (switchbacks near FR-237).
Heavy rain caused the Verde River to rise 2 feet (near the junction of the Verde River and Sycamore Creek).

A vehicle was caught in the flood waters of Dinnebito Wash near Route 6720 and Saltwater Wash. There was one fatality and two others trapped in the water. This was located about 72 air miles downstream from the headwaters of this wash.
Heavy rain over the Paria River drainage (in Arizona and Utah) caused the river gauge at Lees Ferry to rise 2.5 feet.
Major portions of the Twin Arrows Casino were flooded. Flood debris went all over their roads.

The USGS stream gage along Pinal Creek at Inspiration Dam near Globe measured an approximate rise of 4.25 feet in a 15 minute period. The gage recorded a peak of 5.73 feet at 1820MST. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 2 to 3.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes and the closure of many roadways in Green Valley.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 in less than 1 hour fell in Green Valley and caused flash flooding and the closure of several roads. Five homes were flooded in the Casa de Abrego neighborhood, some of which had just been flooded less than 48 hours earlier.
Local Law Enforcement reported that Polacca Wash was overtopping State Route 264 just east of First Mesa.
Major flash flooding was reported on a widely used dirt road between Whippoorwill and Low Mountain.
Two to four inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes up to 3 feet deep across Arivaca Rd. prompting its closure.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than one hour near Kohatk resulted in minor flooding of two homes in that village.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Highway 86 near Indian Route 26 northwest of Sells.

A large area of two inches of rain occurred in three hours in east Tucson, generally east of Craycroft Rd. to the Rincon Mts. with more than 4 inches of rain from Broadway and Wilmot to Tanque Verde and Pantano Rds. Numerous roads were flooded or damaged including Pima Rd. and Robb Wash. Several swift water rescues of motorists occurred including one vehicle washed downstream near Camino Loma Alta and Old Spanish Trail. Alamo Wash left its banks and flooded several homes between Pima and Speedway.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gage on Cline Creek near Jenny Lin Road and 12th Street exceeded alarm stage at 1250MST and bank full at 1254MST. Flow crested at 6.9 feet at 1255MST and fell back below alarm stage at 1307MST. No injuries or damages were reported.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 in 90 minutes west of Interstate 10 and north of Highway 86 in Tucson resulted in flash flooding and the closure of several roads including Bopp Rd, Jamie Ave, Aldon Rd, and Sandario Rd. A vehicle was stranded in floodwaters at Sweetwater and Silverbell.

Strong flows continued in the Canada Del Oro Wash as a result of 1 to 2 of rain in less than an hour in the upper reaches of the basin within the Bighorn burn scar. Overton Rd. was closed due to flooding and the loop trail at Christina Taylor Green Park was flooded. More than an inch of rain in less than 1 hour also occurred from Marana to the southern Tortolita Mountains. As a result a swift water rescue was performed near Grier and Sandario and another west of Edwin and Oracle Rds.
More than 1 inch of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding in Cactus Forest and the closure of Quail Ridge Way near Diffin Rd.

One to two inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in the Benson and St. David areas. Several washes to overtopped in the St. David area and North Miller Rd was closed due to flooding. Ocotillo Road was closed due to flooding north of Benson.
Heavy rain of 2.5 in less than 1 hour at the headwaters of Tanque Verde Creek caused rapid rises of over three feet in Tanque Verde Creek downstream before the channel widens out.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours over the Bighorn burn scar area in the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding of several washes and roadways. Sutherland Wash rose over 5 feet at a gauge just east of Oro Valley and the Canada del Oro Wash also rose, especially downstream of its confluence with the Sutherland Wash. Downstream flash flooding resulted at Overton Rd where 5 people were rescued from two different vehicles which were swept downstream.

Over one inch of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Sabino Canyon Recreation area and the closure of roadways. Several hikers were stranded and needed to be rescued after floodwaters rose.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Davis Rd. between Tombstone and McNeal.

Skunk Creek experienced a significant rise after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area and upstream. At 1400MST the the streamflow gage on Skunk Creek at Carefree Highway exceeded alarm stage. The gage then exceeded bank full at 1410MST and exceeded flood stage at 1418MST. Flow crested at 6.87 feet at 1426MST and would remain above alarm stage until 1715MST. A video posted at 1307MST on social media showed significant flow and debris over Dove Valley Road between I-17 and North Valley Parkway. Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported 27th Avenue was closed between Cloud Road and Dolores Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
One inch of rain in less than 1 hour in Catalina Foothills caused flash flooding of River Rd. near Pontatoc Rd.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flooding from Dewey and the Agua Fria River to Humbug Creek and Mayer. Water was flowing over roads in Dewey and Meyer. A river gauge in Meyer showed a two foot rise.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 fell in less than 1 hour along the entire length of the San Pedro River from San Manuel to Dudleyville and 3 fell near Dudleyville caused the river to rise rapidly, with a greater than 7 foot rise measured in one hour near Mammoth. Extensive flash flooding and severe damage to nearby roadways occurred in the San Manuel, Mammoth and Dudleyville areas.
Early morning rain of 1 to 1.5 on saturated ground caused flash flooding, closure and damage of Camino Adelante Rd between the Picacho Peak Interstate 10 interchange to Park Link Dr.
Two inches of rain in less than 1 hour caused extensive flooding of Arivaca Road between mile markers 10 and 16 with additional flash flooding farther north near Keystone Peak.
More than 3 inches of rain in 90 minutes in Rio Rico Southwest caused flash flooding more than 1 foot deep across several roadways.

More than 1 inch of rain in less than 1 hour fell along State Route 286 north of Santa Margarita Road west to the Baboquivari Mountains causing a number of washes to flow east across Route 286 two to three feet deep.

According to the California Department of Transportation, there were multiple reports of mud and debris covering SR 177 in multiple locations near Desert Lily Sanctuary as running washes flowed over the road, impeding travel. No damage or injuries were reported.

Two people had to be rescued from their mobile home near Central Avenue and Mingus Road after flood waters rapidly overcame the area. Water was reportedly flowing through their windows and there was concern that the home would flow away. They were rescued via helicopter because responders were unable to reach the home on the ground with multiple impassable flooded roads. Rain gages in the area measured over 1.5 inches of rain in less than an hour The two people were uninjured, but their two dogs did not survive.

Heavy rainfall of 10-13 inches fell across much of the county, leading to flash flooding. Approximately 22 water rescues occurred, both from homes and from cars, with 15 in Moss Point. Approximately 150 roads were covered in water, cutting off at least 300 homes and businesses at the height of the flooding. County damage assessments indicate 124 private dwellings with confirmed damage due to either leaking roofs or from flood waters, mostly east of the Pascagoula River. 3 businesses and 13 public buildings were also damaged by water.
Heavy rain of 1 to 2 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in rural areas west of Green Valley. Mission Rd. north of Duval Mine Rd. was closed.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour along Whitewater Draw caused flash flooding downstream where a vehicle abandoned in floodwaters was swept downstream at Kings Hwy. Brooks Rd. was also closed.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour from south of Ajo to east of Why. This caused flash flooding of area washes and the closure of Highway 86 east of Why and Highway 85 between Ajo and Why.
Three hour rainfall of 2.5 fell at the headwaters of Rincon Creek, causing rapid rises in stream flow and flash flooding of Old Spanish Trail.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gage along Skunk Creek at Desert Hills Drive exceeded alarm stage around 1315MST and bank full around 1325MST. Streamflow crested around 5.81 feet at 1329MST and was back below action stage by 1800MST. At 1805MST Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported 19th Avenue was closed between Desert Hills Drive and Irvine Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

A broad area of 1.5 of rain, with pockets of 3 to 4, fell in less than 90 minutes and caused numerous road closures from Picture Rocks to Saguaro National Park West to southeast of Three Points. Kinney Rd. near Sonora Desert Museum was one of the major roads that was closed due to flooding.
