One fatality was at the intersection of Skinker Boulevard and Enright Avenue, just north of the Delmar Loop, where a 60 year old man drowned after driving into the flooded roadway. Firefighters helped or rescued around 70 residents. Property damage was very significant in some hard-hit areas, including the southwest part of the city where 14 to 15 homes experienced significant flooding. A large number of unoccupied vehicles were damaged/destroyed due to the flooding as well. The Metro Link station at Forest Park Parkway and DeBaliviere Avenue was flooded causing $35 million in damage to a two car train, tracks, towers, vehicles and equipment at the station. Dollar amount damage so far is estimated around $85 million.

Video shared on the social media platform Tik Tok showed impressive and devastating flash flooding near Sheep Springs. A massive wave of water near U.S. Highway 491 swept horse trailers, farm equipment, and lawn furniture downstream. Water overtopped the hoods of parked vehicles and inundated a few structures and residences. Damages are a rough estimate.

The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that hours of light, steady rainfall with totals of 1 to 2.5 inches caused burn scar flash flooding on the McBride burn scar near Ruidoso. All of Gavilan Canyon was flooded. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain estimates of 4 to 5 inches from early morning through late afternoon caused a washout of Norwich Road in Ontonagon County 13 miles south of Highway M-64.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Jeff Davis County. There was a video of flowing water over Farm to Market Road 1832 west of State Highway 17 between Balmorhea and Fort Davis.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Scurry County. County Road 1609 north of Ira was almost impassible due to flooding.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Scurry County. Farm to Market Road 1606 and County Road 397 were closed due to high water. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy convective precipitation combined with glacial melt from the Whitney Glacier on Mount Shasta to create a debris flow down Whitney Creek, downstream from the Lava Fire scar. This resulted in the closure of US97 between 1700 PDT and 2100 PDT.
Several vehicles trapped in flood waters in the Socastee and Forestbrook areas.
Cataract Creek/Havasu Creek rose 18 inches at the Supai Gauge.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) Fire scar caused flash flooding over Alice Drive. The water, mud, and many basketball sized rocks made Alice Drive impassable.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2021) caused flash flooding in Schultz Creek. The creek rose 4.84 feet at Highway 180. The water flooded apartments, homes, and streets on the west side of Highway 180.
Granite Creek in Prescott rose about three feet.
Flooding was reported about two miles west of Jeddito at the intersection of State Route 264 and BIA-9101.
The Little Colorado River had a 3 foot rise above Lyman Lake.

Many were suffering hypothermia and were treated on scene. Multiple private roads on the Ashton Hill were washing out. A running track was flooded at North Fremont High School. Moving water was filmed across fields and roads in the area of N 3700 E and E 1400 N. Crops and fields suffered damage in the Marysville area. Several sections of the Ashton-Tetonia Rail Trail were flooded, washed out and covered in mud. 3 cabins reported flooded north northwest of Squirrel. The Henrys Fork River rose one half foot between 5:45 Pm MDT and 9 PM MDT.
Car stalled in 4 feet of water at Highway 38 at Stanfield Cutoff. Parties trapped inside were rescued by Fire Department. Road was closed to clear debris.
Highway 125 was closed overnight in both directions due to mudslide concerns betweek Trail Creek and Forest Road 112.
Bald Knob Road was reported near Blank Road.

Flooding was reported along the Intersection of Orleans Street and North Lakewood Avenue.

Several roadways were flooded within the town of Mansfield.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Video on Twitter showed cars driving through approximately a foot of water on N. Lamar Blvd. at W. 24th St. in Austin.

Heavy rain on I-8 near the Crestwood Road on-ramp. Multiple vehicles parked on the right hand side due to the torrential rain, hail, and poor visibility.

Heavy rain near Yah-Ta-Hey caused water to flow over State Route 264 at mile markers 9 through 10. Any damages are not known.
Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road, near Warrior Drive. Damages are estimated.

The Times and Democrat newspaper in Orangeburg relayed a report and photo, via social media, of a flooded vehicle on Frederick St near Chestnut St in the University Village area of SC State Univ. in Orangeburg. Time estimated.

The Texas Department of Transportation reported that a portion of US Highway 84 was underwater due to heavy rainfall and a large backup in traffic occurred due to the flooded roadway.

In Nashville, the secondary dam on the Nashville City Reservoir sustained a 6 foot wide breach due to the heavy rainfall. The nearby Nashville Memorial Park baseball fields were flooded due to the dam breach.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain moved through an area near the McKinney wildfire in the evening. Rainfall was estimated to be between 1 and 3 inches in an hour. This created a debris flow down Humbug Creek, on the eastern edge of the fire. Four vehicles were reported swept off a culvert over Humbug Creek, and videos showed the swiftly rising water in the area. One person had to be rescued from a partially submerged vehicle. He sustained injuries, but survived.

Roadway flooding near 1509 Shay Rd in Big Bear City. North and south side of Shay Road was flooded. Storm survey by WCM showed several inches of water still flowing over Shay Road. Two to three feet of water flooding across the roadway at SR18 and Johnson Road.

A Marion day care center was evacuated due to flooding. Several inches of water were in the classrooms and hallway. A Cocorahs observer at Marion measured 5.63 inches in a 48-hour period.

The Texas Department of Transportation reported that a portion of Farm to Market Road 597 was closed due to water over the roadway approximately three miles south of Pep. Radar imagery revealed that storms repeatedly trained over northeastern Hockley County for several hours. Although radar reflectivities were not incredibly high during this time, the repeated storms and very efficient rainfall production led to localized flooding.
A car was stranded in high water and the occupants had to be rescued.

Several observations from local media to law enforcement indicated flooding occurring in the Cambridge city limits. The local cooperative observer reported 4.38 inches of rainfall in less than 2 hours with pictures around the city indicating stalled cars in flooded roadways. In addition, a local business had water damage from the runoff.

Media reports water flowing over Big Branch Ball Road near the community of Emmalena.
Water was reported on the road in several locations along KY-550 in Hindman.

The Emergency Manager reports that 6 hour rainfall has been 4 to 8 inches. They also reported that flood waters have moved into the road maintenance shed for the city of Freeport. Additionally, there were two roads washed out in county as well as widespread reports of water on area roadways. The time of the event was estimated using radar.

A trained weather spotter observed Big Clear Creek out of its banks and flowing across U.S. Highway 60. The highway was temporarily closed until flooding of Big Clear Creek receded. No damage to the highway was reported.
Water flooded roads 5 miles east of K'ai'bii'to.

Two boys playing in shallow flood water in a retention area, wandered close to a storm drain, and were pulled under the water. A woman immediately dove into the water to attempt to rescue the boys, and managed to save one of them. The other boy was recovered by first responders, but died at the hospital. The woman was also recovered by first responders, and was taken to a hospital where she was on life support for several days. She later died from her injuries sustained in the drowning.
Water was over the road on the creek-side of Abbott Creek Rd near Bonanza.

Public reports of flooding a the intersection of Baker Road and Galena Road. Report received via social media but flooding likely began earlier.
The Emergency Manager reported flooded roadways with water over the tops of fire hydrants on some of the streets on the northwest side of the city.

West Elm Street was flooded in Jena.

Social media pictures and broadcast media reports indicate that flash flooding caused a home foundation to cave in with water getting into the house. The time of the event is based off of social media and radar data.
A member of the public reported that several yards and alleyways on the south side of Conesville had water up to a foot deep in them.

Heavy rain caused Little Town Hill Creek to overflow its banks, flooding across Hillcreek Road, as well as U.S. Highway 460 to a depth of up to 4 feet. One car was caught in the floodwater and the occupant had to be rescued by emergency responders. Flooding across Highway 460 lasted for around two hours before flooding receded and the highway was reopened. No damage to the road was reported, but with some damage to the flooded vehicle.
Cars stranded in flood waters at the intersection of Dodson Ave and East 3rd St.

Media reported that flooding caused evacuations along State Route 821 between Belle Valley and Cambridge. Also the local emergency manager reported numerous roads closed due to flash flooding.
Flooding of roads and yards on North Choctaw Drive, and also near the intersection of Pinewood Ave and Dellwood Place.
Texas DPS reported that northbound lanes of Interstate 35W near the intersection of Highway 67 were closed due to high water.
A public report indicated several inches of rain in east Dallas with water over the curbs and covering sidewalks.

Flooding caused water to enter a residence on Nellie Hill Road.

Training thunderstorms across the southern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar in San Miguel County produced an estimated 2 to 4 inches of rainfall within the Tecolote Creek and Gallinas Creek areas which caused significant and catastropic flash flooding. Flash flooding and debris flow washed out many roadways within the area, rendering them impassable. The camp director at the Camp Blue Haven said that their playground was underwater for about 40 minutes until water receded. At 2:40 PM MDT, the chief of the Cabo Lucero Volunteer Fire Department received a call about a vehicle floating within the flood waters. When officials responded to the floating vehicle, they also discovered two people dead nearby. While initially thought to have been in their vehicle, officials later determined that the two women, 62-year-old Linda June Cummings and 84-year-old Betty Greenhaw, were swept away from a destroyed home within the Tecolote Canyon subdivision. A third individual from the same home was reported missing, and the National Guard, New Mexico State Police, and San Miguel County Sheriff's Office assised in search and rescue for several days. Finally on Tuesday, July 26th, they found the body of 62-year-old Jimmy Chris Cummings. All three were from Hale Center, Texas, but had a 100-year-lease on a cabin in Tecolote Canyon on the Camp Blue Haven property which they were visiting at the time. Eight feet of water rushing down into the canyon took down two walls of the cabin and partially destroyed the other two walls. Damages for this event are estimated.

MD-28 was closed between Avery and Baltimore Roads due to flowing water from Rock Creek.
A water rescue occurred along Village Lane and Rippling Brook Drive in about two feet of water.
A vehicle was stranded in high water at the intersection of Longmead Crossing Drive and Layhill Road.
About six inches of flowing water was across Dale Drive near Ellsworth Drive.
Three vehicles were stranded in high water along Sligo Creek as it overflowed its banks onto Sligo Creek Parkway near Schuyler Road.

Heavy rain of 2 to 3 inches near Lamy and Glorieta caused flash flooding in the area. A CoCoRaHS observer reported that this heavy rain flooded the arroyo in their backyard, forming a lake. Video shared by local broadcast media also showed flash flooding through a property at La Posta Way. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain in the Tesuque and Chupadero areas resulted in flash flooding. North-northwest of Tesuque, an arroyo overflowed its banks and flooded a backyard near the intersection of Tesuque Village Road and Highway 592. Flash flooding and mud flow also trapped 15 cars in a Tesuque market. Near Chupadero, the emergency manager reported that water over Rio En Medio Road in six locations along roadway. Damages are estimated.

Flash flooding was observed on the northern portion of the Calf Canyon burn scar as heavy rain estimated at 0.75 inches to 1.5 inches fell. The Rito de Gascon rose about four feet and overtopped its banks. Nearby, raging flood waters were observed along a road near Monte Aplanado. The problematic Canoncito Creek also overtopped its banks again which flooded roads and pastures and destroyed fences. Damages are estimated.
Video shared by local broadcast media on Twitter showed flash flooding and mud flow along County Road 117S in Nambe. There are no known damages.
Video shared by local broadcast media shows raging water in a rural part of Pojoaque. Time is estimated based on radar data. No damage reported.

While performing a search and rescue operation for an injured hiker at El Diente Peak, Dolores County Search and Rescue members narrowly escaped a portion of the road exiting the trailhead being washed out as a result of flash flooding from heavy rain.

Roads flooded in town and some flooding on private property. Ridgeview School Building had 3 feet of water in the basement classrooms, and other parts of building had water too. Public reported rainfall of 4.75 inches during the event.

Heavy rain from 1.9 to 3.50 inches was observed near Brush. Flooding was reported along County Road U, just west of Highway 71. A basement in the area also flooded. County Road 28, north of Brush, was completely washed out and underwater.
Received report from social media with photos showing water surrounding multiple homes near the community of Ivel.
Video footage showed Brushy Fork flash flooding over KY-194 at the intersection with Brushy Creek Road near McCombs.
The Pike County Emergency Manager sent a photo of water flowing over the road along Sycamore Creek near the community of Gulnare.
Report of water running across KY-7 near Royalton based on a picture from Twitter.
Video footage showed Ivy Creek flash flooding across Ivy Creek Road near Ivel.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in rural Bandera County between Tarpley and Utopia. The Bandera County Sheriff's Office reported Seco Creek had left its banks and flooded FM 470.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Real County. TxDOT closed Hwy 55 south of Camp Wood due to flooding.
Street flooding was reported via MPing.
Street flooding was reported via MPing.
Street flooding was reported via MPing.
Heavy rain up to 3.5 caused numerous road closures in Sabbatus and some minor road damage to include Elm Street, Jordan Bridge Rd, and Lisbon Rd.
A flood wave around 3 feet or higher passed through Pleasant Creek within Captitol Reef National Park. The flood wave was associated with heavy rainfall in close vicinity to the creek.
Runoff from heavy rain caused some flash flooding to occur near McGregor. Rocks and debris were pushed onto some roads.
Runoff from heavy rains caused some flash flooding to occur across northeast Clayton County. Flood waters from Bloody Run Creek took out a bridge in the Bloody Run County Park west of Marquette.
Six swift water rescues were conducted in Fort Smith, as vehicles had become stranded in flood water. Several roads were closed due to high water.

Radar estimated that as much as 2 to 4 inches of rain fell across the area, the highest amounts focused in a small area in far northwestern Buffalo County north of Miller. Measured amounts of 2.5 to 3.5 inches were reported in and just to the southeast of Pleasanton. There were reports of creeks running full and some rural roads were covered with water.
There were multiple reports of a water hazard on Interstate 95 between Wade and the Godwin/Falcon area.

Up to 10 inches of rain fell in a 6 to 10 hour period causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded including Highway A at the intersection with Highway W, Morsey Center Road about half a mile east of Highway A, and State Highway 47 just south of Powerline Road. Culvert was washed away on Pin Oak Church Road just east of y intersection near New Truxton Road, making the road impassable.
Whitley County 911 dispatch reported that a water rescue took place along Little Wolf Creek Road near Mountain Ash.
Pond Creek was out of its banks and flowing across the back alley at Belfry Middle School.
Wilsons Creek at Old Limey Road was flooded and impassable due to heavy rain and flooding.
Street flooding was reported causing traffic issues.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Edwards County. The Edwards County Sheriff's Office reported several low water crossings on Hwy 55 near Barksdale were flooded and impassable.
The Clarkdale Police Department reported that the Old Jerome Highway/89A was closed due to flooding and debris. Reta Street was also closed due to the flooding.

A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall, primarily over the high terrain just east of U.S. Highway 191/U.S. Highway 6 near milepost 292. Radar estimates showed roughly 1 to 2 inches of rain over the course of around an hour to an hour and a half. This resulted in a flow of water, mud and debris, including railroad ties from an adjacent railroad, to flow over the highway in the vicinity of milepost 292. It was later reported that this led to a family's SUV being washed off of the road, and the family required rescue. No injuries were reported.

Locally heavy rainfall resulted in the flooding of portions of several county roads. A vehicle was driven into a flooded low water crossing west of Stilwell, where it was washed downstream. Four people were inside the vehicle at the time. A 14-year old boy and a 9-year old girl in the vehicle were taken to the hospital, treated, and released. A 6-year old girl was drowned in the vehicle. A 43-year old man was also drowned, and was recovered eleven miles downstream, two days after the incident.
Social media video taken from Queen Creek showed a significant water current several inches deep flowing in the area just south of the San Tan Mountains. No damages or injuries were reported.
The Emergency Manager reported that several roads in town were impassable due to high water.
The Emergency Manager reported that roads were washed out in town.
Flooding was reported in Alberson Wash/Rose Creek, Lynx Creek, and Agua Fria River all the way to Skull Valley.

Local authorities reported closed roads due to flooding in the city of Stanley. In addition, several culverts were washed out and streams were running high between Stanley and Colburn. Based on the flash flood guidance, the rainfall totals were nearly two times that amount to flood. Radar estimates between Colburn and Stanley average between 4 and 6 inches, with an unofficial report of 5.40 inches in the city of Stanley.
Pike County dispatch reported that Indian Creek Road past Sunny Fork was closed due to high water.
Pike County Dispatch reported that Ashcamp Road was closed at the 10000 block due to high water.
Water was observed flowing over KY-221 near the community of Straight Creek.

Up to 9 inches of rain fell in a 6 to 10 hour period causing widespread flash flooding. The heaviest rain axis extended from East St. Louis southeastward towards Mascoutah. Numerous roads were flooded, including northbound I-55 at I-64, ramps from I-64 to I-255, U.S. Highway 50 between O'Fallon and Lebanon, and Illinois Route 15 near intersection with Frank Scott Parkway. Several water rescues were performed including on Illinois Route 15 at Karch Road, east of Freeburg and on West F Street near North 3rd Street in Belleville. An estimated 600 St. Clair County households were damaged by flash flooding. The St. Clair County Animal Shelter was flooded in Belleville so several dozen dogs and some cats had to be evacuated and placed in other shelters or homes temporarily. Overall, no injuries were reported in St. Clair County.

Multiple roads inundated. Multiple structures flooded. Some roadside washouts. For the Marble flash flood event, damages were estimated to be at least $1,000,000, with $750,000 of that going to road repair, and the remainder toward properties.

Flooding closed roadways near the intersection of Big Branch Rd and South Fork Rd, and a home was flooded. Minor flooding of businesses and the river gage house on Main Street. Flooding was also beginning in the Pound Bottom community, which was being monitored for potential evacuations.
US-23 Business Route south of Pound was flooded in several places. Riverside Drive in the Pound Bottom community was flooded near the hairpin turn.
Road closures at the intersection of Wears Valley Rd at Valley View Rd, and at the intersection of Hatcher Mountain Rd at Indigo Ln.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall of around an inch in around a half an hour across a portion of Carnegie. The Pittsburgh fire chief reported flash flooding along Washington Ave between Hope Hollow and Boden Ave.
A member of the public shared a video on social media showing street flooding in Dpue with water flooding an estimated 6 inches deep.
Water was observed flowing over the road in front of Johns Oil (Lonesome Cedar Lane) in the community of Coal Run.
Water was reported out of the banks of Coon Creek and flowing over the road at Johns Branch.
Water was observed flowing over Sukey Hollow Road near Saxton.
A swift water rescue was performed to help a man trapped in a vehicle at low water crosssing on Highway 638, just outside of Manchester. This was also confirmed by the Clay County Emergency Manager.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and road closures in Verde Lakes.

Prescott Valley Police reported hazardous flooding at the intersection of East Lakeshore Drive and East Towago Drive and the intersection of Navajo Drive and Florentine Road. Rain Gauges in the area recorded from 1.50 and 1.86 inches of rain.

Heavy rain fell over the western part of the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022). This caused Schultz Creek (Dry Lakes gauge) to jump 2.84 feet. This flowed over Mt Elden Road, overwhelmed the drainage system along Highway 180, and flooded apartments and homes along Stevanna Way.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010), Tunnel Fire scar (April 2022), and Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flooding in the area below. The water transported mud, ash, and debris across roads and filled ditches.
Flash flooding was reported on the north side of Tuba City washed away dirt roads and people had to be rescued from the water.

Mullen Creek, Savage Run, and Cottonwood Creek all flooded with the Mullen Creek rising 3 feet near the confluence with the North Platte River near A Bar A Ranch. Heavy rain was reported higher upstream over the Mullen Fire Burn Scar Area with 1 hour rainfall accumulation near 1 inch. A Bar A Ranch measured 0.58 inches of rainfall.
Whitley County 911 dispatch reported that Kensee Hollow Road near Red Ash was washed out and active rescues were taking place for people who were trapped on the other side of the washed out road.
Street flooding was ongoing at 6th and Cliff Ave.
Highway K was flooded at a low water area south of Salem.
Spring Creek was reported out of its banks and over the low water bridge.
Retaining ponds and low water areas in the area around Washita and South Streets were flooded. Water was reported making it into one home.

Numerous reports of significant street flooding with water over several portions of Kansas Expressway, Sunshine, Battlefield and Walnut Streets. Record flooding occurred along South Creek and several cars were stalled and flooded on city streets.
Water running along the eastbound lanes of I-10 resulted in closure of the highway near Ford Dry Lake Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Car Stranded along Senator Wash Road about 5 miles south-southwest of Martinez Lake due to flooding. No injuries were reported.

Significant flooding was reported in the El Centro Regional Medical Center. There was 18 inches of flowing water in the parking lot, with the water entering the facility and affecting the emergency room as well as the radiology department. No injuries were reported.
A car was stranded in flood waters on Willow Avenue between Spring Street and Broad Street.
Several vehicles were flooded near the high school in water which reached a depth of 2 to 3 feet.
Flooding closed several lanes on Glenwood Ave near Crabtree Valley Mall in Raleigh.
A public report stated that water was flowing over a street in the community of Emmaafter torrential rainfall.
The Fedscreek Co-op observer reported that water was flowing over the road along Big Card Road near the junction with Hwy-460.
Flooding reported on I-17 near Bell Road in Phoenix. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media report showed slow traffic on SR-238, between mile markers 23 to 40 due to flooding on roadway. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Along CA 177 near the border of Joshua Tree National Park, just north of Desert Center, two washes were completely flooded. The California Highway Patrol requested for Road Flooded signs to keep cars from driving into the flooded roadway. No damages or injuries were reported.

Flash flooding in Greenbriar Campground with multiple people stranded. About 20 parked vehicles washed downstream. Downstream from the Campground, Emerts Cove Road flooded, with bridges inundated and dwellings taking water. Evacuations took place along Pittman Center Road. Upstream from the Campground, significant damage occurred to Greenbriar Road in the National Park.

Runoff from heavy rains pushed some creeks out of their banks. Water from the South Branch O'Neill Creek went over County Highway Y between Chili and U.S. Highway 10. Water from the North Fork Eau Claire River went over County Highway X west of Thorp, and County Highway H northwest of Chili was covered by standing water.

Local creeks in the county, including Gilbert Creek, rose above their banks and restricted access to residential homes only accessible by bridge. Several roadways within the Gilbert Creek community became washed away in spots. It would take until later that evening for roads to become accessible once again.

Nelson Branch rose out its banks and spilled onto Nelson Branch Road. Several other roads were blocked by high water for an extended amount of time between Hanover and North Spring, including Garden Gap Branch Road, North Spring Road, and Rose Branch Road. Some homes were affected.
In Isaban, water surrounded multiple homes due to Cub Creek rising out of its banks.
Six inches of water was observed flowing over Hwy 1804 at the I-75 overpass near Fairview.
The left hand lane of Hwy 25 was blocked under the I-75 overpass due to water flowing over the road.

High water and impassable roads resulted in an evacuation of the Scarbro community. Other roads in the county became flooded and impassable during the early morning hours of the 27th, including Virginia Street, Main Street of Oak Hill, Allman Street, Scarbro Road, White Oak Fork Road, Wolf Creek Road, Shelton Road, and Summerlee Road.

Extensive flash flooding occurred in northwest Perry County.
