Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flash flooding in Government Wash with 8 inches of water, mud, and debris flowing over Highway 89 once the culvert was overwhelmed. Four garages on Heritage Drive and Pioneer Valley Road were flooded.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (2022) resulted in 1-2 feet of water flowing in Schultz Creek, over Mount Elden Road, and overwhelming the culvert at Highway 180, and flowing onto the bike path next to Highway 180. The water flowing over the highway caused a temporary closure.
A swift water rescue took place along Indian Route 4 by Burnt Corn Wash (about 5 miles east of Pi��on) where an elderly gentleman in his car was rescued.
Flash flooding unearthed two main water pipelines (8 and 10 inch) which had to be shut down. This left around 75 people with out flowing water in Indian Wells, Dilkon, and Seba areas.
Flash flooding was reported over Highway 98 five miles east of K'ai'bii'to. Some roads washed out in the area.
Tees Toh Wash was flowing about 2 feet deep about one mile west of Seba Delki.

Evacuations ongoing along the north fork Salmon Creek road, with the bridge on north side of town overtopped with water. Several people are trapped in Kerr campground from flash flooding of the north fork of the Salmon river. North fork salmon creek road washed out in multiple locations from flash flooding. Sinlahekin road flooded and impassable. Road washed out near Salmon Meadows campground from flash flooding. |Reports of at least 25 residences inundated with water. A cabin under construction was destroyed from flood waters.
Flowing water was surrounding a residence along US-460 just west of the Magoffin/Johnson county line.

Up to five inches fell in a three hour period causing flash flooding across the northern half of the city of St. Louis. Numerous roads were flooded including Washington Avenue near the intersection with Walton Avenue, south bound Skinker near Forest Park, Lindell Boulevard near Vandeventer Avenue, South Vandeventer Avenue just south of I-64 and Kingshighway Boulevard between Natural Bridge Avenue and St. Louis Avenue. Flash flooding in the 4700 block of Washington Avenue flooded a local daycare. The fire department had to rescue 15 children and 3 adults from the facility. No injuries were reported. Also, several dozen motorists had to be rescued from their flooded vehicles. Five city schools were damaged due to flooding. The flooding affected schools from north St. Louis to south. Soldan High School had at least 2 feet of water in the cafeteria on the basement floor. At least 4 businesses sustained water damage from the flooding in the Central West End. Both directions of Interstate 64 at Hampton Avenue and eastbound Interstate 70 at Union Boulevard were closed for part of the afternoon due to flooding.
Heavy rainfall occurred along Spring Cove Road. One vehicle had water inside as it was stuck in four feet of water. Several other roads were impacted by flood waters.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Winters Wash in Tonopah showed flow going above alarm stage (1.28 feet) between 18:06 and 18:08 MST, with the flow going above the bankfull stage (3.32 feet) at 18:38 MST and peaking at 4.27 feet (1400 cfs) at 19:18 MST. The flow went below bankfull at 22:49 MST and below alarm stage at 01:43 MST on the 16th. Roads intersecting the wash that were affected from the flow along Winters Wash included Indian School Road, located 1.1 miles downstream of the gauge, and along Salome Highway south of I-10 located 4.6 miles downstream of the gauge. Along Indian School Road, there were reports at around 19:37 MST from a trained spotter of many cars stranded and it is unknown whether or not any of the vehicles sustained damage. No injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Cruff Wash showed flow going above alarm stage (2.5 feet) between 20:29 and 20:31 MST, reaching a peak flow of 3.25 feet (448 cfs) at 21:13 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred at Agua Caliente Road, located about 2 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage between 21:42 and 21:48 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
Rangers at Zion National Park reported flash flooding in Pine Creek and side canyons off of Bridge Mountain due to excessive rainfall in the region.
Flash flooding was reported in X Canyon, Antelope Canyon, and Lower Antelope Canyon (all the same drainage). Standing water remained in Lower Antelope Canyon on July 6.

Law enforcement reported standing water in downtown Cave Spring due to heavy rainfall producing a rise on nearby Cedar Creek and slow drainage. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain fell quickly on top of 1 to 2.5 inches that occurred in the preceding 24-hours.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) and Schultz Fire (2010) scars caused extensive flash flooding northwest through northeast of Flagstaff. Highway 89 northeast of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around mile post 425 around 442 PM MST. The following roads in far northeast Flagstaff were flooded: Copeland Lane, Gunman Road, Vista de Oro, Pioneer Valley Road, and Neptune Drive. Highway 180 northwest of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around MP 218 at 419 PM. The Stevanna Way and Coconino Estates neighborhoods on the northwest side of Flagstaff flooded with apartments, homes, and streets impacted.
The river gauge on Granite Creek showed a rise of 2.55 feet in 90 minutes (at 1130 AM). Flooding was reported on Highway 69 near milepost 295.
Bell County dispatch and the public reported water blocking KY-188 near the Colmar community.
Bell County dispatch reported flood waters blocking KY-217 near Pine Branch Road. Social media reports also indicated flooding just upstream in the Hutch community.
A portion of Route 687 was closed due to flash flooding near Manchester.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a three hour period causing flash flooding across the eastern portions of St. Louis County, including University City, Glendale, Brentwood and Maplewood areas. Numerous roads were flooded including McKnight Road where Deer Creek flows under it, Olive Blvd. and Skinker Blvd. intersection, and Waldron Avenue north of Olive Blvd.
Street flooding was reported in Nixa via MPing.
All washes along SR-177 just north of Desert Center were flooded with Big Wash estimated to have received the most rainfall. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Plows from the California Highway Patrol removed flood debris from SR-111 near Milepost 65. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

A line of thunderstorms with high rain rates resulted in one to two inches of rainfall in less than an hour. This resulted in a portion of highway 65 flash flooding by Broad Street in Leetsville with water rushing across the road.

A line of thunderstorms with high rain rates resulted in around an inch of rainfall in less than thirty minutes across downtown Pittsburgh. Shingiss Rd This resulted in flooding of the low lying portion of Shingiss St underneath the Crosstown Blvd / I570 on-ramp.

Heavy rain in portions of the headwaters region of the Paria River resulted in a flow downstream. The Paria River Near Kanab, Utah gauge indicated a rise from 5 CFS to over 520 CFS in a span of 10 minutes, and peaked at 842 CFS, with a rise of over 2 feet.
Pictures on social media show minor flash flooding and debris along Page Cutoff Road near the community of Calvin.
Water covered the road at the intersection of Highways 189 and 133.
Street flooding occurred on Meadowlane Drive at Michel Street in Brandon.
Water was flowing over the roadway near the intersection of Sambo Jackson Rd and Stewart Rd.

Widespread flash flooding across the city with heavy rainfall from stationary thunderstorms. Numerous CoCoRaHS observers across the city measured between 1.5 to 2.75 inches of rainfall. Flooding was ongoing from 22nd Street to 1st Street and from Harney Street south to Spring Creek.
Water inundated Highway 55 in Merritt, making it impassable. Department of Transportation was on site.
Social media videos showed water entering homes from backyards being flooded in the area of roadway MC 85 and East Baseline Road. No injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge located along Tiger Wash reported water levels along the wash going above alarm stage (5.9 feet) at 16:48 MST, with water levels peaking at 6.06 feet (587 cfs) at 16:57 MST. Flow went below alarm stage at 17:17 MST. Flooding from the wash would have occurred 3.5 miles downstream along Eagle Eye Road 65 minutes later, at around 18:00 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flash flooding along Ogilby Road near Indian Pass Road resulted in mud and gravel mult spots along the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall over the high terrain near the town of Hildale over the course of an hour, with Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour estimates of around 1 to 1.5 inches of rainfall. Light to moderate rain persisted for 2 to 3 hours thereafter. The rainfall resulted in a strong flow in Short Creek through Hildale and on into Colorado City. Dispatch from Colorado City reported all street crossings across the creek were closed due to flooding, and 3 feet of fast moving water was reported to be flowing across Hildale Street.
A video of flash flooding three miles north of Fort Defiance was posted on social media.
A few roads were closed in Rover due to high water, including Cedar Grove Road.
Flash flooding was observed along Main Street in Clarksville, temporarily closing portions of the road.
Trained storm spotter near Bonaza, KY reported that 1.5 to 2 feet of water was flowing down Abbott Creek Road.
Received a picture from the emergency manager of water flowing over the road on KY-194 near the intersection with KY-2059 (Woodman Creek Road).

Up to 11 inches of rain fell between a 6 to 10 hour period causing flash flooding. The heaviest rain was across the far southern portions of Lincoln County. Numerous roads were flooded including Route J south of Troy, Route C west of Old Monroe, and Route MM. Also, a culvert was washed out on Route U between Fred Norton Road and Giles road. Several water rescues were performed. One driver was northbound on Highway J just south of Big Creek in the early morning hours and could not see the flooded roadway in front of her. Before she knew it she was in the water and could not back out of it. The vehicle began to float and fill with water. She called her husband, told him where she was at and asked for him to call 911. She managed to get out of one of her back doors and slip out, grabbing a branch just before her vehicle was completely submerged. It took two and a half hours for the fire rescue to get a boat to the location and rescue her from the tree she was clinging to. She was uninjured. With the other rescues, no one was injured as well.
Video footage from a storm chaser showed flash flooding and a debris flow over KY-194 near Spears Branch Rd in the community of McCombs.
Hyer Branch flooded two sections of County Road 2070 making it impassable.
Heavy rainfall caused Horse Creek to flow out of its banks making County Road 2120 impassable.
Excessive rainfall flooded several roads.
The Professional Building at Cherry Street and Kimbrough had water in the first floor.
A local hospital emergency room reported water from flash flooding due to very heavy rainfall. This caused the ER to closed, diverting ambulance traffic to other hospitals.

Video from a storm chaser showed flash flooding washing away Mohave Road. The location of the flooding was about 6-7 miles north of I-10, just northeast of Blythe, CA. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Pictures were sent in from a trained spotter of water entering the Adelante Healthcare facility and some of the downtown stores in Buckeye. Water was estimated to be 6 to 8 inches deep. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on US-95 near Milepost 104 in Quartzsite. No damages or injuries were reported.

A thunderstorm moved along Birch Creek near state Route 12, east of the town of Escalante. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall 1-hour estimates were around 1 to 1.5 inches in the vicinity of Birch Creek, near the confluence with the Escalante River. A video from social media showed that this resulted in flash flooding on Birch Creek into the Escalante River.

A series of moderate, to at times strong, thunderstorms moved through Capitol Reef National Park over the span of 2 to 3 hours. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 3-hour rainfall estimates showed around 1 to 2 inches within the park. As a result, a flow of 6-8 inches of water moved through Capitol Gorge, as reported by Park officials.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall in the high terrain around the town of Hildale, as well as within the town itself. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor (MRMS) 1-hour estimates showed around 1 to 2 inches of rainfall with this storm. Light to moderate rain continued for a while thereafter, with 3-hour MRMS estimates exceeding 2 inches of rainfall in spots. This rainfall ran into Short Creek, and resulted in a flow through the town of Hildale, though the flow was not significant enough to overtop any road crossings within town.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall over the course of an hour or so in the high terrain northwest of the town of Leeds, UT. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour estimates show around 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rainfall with this storm. An initial report was received of water over the bridge at Red Cliffs Campground as water flowed out of Water Canyon and through Harrisburg Creek. A short time later, a video was found on Twitter showing water flowing through the campground and overtopping the access bridge.
Radar estimates indicated 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across the eastern sections of Mower County. This resulted in some flash flooding that sent water over a road east of Grand Meadow.
Received report via Facebook that the park behind the middle school was flooded.
Significant runoff and street flooding observed near Kimball. Kimball Airport AWOS station (KIBM) measured 1.26 inches of rainfall in less than 90 minutes.
Excessive rain caused flash flooding across Hines Street near Brookline Fire Station 2.
Heavy flooding reported on the on and off ramp of South 4th street and I-8 in El Centro. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Centennial Wash at the Union Pacific Railroad showed flow going above alarm stage (8.5 feet) between 21:53 and 21:56 MST and continuing to rise for several hours more to reach a peak flow of 13 feet (4315 cfs) at 02:06 MST on the 16th. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along the Old US Highway 80, located 6 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage at 13:34 MST on the 16th. No damages or injuries were reported.
The intersection of Griffith Rd and Salem Creek Dr was closed due to water covering the roadway.
Route 11 was closed due to water over the road. Water was on it's way down at the time of the report.
A water rescue was reported at the intersection of Grant Avenue and Commercial Street due to flooding.

Up to 13 inches of rain fell in a 6 to 10 hour period causing widespread flash flooding. The axis of heaviest rain extended from just north of Wentzville east southeastward through northern portions of O'Fallon through St. Peters and into St. Charles. Numerous roads were flooded throughout St. Charles County. Interstate 70 was flooded with up to five feet of water around the intersection with Mid Rivers Mall Drive. Fire and rescue searched and cleared several dozen vehicles in this area and rescued 8 people from the rising waters. Also, in the area of Harry S. Truman Blvd and Premier Parkway, several drivers were rescued from their flooded vehicles. In the area of Mexico Road and Spencer Road, multiple vehicles were trapped by rapidly rising waters of Spencer Creek. One vehicle in this area was swept off the roadway into Spencer Creek. The driver escaped but was clinging to a tree in the fast moving water that was over 8 feet deep. He was rescued and was not injured. Between 1 am and 11 am, 87 people were evacuated from homes or businesses in St. Charles County. One hundred seventeen buildings were damaged from the flooding. Forty Nine of them sustained major damage, 46 sustained moderate damage and 22 buildings sustained minor damage. So far damage is estimated to be around $10 million dollars.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Del Rio. The Del Rio Police Department reported several roads flooded around the city.
Route WW at Archer Creek was closed and impassable.

Up to three inches of rain fell in about an hour and a half causing flash flooding. Several roads in far northern portions of Jefferson County were briefly flooded. One vehicle became stuck in flood waters after being driven into the flooded section of roadway, about 3 miles southeast of Murphy. No injuries were reported.
Street flooding was reported via MPing.
Street flooding was reported via MPing.
South Creek was reported out of its banks.
The intersection of Cherry Street and National Avenue were reported as impassable due to high water.
The intersection of Jefferson and Chestnut Avenues were reported as flooded and impassable.
Flooding was reported at the intersection of Campbell and Chestnut Avenues.
A water rescue was reported at the intersection of Chestnut Expressway and National Avenue due to flooding.
A water rescue was reported at the intersection of Main and Mill Streets.
Emergency management reported moderate flow of water down Utah Trail located in the northwestern portion of Joshua Tree National Park. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road showed flow going above alarm stage (3.3 feet) between 19:28 and 20:07 MST and continuing to rise for several hours more to reach a peak flow of 7.25 feet (1700 cfs) at 23:38 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along Tuthill Road, located 3.2 miles downstream and Narramore Road, located 6.4 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage at 07:03 MST on the 16th. A truck was swept off Narramore Road due to the strong current from the wash. There was no information received about the occupants that were inside the truck.
Significant street flooding was reported via MPing.

Very heavy rainfall occurred in a short period of time in the city of Owatonna. There were a few streets that had water covering the roadway and were impassable at one point. These roads included the intersection of Elm and Main Street, and Rose and Elm Street on the east side of town.
Heavy rain caused Little Pine Island to go over bank full and flood streets around Pinewood Estates.
Stream gages indicated multiple bayous or ditches overflowed in China and Hampshire. Numerous roads were also flooded by several inches of rain in west Jefferson County.
A HAM radio operator reported multiple cars stalled in standing water near the Stewart Road and Dick Drake Way intersection. Mississippi River Drive in the downtown area was also flooded.
Rapid Creek at Wilson's Orchard came out of its banks, overspreading an area the size of a football field with 2 to 3 feet of fast flowing water. Access to the south side of the orchard was cut off.
The COOP Observer reported patio flooded with water flowing through the basement window. Measured 3.05 inches of rain between 9 and 11 PM.
Flash flooding occurred southwest of Collins near the Williamsburg community.
Multiple streets were flooded in the city of Cleveland.
Highway 129 was flooded and impassable east of Lynnville.
Facebook report indicated major road flooding occurred on Bear Creek Road.

Reported flooding across low lying areas south of Centennial near the North Fork Little Laramie River after 2 inches of heavy rain fell in less than an hour just north of Centennial and on the west slopes of Sheep Mountain.
Four feet of water was flowing over Back O' Beyond Road in Sedona near Cathedral Rock.
Flooding reported in the area of SR-387 and SR-187 in Sacaton. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Rainbow Wash reported flow rising to above alarm stage (1.4 feet) between 17:21 and 17:25 MST, exceeding the bankfull stage (4.1 feet) between 18:17 and 18:27 MST and peaking at 4.42 feet (2368 cfs) at around 18:55 MST. Any flooding impacts from the wash included Old US-80 and Patterson Road, located about 5.6 miles downstream. The wash went below bankfull stage at around 19:31 MST, before another rise above the bankfull stage occurred at around 23:02 MST. The flow did not go below action stage until around 00:47 MST on the 16th.
Burro Creek Crossing was closed from Hwy 93 to mile post 14.
Heavy rain over the Government Tank drainage and Pipeline/Tunnel fire scars caused flooding along the side of Highway 89 with only one lane open.
A car stalled in high water with three people trapped inside on Mount Ararat Road. Flood waters also reached 1 to 1.5 feet deep on Weakley Creek Road.
Several sections of roads north and west of Nixa, including Tracker Road, were flooded and impassable.
Dry Crane Creek flooded 2-3 feet over Jasmine Road.
Wilsons Creek was reported out of its banks and flooding Farm Road 146 near Rutledge Wilson Farm. Additional heavy rainfall fell on the headwaters of the Jordan and Fassnight Creek basins.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Delaney Wash showed flow going above alarm stage (1.87 feet) between 22:51 and 22:53 MST, with a peak flow of 2.3 feet (255 cfs) at 23:07 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along 411th Avenue, located 2.1 miles downstream and Salome Highway, located 3.7 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage between 5:05 and 5:51 MST on the 16th. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along East Fork Cave Creek near 7th Avenue showed the flow going above alarm stage (2 feet) at around 2:36 MST, peaking at 3.33 feet (1239 cfs) at 3:05 MST, and dropped below alarm stage between 4:01 and 4:36 MST. Flooding likely occurred at the low water crossing along 7th Avenue. No damages or injuries were reported.

A video showed flooding occurring from Bloody Tanks. Water was reaching the bottom of a bridge as well as going around it, briefly trapping the person recording the incident. The location of the incident was in the area of Schulze Ranch Road and U.S. 60. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Stream gauges indicated Goose Creek exceeded its established flood stage after 2.5 to 3.5 inches of rain fell in the headwaters in just a couple of hours. Stevens Mill Rd along with a few other roads were inundated in the Indian Trail area.

A 64 year old woman was killed when water left the banks of Brushy Fork and swept away her house on Brushy Fork Road. A barn and all the family's belongings were also swept away in the flood waters. The body of the woman was found 5 miles downstream by family members after first responders suspended their efforts overnight. The value of the damaged property is unknown.

Flash flooding affected many locations within Orange and Seminole Counties due to 8-14 inches of rain, which occurred primarily over a 12-18 hour period. Numerous roadways were flooded and became impassible. FDOT reported several water rescues along on-ramps to Interstate 4, where between 3 to 5 feet of standing water was noted. Emergency Management officials indicated numerous water rescues elsewhere along area roadways and within residential communities.
Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed.

County comms reported flash flooding developed along tributaries of the Tallulah River in south central Rabun County ater 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the course of a few hours. This was in addition to the 3 to 5 inches that had fallen over the area since the 2nd. Ramey Rd, Shady Ln, and Old Highway 441 were inundated by overflowing creeks.
Road Department closed Commerce Street due to flooding. Location notoriously floods due to low elevation. Depth of water now 6-12 inches.
Flashing flooding was reported near United States Highway 501 and Stadium Drive.
Flash flooding was reporte along Walnut Creek at Rose Lane.
Flash Flooding was reported along Crabtree Creek greenway near Morrisville.

County comms reported that a campground on Burrells Ford Rd at the Chattooga River was inundated with 2 to 3 feet of water and evacuated after 1 to 2 inches of rain fell during the morning of the 5th. This was on top of 3 to 5 inches of rain that had fallen across the area since the 2nd.
Flash flooding was reported along Highway 41 in the retail area on the east side of Henderson.

A number of roadways were flooded in and around Owensboro, including Carter Road. Storm total rainfall ranged up to 5.48 inches at a rain gage on the west side of Owensboro, near the east end of the Audubon Parkway where it meets Highway 60. A residential neighborhood in the immediate vicinity of this gage was flooded. There was also a report of 5.37 inches a mile west of the Owensboro airport.
Water completely covered the intersection of Highways 57 and 68.
Officials from Capitol Reef National Park reported 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through a wash that feeds into the Grand Wash, as well as 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through Grand Wash itself.

Zion National Park officials reported that normally dry washes near Canyon Junction were seeing flash flooding, that there were waterfalls on both sides of Zion Canyon, and that the campground had minor flooding. A thunderstorm which moved through produced an estimated 0.25 to 0.75 inches of rainfall per Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour analysis.
Water flowing over roadways.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Rd.
Several roads were closed, and a swift water rescue was performed on Oatman Highway.
Burro Creek Crossing Rd was closed.
Seventeen Mile Road was closed.
Signal Rd was closed.
Oatman Hwy was closed.
Eight water rescues occurred, five to ten homes had water in them, and an observer measured 3.86 inches of rain in just under two hours.
Numerous roads in and near Golden Valley were closed.
Banegas Crossing was closed.
Huffriter Rd was closed.
Woman helped from vehicle after driving into floodwaters on Commerce Street. Depth of water was 6-8 inches.
Intersection of Chisholm and Gresham Roads underwater. Depth estimated at 1-2 feet from earlier heavy rainfall. Elevation is in low spot. Report relayed via social media.
A Facebook report showed flooding at the Brookwood Apartments in Columbia on West 7th Street and Academy Lane with several cars flooded. Damages are estimated for the flooded cars.

Bureau of Land Management officials reported a flash flood wave moving down Phipps Wash toward the Escalante River. This is most likely associated with a brief thunderstorm which moved through the area between roughly 11:30 am MST to 12:30 pm MST and produced moderate to heavy rainfall. Event time is based upon report.
Route 1 experienced flash flooding from Big Fork to the Virginia/North Carolina border. In addition, it was reported that rocks and debris were washing onto portions of the road.

Widespread significant flash flooding due to 8 to 12+ inches of rain in less than 12 hours across much of Chattooga County. Numerous roads were washed out or closed. At one point during the afternoon, the impacts triggered a Flash Flood Emergency for areas between Lyerly, Summerville, and James H Floyd State Park.
Bogles Ranch Rd was closed.
Pump Station Rd was closed.
Hwy 395 was partially flooded.
Flooding, debris, and road damage closed Hwy 190.
Hwy 168 was flooded at The Narrows.
Badwater Rd was closed due to flooding, debris, and road damage.
Hwy 136 was closed due to mud with a motorcycle stuck.
Hwy 190 was flooded and damaged at and just west of Towne Pass.
Pine Creek Rd was covered with water, boulders, and debris, stranding campers.
Zzyzx Rd was damaged, and Mojave Rd was impassable from Rasor Rd to Kelbaker Rd.

Heavy rain near Nolensville resulted in several inches of standing water in the subdivision near Burnt Knob Road and Stewart Creek Road. This same subdivision was impacted by flooding about 24 hours prior.
Heavy rain and flooding southeast of Smithville forced the closure of an intersection at Bright Hill Road and Hooper Road.
Water rising over a creek bank and an estimated 6 inches of water flowing over the road on Willow Lake Circle. Report relayed via social media.
Several roads in Marshall County are impassable due to flash flooding: Askea Grove Lane, Warrenton Road, Brashiers Chapel Road, Cobb Road, Lookout Drive, and Lexington Drive.
Hulaco Road underwater due to flash flooding. Depth of water unknown.
Widespread flash flooding was reported in the town of South Hill.
Flooding occurred on North Main Street in Franklin, resulting in the temporary closure of the road.
Connector Road was closed due to water rises along Hardy Creek and the Little Kentucky River. Five other roads experienced minor flooding across Trimble County.
A large amount of water and mud covered Main St at Hinkley Rd.
Fort Irwin Rd was flooded.
Both sides of Hwy 395 were flooded near Olancha Ln. Later reports noted large boulders in the road, and stated that the road was flexing from the water.
Hwy 190 was closed.
Hwy 395 was flooded at Lone Willow Dip (in addition to the Olancha Ln flooding also documented in this episode), stranding 50 to 100 cars between the two flooded areas.
Hwy 190 was washed away by a 10 to 15 foot high wall of fast-moving water near Centennial Flats. One truck was swept away; the occupant was unharmed.
Hwy 136 was closed.
Knee high mud was over Hwy 190, and a school bus was stuck in the mud.
Hwy 6 was flooded with water and mud.

County comms and stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed across Avery County after 4 to 7 inches of rain fell across the eastern half of the county in around 24 hours, with 1 to 2 inches of that falling in a couple of hours during the late morning and early afternoon. Multiple roads were closed due to high water including Greene Rd and Puckett Rd (due to flooding along the Elk River). Multiple other streams were impacted in the Banner Elk area, where at least one building was surrounded by floodwater. A stream gauge on the North Toe River in Newland also exceeded its established flood stage indicating inundation of Linville St.
The Lincoln County emergency manager reported Gavilan Canyon Road near Janet Drive experienced flash flooding as heavy rain fell on the McBride burn scar. Damages are not known.

A nearly stationary thunderstorm over El Porvenir produced over two inches of rainfall on this area of the Calf Canyon burn scar. This caused flash flooding on Beaver Creek and Gallinas Creek with significant debris found on Highway 65. The IMET on duty found several locations along Highway 65 that were covered in tree debris, rocks, and mud. Some buildings along the roadway were inundated with a couple of feet of water. The IMET also noted that water had threatened homes in the area as well, but these homes seemed to have been protected with sandbagging. Damages are estimated.
High water was reported on several roads near the downtown area. Barricades were requested to close off affected roads.
Multiple streets in the South Shore Estates of Corpus Christi were flooded.

A home was swept off of its foundation at 7701 Hatton Road along the Dutch Fork, resulting in the rescue of two individuals in that home. Seven other homes received damage along the Dutch Fork, including along Quisenberry Lane.

A portion of Stockton Road washed away immediately south of the bridge over North Benson Creek. The roadway surface was washed away and the road was temporarily closed while repairs were made. A pickup truck was also washed into a tree, with the driver escaping the truck without injury.
Hwy 317 was closed, and water flowed through stores in southeast Caliente off Elle Mtn.
Six to eight inches of water plus mud and debris covered the northbound lanes of Hwy 160.
One lane of Hwy 93 was flooded just south of Hwy 168.
Hwy 93 was flooded at Lincoln Co mile markers 105 and 109.
There were multiple reports of flooding in Alamo.

Significant road flooding occurred in Moapa, Moapa Valley, Overton, and Valley of Fire State Park. The Overton co-op observer measured 1.89 inches of rain, including 0.80 inch in 20 minutes. Multiple vehicles were stuck in Valley of Fire.
Hwy 160 was flooded.
The intersection of Farm Rd and Grand Canyon Dr was flooded.

Widespread flash flooding across the Boardman area. Local dispatch, local media, and the local stormwater district reported over 250 residences that experienced basement flooding, with a few reports of water filling entire basements. Widespread street flooding with reports of dozens of car stranded in high water as high as three feet deep. Radar estimated rainfall totaled up to 4.5 in just under a three hour period, which has a 0.2% chance or less probability of annual occurrence per NOAA Atlas 14. Instantaneous rates of up to 6 per hour were observed, with a peak 15 minute rainfall accumulation around 1.25.
Park Blvd was closed just outside the west entrance to Joshua Tree National Park.
Multiple roads were flooded, and one van was stuck in flowing water.
Hwy 62 was flooded and partly washed away.

Localized heavy rainfall on Gavilan Ridge flowed downhill onto the McBride burn scar which caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road from Janet Drive northward to Airplane Canyon. Burn scar flash flooding resulted in rock and mud debris along the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek. Water was several feet deep and came within 2 feet or so from the bottom of the bridge on state Route 24.
Flash flooding was reported in Clear Creek within Zion National Park.
Flash flooding was reported in the vicinity of The Narrows in Zion National Park.
The Hildale Dispatch reported two road closures near waterways due to rises from flash flooding.

A school basement in the town of Dubois flooded, and local emergency services were requested to help remove water from the school. Rainfall totals of between 3 and 4 inches were observed in the vicinity of the flooding reports.
Highway 527 in northern Taylor County became temporarily impassable due to water over the roadway.
A water rescue of a vehicle occurred near the intersection of Kentucky Route 210 and Kentucky Route 569.

Flash flooding affected many locations within Orange County due to 8-14 inches of rain, which occurred primarily over a 12-18 hour period. Numerous roadways were flooded and became impassible. Emergency Management officials indicated several water rescues along area roadways and within residential communities to the north of Orlando International Airport due to standing water of up to 3 to 5 foot in depth.
Three drivers were rescued after their cars stalled in water, and Nellis Blvd was closed due to the flooding.
Side creeks overflowing, along with nearby cropland. A yard was covered with water and a basement was flooded. Depth of water unknown.
Flash flooding with road closures occurred on South Union Street and Martha Avenue just south of Olean.
Flooding was reported on Jolls Road and Dewey Road.
Flooding was reported at Allen Street and James Street.
Numerous roads in and south of Golden Valley were closed due to flooding.
Kentucky Route 90 (Burkesville Road) was completely covered with water due to heavy rainfall.

Flash flooding affected many locations within Osceola County due to 8-12 inches of rain, which occurred primarily over a 12-18 hour period. Numerous roadways were flooded and became impassible. Emergency Management officials indicated several water rescues along area roadways and within residential communities in St. Cloud due to standing water in excess of three feet in depth. Florida Highway Patrol reported a full closure of the Florida Turnpike between Mile Marker's 254-267 near St. Cloud due to standing water on both sides of the highway.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding in Big Bend National Park. All dirt roads, backcountry roadside campsites, and at least one paved road were closed throughout Big Bend National Park due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Portions of State Road 30 near Pikeville were impassable.
Flooding was reported on Route 39.
Flooding was reported at Morey Street and Williams Street.
Flooding closed northbound Route 219 at Clark Road.
Water was reported flowing over Windfall Road.
Flooding was reported on River Road.
Flooding was reported on Route 305.
Flooding was reported on Yaeger Hill Road near Route 417.
Received a report of a stalled car due to heavy rain and sitting water at the underpass of the Acadian Thruway underpass.
Heavy rainfall resulted in flooding at the intersection of Corporate Boulevard and Energy Drive with water approximately 1 foot deep.
Heavy rain resulted in street flooding near Webb Park. Water estimated to be around 1 foot deep. Time estimated by radar.

Flash flooding affected northern Brevard County due to 8-14 inches of rain, which occurred primarily over a 12-18 hour period. Emergency Management officials indicated numerous water rescues elsewhere along area roadways and within residential communities, particularly in Mims and Scottsmoor where the heaviest rain fell. Many areas experienced standing water at/above 3 feet above ground level and|water approached or entered several homes.

Madison Police Dept reported flooding of Hursthaven Court at Hursthaven Drive in the Mountain Brook neighborhood. Flood water was deep enough to block residents from entering their homes. Flooding also reported along Zierdt Road. Depth of water estimated at 6-12.

Moderate rainfall coincided with a very high astronomical tide and storm surge, resulting in overtopped storm drains and flooding in low-lying urban areas. Several portside business and parking lots were inundated. The flooding was a combination of freshwater runoff and high tide storm surge.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. Several roads were closed along Black River near Malaga. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Terrell County. There was several feet of floodwater in Sanderson Canyon which resulted in evacuations. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the Big Bend National Park. A section of the Lost Mine Trail collapsed which resulted in heavy damage to that section of trail. The bottom of the trail was covered in rocks and the top of the trail was too narrow to safely cross. The trail was closed as a result. Also, high water and debris crossed the pavement along the Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive. The pavement was broken off and washed away. Logs and rocks were washed onto the road which made it unsafe to travel. The damage and debris resulted in the road being closed. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Interstate 290 was closed due to flooding near Des Plaines Avenue.
The intersection of Burlington Avenue and Cass Avenue was flooded with 6 to 8 inches of flowing water just north of the train tracks.
Several underpasses were under water across Springfield.
The underpass at Kirby Avenue and Neil Street was flooded.
Heavy rain resulted in street flooding on Freret near the Fogelman Arena in Devlin Fieldhouse. Water estimated to be around 1 foot deep.
Heavy rain resulted in street flooding near the intersection of Magazine and Napoleon Avenue. Water estimated to be around 1 foot deep.
Heavy rain resulted in street flooding near the intersection of Willow and Calhoun. Water estimated to be around 1.5 feet deep.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding around 1.5 feet deep near Napoleon and Camp. Time estimated by radar.

Flash flooding affected northern Brevard County due to 8-14 inches of rain, which occurred primarily over a 12-18 hour period. Emergency Management officials indicated numerous water rescues elsewhere along area roadways and within residential communities in Cocoa and Port St. John. Many areas experienced standing water at/above 3 feet above ground level and water approached or entered several homes. State Road 528 was closed between Interstate 95 and SR 520 due to standing water on both sides of the highway.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the City of Midland. There were multiple stalled vehicles reported in flash flooding at the intersections of North Loop 250 and Lancashire, North Garfield and Castleford, and Midland Drive and Wadley. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in north Odessa. There was a road closure at the intersection of Andrews Highway and 87th Street in north Odessa due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time, especially in the Lake Glenn Shoals and Irving areas. Several roads were flooded including Illinois Route 16 just northeast of Irving. A vehicle was driven into the flood waters and stalled in this area. The driver was rescued and no injuries were reported.
Flash flooding occurred on the lower portion of the Palisade Plunge trail in Mesa County as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms.
Several creeks were out of their banks in the vicinity of Aberdeen Road, mainly to the west of Aberdeen.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding around 1 foot deep near Chippewa and Felicity streets. Time estimated by radar.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding around 1 foot deep near the intersection of Washington and Annunciation Streets. Time estimated by radar.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding around 1 foot deep along General Pershing. Time estimated by radar.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding around 1 foot deep near the intersection of Dante and Oak Streets. Time estimated by radar.

Flash flooding affected many locations within Volusia County due to 12-16 inches of rain, with isolated totals of up to 20 inches, which occurred over a 12-18 hour period. Many areas experienced standing water at/above 3 feet above ground level and water entered numerous homes. Numerous roadways were flooded and became impassible. Emergency Management officials indicated numerous water rescues occurred within the communities Daytona Beach, Port Orange, and New Smyrna Beach.
Multiple vehicles were stranded in high water in the streets of northern and western Sioux Falls.
In Westport, Cheryl's Way was flooded with debris and rocks in the road. Report relayed by amateur radio.
In New Bedford, Dartmouth Street at Rockdale Avenue was flooded to the point where DPW assistance was required. Padanaram Ave. was also flooded. Report relayed by amateur radio.

Park rangers relayed a report of flash flooding in Capitol Gorge, with floodwaters as much as 4 feet deep. This is associated with showers and thunderstorms which moved through the area between around 12:30 pm MST to 2:00 pm MST and produced around 0.50 inches of rainfall.

Eight to 10 inches of rain over a few hour period caused significant flash flooding over portions of western Switzerland County. Numerous creeks and streams were out of their banks. The hardest hit areas were in the vicinity of Bennington and along Indian Creek, where several county bridges were heavily damaged and a couple of bridges were washed out. Significant damage occurred to numerous homes along Indian Creek with trees also downed by the flowing water and roadways along the creek washed out in places.
Several inches of water were reported on Rucker Blvd near the Coffee-Dale county line.
Broadcast media reported several impassable streets throughout Tulane University due to flooded streets.
In Webster, police reported that West Main St. (Rt. 197) at Mason Lane was closed due to flooding. Also, a portion of Worcester Rd (Rt. 12) was closed and impassable. Relayed by amateur radio.
Ditches were completely full and overflowing onto Maumelle Blvd/Highway 100 at the I-430 interchange. Four to six inches of water was flowing over the roadway.
Multiple streets were flooded in Pine Bluff.
The sheriff's office reported multiple roads underwater across the southern half of Saline county.
The sheriff's office reported multiple roads underwater north of Glen Rose.
Multiple flooded roadways were reported in the area between Grove City and Sandy Lake.
Heavy rain caused roads in the area north of Wesley to flood.

Moderate rain moved over portions of Wire Pass and Buckskin Gulch slot canyons, as well as nearby drainages, with 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates up to 0.75 inches. Flash Flooding was reported by the Paria Contact Station at 12:00 pm MST, with reports of several hikers in the area needing to form human chains in three separate locations to escape flood waters. No injuries were noted at the time of report.

A strong thunderstorm moved through portions of the Paria River drainage basin, with widespread 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches. This generated a flood wave that propagated downstream, with the Paria near Kanab river gauge rising from 100 CFS around 1:00 pm MST to 1180 CFS at 1:25 pm MST.

Moderate to heavy rain fell across Zion National Park and surrounding areas, with 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of around 0.50 inches. As a result, the North Fork Virgin at Springdale river gauge recorded a rapid rise in stage from around 50 CFS to over 1200 CFS in under 2 hours. Additionally, park rangers at Zion National Park reported flooding in many slot canyons in the park, as well as several observed waterfalls.

In Providence, 7 to 10 inches of rain fell over the course of a few hours during the mid to late afternoon creating serious flash flooding. 8.31 inches of rain fell in the Elmwood section of the city and 6.89 in the College Hill section. National news media showed aerial views of Interstate 95 which had become completely flooded and was closed in both directions. The snarled traffic lasted for multiple hours. Cars were reported to be stuck in the following locations: Webster Ave., Hamilton St., Cadillac Ave. at Melrose St. (water up to the windows), Narragansett Ave at Santiago St., Rugby St. at Thurbers Ave. Additional flooding and road closure reports included: Thackery St. at Melrose St., the underpass of Rt. 10 north at Westminster St., Hartford Ave. at Heath St., Smith St. at Gentian Ave., Exchange St., Pleasant Valley Parkway at Berlin St., Huntington Ave., Manton Ave. at Saban St., Elmwood Ave. ramp to Rt. 10, and Olneyville Square. One block of Atwells Avenue was washed out. Many water rescues were necessary due to life-threatening situations. All together, there were 3 injuries related to motor vehicle accidents during the storm and roughly 25 individuals rescued. On Benevolent St. water invaded the 1st floor of a Brown University campus building. On Elmwood Ave. there was rapid flooding of a structure of unspecified type. On Peace Street, there was a partial (25%) collapse of the roof of a vacant building, which was being redeveloped into a shopping plaza. A total of 41 homes and businesses were flooded. The West River overtopped its banks and flooded Charles Street and portions of Silver Spring Street in the evening. The Woonasquatucket River crested at 6.07 ft. at 315 AM on September 7th, which was above the 5.5 ft. flood stage. Many thanks to the Providence Emergency Management Agency for some of these details.
Bridge flooded and impassable on County Road 828.
A basement wall collapsed due to flooding on Hemslock Lane.
Significant street flooding was present at Interstate 229 and 10th Street.
Route 138 is closed in both directions between Route 169 and Ross Road due to flooding in the Town of Lisbon.
Road closed due to flooding at intersection of Bank Street and Blinman Street.
Road closed due to flooding at the intersection of Broad Street and Ledyard Street.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Highway 166, west of New Cuyama. The flooding was the result of heavy rain from strong thunderstorms.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Mount Baldy Road, about 6 miles north-northeast of Claremont.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along State Route 33, about one mile north of the Lockwood Valley Road intersections. Several vehicles were stuck in mud and debris.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding with mud/debris flows across Lake Hughes Road, about 2 miles south of the Elizabeth Lake Road intersection. Several vehicles were stuck in mud and debris.
In North Providence, Library Rd. by Adams Library was flooded and impassable. Relayed by amateur radio.

In Providence County, very heavy rain fell, eventually amounting to 7 to 10 inches. Approximately 6 inches fell in 2 hours leading to flash flooding. At 1:51 PM EDT Oregon St. at Whipple St. was closed. At 2:05 PM EDT a car was stuck in street flooding on Valley St. at Eagle St. Cars were traveling in the wrong direction to avoid flooding on Pleasant Valley Parkway. At 2:26 PM EDT Dexter St. at Huntington Ave. was reported to be flooded and impassable. Relayed by amateur radio.

In Cranston, at 2:02 PM EDT a car was stuck in street flooding on Fletcher Ave. Between 2:04 and 2:11 PM EDT multiple cars were stuck in street flooding on Atwood Ave. At 2:13 PM EDT Rt. 10 north at Union Ave was flooded and impassable with cars stuck in the flooding. Relayed by amateur radio.

Widespread street flooding occurred in the Evansville metro area. The water was waist deep in spots. Some water rescues were conducted from stranded vehicles. In the large retail area on the east side of Evansville, Green River Road was flooded both north and south of the Lloyd Expressway. Flash flooding was reported all along Highway 41 in Evansville. The storm total rainfall was about three inches at rain gages in the county.
Portions of Highway 77 were underwater.
Water was approaching a home.

Moderate to heavy rainfall from earlier in the day resulted in a flood wave traversing downstream along the Virgin River. The Virgin at Virgin river gauge recorded a flow increase from 333 CFS at 12:15 am MST to a peak of 2020 CFS at 2:00 am MST.

Strong thunderstorms moved over the Oquirrh Mountains over the course of an hour or two, resulting in moderate to at times heavy rain over the Jacob City Fire burn scar. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour rainfall estimates were in the 0.50 to 0.75 inch range. This was enough to result in a flow along Soldier Creek, which resulted in the evacuation of one house by State Route 36 and a road closure.

Multiple thunderstorms with moderate to heavy rainfall moved over Bryce Canyon National Park during the late evening hours. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 3-hour rainfall estimates showed widespread amounts of 1 to 2 inches, and the Bryce Canyon Airport ASOS recorded nearly 1.5 inches of rain over the span of 3:30 pm MST to 4:30 pm MST. Many trails sustained damage, with some leading to extended trail closures. The Queen's Garden trail suffered a few debris flows with unstable footing and two retaining wall failures. The Peekaboo Loop suffered numerous debris flows and points of trail surface erosion. The Bryce Point Peekaboo Connecting Trail suffered numerous rockfalls and debris flows, two retaining wall failures, and deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Fairyland Loop trail suffered deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Navajo Loop trail had a tree downed on the Two Bridges side. The Wall Street side of the Navajo Loop Trail suffered further debris flows and complete trail erosion in some sections, resulting in an extended trail closure.
Bridge flooded and impassable on County Road 13 at Thobolocco Creek.
Broadcast media reports car stuck on Brewery Street due to flooding.
Painter Drive in West Haven closed due to flooding. Multiple underpasses around West Haven closed due to flooding.
Flash flooding on McClellan Street with traffic blocked.
Flooding on Hutchinson River Parkway northbound at Exit 9 in New Rochelle. All lanes closed.
Widespread flooding on Queens Blvd in Elmhurst.

California Highway Patrol reported significant flash flooding and mud/debris flows across Pine Canyon Road, west-northwest of Lake Hughes. Officers reported 24 vehicles stuck in mud and debris. Over 50 people had to be air lifted out of the area due to no emergency vehicle access.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud/debris flows about 3 miles south-southwest of Neenach. Several vehicles, including a fire truck, were stuck in mud. Several miles of Old Ridge Route Road were closed.
