US-95 near Milepost 69 was flooded. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
South Boundary Road of Joshua Tree National Park was closed due to flooding. All visitors were evacuated from the southern portion the park. No damages or injuries were reported.

A video showed a wash flowing across a low water crossing along Silver King Road, making the road impassable. Other videos in the Queen Valley area also showed high flow in Queen Creek. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.

ADOT reported that SR 95 was closed due to flooding near milepost 80. There were also reports of a couple of cars that attempted to cross the flooded road but were not able to make it across and had to be pulled out. No injuries were reported.

Signal Butte Road between East Germann Road and East Barnes Parkway as well as Germann Road at South Crismon Road were closed due flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
S22(Borrego-Salton roadway) was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding with water 3-4 feet deep was reported along US-95 about 14 miles south of Quartzsite. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media pictures and video showed flooding along SR-87 near Shooting Range Road. Water appeared to be several inches deep, flowing over the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video showed a car submerged from the floodwaters of Indian Bend Wash along East Starlight Way and North Hayden Road. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge near the incident showed water levels above alarm stage at 1815 MST, peaking at 4 feet (3397 cfs) at 1924 MST, and dropping below alarm stage at around 2145 MST. No injuries were reported.
Pinto Basin Road in Joshua Tree National Park was closed due to washes running over road. The water was estimated to be running 1 foot in depth over the road. No damages or injuries were reported.

Image from social media along Hackney Avenue in Globe showed a destroyed pickup truck lying along a box culvert, likely swept away by flood waters several feet deep along a wash running adjacent to the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Big Horn Pass road was closed due to flooding and debris on the roads. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based from radar.
The intersection of 4th Ave and 22nd St around the Post Office in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Caltrans closed SR-177 in both directions between I-10 and SR-62 due to flooding in multiple locations. Power lines were also down along SR-177. SR-177 was reopened around 0800PST, August 25th. Timing of flooding impacts based on radar. No injuries were reported.
Video of flash flooding on Peralta Road, east of Gold Canyon, which stranded motorists. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video showed a wash flowing across a low water crossing south of Salome on Harquahala Road, making the roadway impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Highway 78 was flooded at Milpitas Wash with debris across the road. A vehicle was reported to have been damaged by the rocks on the road. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along SR-95 northbound near the Yuma and La Paz County Line. No damages or injuries were reported.

Clatrans closed SR-78 in both directions near the I-10 interchange due to flooding. SR-78 was reopened around 0800PST, August 25th. Timing of flooding impacts estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
An image showed Ashbrook Wash running across a low water crossing along El Pueblo Boulevard north of Grande Boulevard, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along East Fork Cave Creek Wash near North 7th Avenue in Phoenix indicated water levels rising above alarm stage at 2232 MST, with the flow peaking 3.77 feet (1557 cfs) at 2259 MST, and not going below alarm stage until 2359 MST. This likely made North 7th Avenue impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.

Photos from the La Paz County Public Works showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to extensive flooding from overflowing washes that intersect the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
MCDOT reported that Patton Road between 195th Avenue and 203rd Avenue was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

Separate social media videos showed water from Fortuna Wash flowing over S Ave 14 1/2 E and E 48th Street, causing the streets to become impassable. Most of the rain, estimated around 1 to 2 inches fell over the headwaters of Fortuna Wash, 3 to 5 miles to the southeast of Fortuna Foothills. No damages or injuries were reported.
SR-238 was closed entirely from Gila Bend to SR 347 due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Multiple road closures due to flooding were reported in Aguila from the Flood Control District of Maricopa County. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video showed running flood waters, several inches in depth, in the intersection of North Tatum Road and East Doubletree Ranch Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Picture shows Russell Rd near Utility St impassable due to flash flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Ogilby Road closed near the intersection with Sidewinder Road due to flooding. Vehicles were stranded between two washes pushing sediment and debris onto roadways. No injuries were reported.
Tyson wash was reported to hit 12 feet deep with debris. No damages or injuries were reported.

Videos showed washes overflowing in Fountain Hills, with water moving across Golden Eagle Park and then downstream over North El Pueblo Boulevard. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported that Eagle Eye Road was closed between Aguila Road and Mile Post 0 due to flooding. Timing and location of impacts was adjusted based on radar. There were no reports of damage.
Flooding was reported along SR-95 Northbound near Cyprus Mine Road. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video showed Arizona Department of Public Safety performed a swift water rescue by air around 2100MST. A family of 6 (2 parents and 4 kids) in an SUV were washed off of Val Vista Road near Warren Road at a low water crossing with Vekol Wash. Floodwaters were over the hood of the SUV after being pushed downstream. All 6 individuals were safely rescued from the roof of their vehicle and were unharmed. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge on Vekol Wash near I-8, located approximately 14 miles southwest, showed the flow going above alarm stage at 1340 MST, peaking at 7.80 feet (2465 cfs) at 1540 MST, and returning below alarm stage at 1754 MST. A news article mentioned this was the second swift water rescue performed in a matter of a few hours. Details on the other rescue were not found.
SR-177, just north of Desert Center, was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
A park employee with Joshua Tree National Park share video and report of roads washed out in the Indian Cove section of the park. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based on radar.
SR-72 at Milepost 25 near Bouse was impassable due to wash flowing over the roadway. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

The City of Queen Creek posted on social media at 2140MST saying Rittenhouse Road near Ocotillo Road was closed due to flooding. Timing of impacts based around radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Ogilby Rd was closed due to flood debris and a road washout. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
East County 14th Street in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on SR-87 Northbound near N Fort McDowell Rd (MP 191). No damages or injuries were reported.
Water, rocks, and debris were reported across Hwy 95 north of Blythe. No injuries were reported.
Video from broadcast of media showed water and debris flowing over roadway off of Grand Ave & Jomax near Wittman. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Interstate-10, a major throughway between Phoenix, AZ and Southern California, had a section of the two eastbound (EB) lanes fully washed out due to flash flooding. Video during the washout appear to show the drainage pipes under the road were overcome and compromised by the magnitude of floodwaters. Radar rainfall estimates in this area were around 2-3 inches, with much of the rain falling in less than 2 hours. The washout occurred a few miles east of State Route 177/Desert Center. Caltrans closed I-10 EB due to the washout. I-10 westbound (WB) was also closed briefly due to an overturned semi-truck and SR-177 had already been closed, due to its own separate flooding impacts and downed power lines, by the time of the I-10 washout. This caused major traffic delays and detours through Eastern Riverside County. One EB detour lane was opened around 0700PST on August 25th after emergency construction and the second EB detour lane was not opened until 2300PST August 27th. Timing of flooding impacts based on radar. No injuries were reported from this event.

The Surprise Emergency Manager said there was significant flash flooding in the Asante Community, with evidence of water over the roads. The Emergency Manager also shared there was significant mud and runoff at a water treatment plant near 29 Palms RV Park. On social media there were several reports of at least minor street flooding around the area as well. Timing of impacts estimated from radar. No reports of damage or injuries from flooding.
Flooding reported along the entrance ramp at Princess Drive onto the Loop 101 in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along US-60 near milepost 75. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding on roadway near the intersection of North Via Linda and East Via de Ventura in Scottsdale. No damages or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Sols Wash exceeded alarm stage, making a low water crossing along Vulture Mine Road impassable. At 0424MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 3.65 feet and a flow of 3,822 CFS. A social media video showed Sols Wash flowing across Vulture Mine Road and Wickenburg dispatch reported the road was closed as a result of the flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

Flow in Centennial Wash caused a low water crossing along Centennial Park Road to become impassable. An RV attempted to cross the flooded roadway but was swept off the road. Images also showed damage to the roadway from the flooding. No injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on SR-72, west of McVay Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Report from La Paz County Emergency Management of water rushing into houses. Washes in the area were running full. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Baseline Rd in the Palo Verde region was closed between Johnson Rd and 331st Ave due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Video showed Cactus Park in Scottsdale flooded with multiple feet of standing water. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video showed Bloody Tanks Wash in major elevated stage as it was flowing down the city of Miami. No damages or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Delaney Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along 411th Avenue. At 2139MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 2.94 feet and a flow of 426 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

Several incidents occurred between the Mountain Springs and Ocotillo area due to flash flooding. Large rocks were reported falling onto I-8. Significant water flow was reported along Meyer Creek wash, resulting in several roads which intersect the wash to become impassable. Highway 98 was closed between Imperial Highway and Drew Road due to the flooding. A mesonet station in Mountain Spring reported 2.67 inches with 1.02 inches falling in one hour. No injuries were reported.
About 6 inches approximately of flowing water was observed across Dolphin Drive in Salton City. No damages or injuries were reported.
Images showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to high flow over low water crossings. Timing and exact location estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on the southbound lanes of SR-87 near Milepost 180. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Cave Creek exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings such as Canyon Creek Road. At 1809MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 6.89 feet and a flow of 3,670 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

A video showed Flying E Wash flowing across a low water crossing along Vulture Mine Road, making the roadway impassable. An upstream FCDMC streamflow gage along the wash exceeded alarm stage, peaking at a depth of 1.77 feet and a flow of 269 CFS at 1858MST. No damage or injuries were reported.
Highway 78 near Milepost 53 was flooded, with multiple vehicles stuck in the floodwaters. No damages or injuries were reported.

Flood Control District of Maricopa County stream gage along Jackrabbit Wash exceeded alarm stage at 2236 MST, making the Vulture Mine Road low water crossing impassable and mostly likely Wickenburg Road, located 5 miles downstream. Flow peaked at 3.35 feet and 1034 CFS at 2305 MST and dropped below alarm stage at 2340 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

Broadcast video showed a lady stuck at a skate park located along the Indian Bend Wash near McDowell Road in Scottsdale. Rescuers unable to get to her for a couple of hours at least due to the flood waters of several feet along the wash. An aerial rescue was performed around 2215 MST. Just 2 miles upstream along the wash near Indian School Road, a Flood County District of Maricopa County gauge reported water levels going above alarm stage after 1830 MST, rising to a record stage of 5.76 feet (3929 cfs) at around 1907 MST. The water level did not go below flood stage until several hours after, at 230 MST on the 13th. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video images from social media showed raging flood waters occurring near Salome Highway just east of US-60. Timing estimated from radar. In addition, the Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge located along Centennial Wash in Wenden showed water levels rising above alarm stage at around 1950 MST, peaking at 3.37 feet (1323 cfs) at around 2034 MST and not going below alarm stage until around 2330 MST. The impacted areas from Centennial Wash include Salome Road, which is located about 4.8 miles downstream of the gauge location in Wenden. No damages or injuries were reported.

Several roads that intersect Waterman Wash in the Rainbow Valley/Buckeye area were impassable/closed due to flooding. This included Riggs Road, Tuthill Road between between Pecos Road and Fairview Street, and Narramore Road between Dean Road and Airport Road. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge of Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road reported a peak flow of 6.12 feet (1151 cfs), which was 2.82 feet above alarm stage. No damages or injuries were reported.

SR-238 was closed in its entirety between Gila Bend and SR-347 due to significant flooding. The Maricopa Fire and Medical Crew as well as the Goodyear Fire Department in a collective effort had to rescue approximately 32 people in stranded vehicles. No injuries were reported.

A video showed a flood wave traveling down Pinal Creek in Six Shooter Canyon before overtopping a bridge along Six Shooter Canyon Road. Flood waters could be seen traveling down the road making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Washes were reported to be running across SR 72 and McVay Road, causing impacts to the roadways. No damage or injuries were reported.
Multiple instances of flooding were reported along SR 95 south of Quartzsite, impacting travel on the roadway. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along SR-95 Northbound near Blevens Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
SR-238 was completely closed between Gila Bend and SR-347 due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
SR 95 north of Quartzsite was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge of Jackrabbit Wash at Vulture Mine Road reported water levels rising rapidly above alarm stage at around 1713 MST, with a peak flow of 4.88 feet (3651 cfs) at 1803 MST, and going back down below alarm stage at around 1926 MST. This amount of water flow likely flooded Aguila Road upstream of the gauge and Wickenburg Road, where a water rescue was performed, located 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No injuries were reported. Based on the report from the Phoenix Dispatch, water got halfway up on an unoccupied vehicle stuck along the flood waters from Jackrabbit Wash located along Wickenburg Road.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Columbus Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings along Highline Road and 579th Avenue. At 0110MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 3.57 feet and a flow of 322 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.
A low water crossing on Pima Road south of Legend Trail Parkway became impassable due to a wash flowing approximately one foot in depth over the roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.
Box Canyon Road near I-10 was closed due to flooding. Vehicle with two occupants was stranded in the flood water. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along Loop-101 near East Cactus Road in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Jackrabbit Wash just downstream of North Vulture Mine Road indicated water levels rising above the alarm stage of 2.9 feet at 1800 MST. The flow peaked at 5.70 feet (6000 cfs) at around 1910 MST. Impacted area included Wickenburg Road, located about 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video showed Indian Bend Wash running multiple feet deep, resulting in a car nearly submerged by the running flood waters along McCormick Parkway in Scottsdale. The person inside the vehicle had to be rescued by the Fire Department. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard, located about 3 miles upstream of the incident showed peak flow of 2.92 feet (1875 cfs), which was above alarm stage, at 1640 MST. Additional flow of just over 1000 cfs was likely added to the wash from the Berneil Wash, located about 1 mile upstream of the incident. The gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard did not go below alarm stage until just after 2015 MST. No injuries were reported.
MCDOT reported that Centennial Road between 517th Avenue and 555th Avenue was closed due to flooding in Centennial Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
Three to four pickup trucks were stuck in the wash on Dunaway Road near I-8, causing the closure of the road. A vehicle was washed off Evan Hawes Highway. No injuries were reported.
Highway 78 east of Ocotillo Wells was closed due to flooding and debris on the road. No injuries were reported.

Between 1 and 3 inches of rain fell within 1-2 hours across Apache Junction and the adjacent higher terrain north and east of the city, towards the Goldfield and Superstitions mountains. Water from those mountains drained down towards the area washes, including Weekes Wash, which runs through the city. Numerous roads were flooded and damaged along with multiple water rescues taking place of residents in homes that either were surrounded with water or had water inside them. One of the more dramatic water rescues occurred when a woman had to be rescued from her vehicle that was swept away by the flood waters of Weekes Wash and traveled half a mile downstream before encountering a box culvert. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding between mileposts 7-23. No damage or injuries were reported.
MCDOT reported that Salome Road was closed between I-10 and milepost 22 due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Centennial Wash near the Railroad area reached action stage at 954 MST, with a peak flow of 10.12 feet (1341 cfs) at 1112 MST. Flash Flood impacts downstream where Centennial Wash crosses old U.S. 80 occurred 1.5 hours after action stage was reached, which is 6 miles downstream of the gauge. The flow returned below alarm stage at 1507 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
North Imperial Avenue between Adams Avenue and East Main Street in El Centro was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
SR-238 closed between Milepost 4 and 24 due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

Ralston Road at the Vekol Wash low water crossing in Ak-Chin Village was flooded and was impassable for several hours. Peak floodwater height was measured at nearly 7 feet at around 1951 MST by the Pinal County Flood Control gauge at the crossing. Timing estimated based off when the water level first reached 1 feet deep. No damages or injuries were reported.
Tonopah Salome Highway in Tonopah was closed between 315th Ave and 327th Dr due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

Two periods of heavy rain, each of 1 across much of the watershed, which was part of the Bighorn Fire burn scar, caused Sabino Creek to overtop bridges at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area. Some hiking trails, which were affected by high flows earlier in the month, sustained additional damage.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in the vicinity of Davis-Monthan AFB caused flash flooding and the closure of nearby roads including Contractors Way.

One inch of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding near State Route 83 in the Lyle and Brushy Canyon areas south of Canelo. Two occupants of a pickup truck were rescued from three feet of flowing water.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 2 hours over the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding in San Manuel and nearby areas with several dirt roads washed out.
Heavy rain of 1.5 on the Bighorn burn scar caused rapid rises in Finger Rock Wash. Road closures resulted near Havasu Rd and Columbus Blvd and Pontatoc Rd. south of Skyline Dr.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour fell upstream to north of the Catalina Mountains in Pinal County. The Canada Del Oro Wash flowed over its banks south of Edwin Rd.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 2-3 hours caused Old Ajo Hwy. and West Snyder Hill Rd. north of Ryan Field to be closed due to flash flooding.

Very heavy rainfall fell over Macho Creek in western Duval County with radar estimates showing 8 to 15 inches of rainfall. Flood waters rose on Macho Creek and moved into the community of Realitos. Two homes on south Cadena Street between Highway 359 and Adkins Street had water up to the window sills. Around 20 people were evacuated, with some of them going to a shelter in Benavides. Multiple agencies responded to the rescue effort.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding in southern Tucson. Swift water rescues from vehicles occurred near Bilby Rd. and Nogales Highway and Valencia Rd. and Park Ave.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in Saguaro National Park and damage to Bajada Loop Rd.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 southeast of Valencia and Mission Rds. caused the West Branch of the Santa Cruz River to flood Drexel Road, causing its closure.

Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Davis Rd. east of Route 80 north of Bisbee. Flash flooding also occurred in Tombstone with the road washed out at the intersection of Ave. De La Loma & S. Laguna Ave.
Heavy rain of 1.5 to 3 inches in less than 3 hours caused flash flooding along Empire Ranch Rd.

Heavy rain of 2-2.5 in less than 90 minutes northeast of town caused flash flooding in St. David, mainly southwest of State Route 80, although the highway was closed due to flooding for a period of time. A total of 53 homes sustained at least some flood damage. A homeowner with a basement reported flood water hit a depth of 6 feet, destroying a new furnace and damaging electrical wiring. Floodwaters also affected septic tanks and wells.
Images showed Beer Tree Crossing barricaded due to Pinal Creek running across the road. Other images also showed Walliman Road was impassable due to flooding across the roadway.
Heavy rain of 1-2' in 1 hour in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise in Nogales Wash. The Doe St. bridge was overtopped and nearby roadways were flooded.
Heavy rain of 3-4 in three hours caused flash flooding and road closures in Green Valley, including Camino Del Sol and Abrego Drive.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in southwest Tucson. Roads closed include Old Ajo Highway, Long Cast DR. and Iberia Ave.
Heavy rain of 3-5 in 2 hours in the Chiricahua Mountains caused high flows on Turkey Creek. Fort Bowie Rd. was washed out well downstream.

Heavy rain of more than 1 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and closures of residential streets south of Orange Grove Road between La Cholla and La Canada. Additionally, a man was rescued after becoming trapped under a bridge by floodwaters near Blacklidge and Walnut.
Heavy rain of 1-2' in less than 1 hour caused the flooding of Magee Rd. east of La Canada Dr. at Pegler Wash and the closure of Ina Rd. at Pima Wash east of Oracle Rd.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 1 hour caused urban washes to flow over roadways from midtown to southeast Tucson. One person was washed downstream in the Columbus Wash near Blacklidge Dr. but was able to get themselves to safety. A young woman was rescued from her car which was stuck in Arcadia Wash near Pima and Rosemont. Kolb Rd. was closed between Irvington and Valencia while Irvington Rd. was closed due to flooding at the Atterbury Wash.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 on Tucson's southeast side caused localized flash flooding. Escalante Rd. was closed at the Atterbury Wash and a man was rescued from his vehicle in the Alamo Wash at Yale Dr.

The Bouse Fire Department reported washes were running along SR-72 near Bouse, resulting in difficult access as well as the closure of several sections of the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed North Trekell Road just south of W Hopi Drive flooded with water flowing down the road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flood water over Kortsen Road and SR-347. No damages or injuries were reported.
Report received through Mping of yards being flooded along with waters flooding a basement near Ennis Joslin Road to the west northwest of the Naval Air Station.
Emergency manager reported street flooding in area around McKinzie Road and Leopard Street to Interstate 37 where the right two lanes were flooded.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in Oracle caused extensive street flooding throughout the town.
Emergency manager reported street flooding across the city from Flour Bluff to southeast Corpus Christi to Midtown to the Bayfront area.

Harbor Bridge construction project crews temporarily closed the Port Avenue and Nueces Bay Boulevard exits to Martin Luther King Drive and the northwest loop ramp connecting to southbound Crosstown Expressway in downtown Corpus Christi.
Public reported street flooding in the southeast part of Laredo.
Farm to Market Road 624 southeast of Cotulla had flood waters covering the road.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 1 hour east of Saint David caused flash flooding in town. Homes were flooded near Cottonwood and Miller Lanes.

Heavy rain of 2-3 at the headwaters of Sabino Creek and Bear Canyon caused rapid rises in both streams. Flash flooding occurred at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area causing damage to trails and flooding of all recreation area bridges. Twenty five people became stranded in Bear Canyon and needed to be rescued as trails across the wash were flowing heavily and dangerously impassable. No injuries were reported.
Post on Twitter was received of flooded waters on roadways reaching car bumpers from Flour Bluff to Rodd Field Road.
Report received from Mping of flooded streets with vehicles stranded along South Padre Island Drive between Rodd Field Road and Staples Street in Corpus Christi.
Snapchat video showed flooded underpass near Zapata Highway and North Arkansas Avenue in southeast Laredo.
Houses were flooded near Barrios Street and near Arkansas Avenue in southeast Laredo.
Flood waters entered homes in northwest Laredo.
Corrects previous flash flood report from 2 SW Moores Mill. Subdivision on Lamirda Court NW of Countess Road near Meridianville is flooded. A few homes had water approaching or in them.
Upstream heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 2 hours caused Canada Del Oro Wash to flood part of N Lago Del Oro Parkway, resulting in its closure.
Reports of Flash Flooding along Bob Wade Lane West of 231/431 and East of Research Park Boulevard.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 2 hours fell across the Rincon Mountains causing rises in Tanque Verde Creek that caused road closures of Wentworth Rd. and Tanque Verde Loop Rd.
Rodd Field Road south of SPID became flooded and impassible with flood waters. Report by NWS employee of stalled cars with water up to the windows in spots.
Emergency manager reported street flooding at Everhart Road and McArdle Road in Corpus Christi.
Water was over the roads near Loma Alta.
Several people were rescued from flooded homes in a low lying area in southeast Laredo.
Emergency manager reported street flooding at Tarlton Street and Blanc Courts near downtown Corpus Christi.
Emergency manager reported access roads on Interstate 37 were flooded near Labonte Park.
Public reported flooding of streets in northeast part of Laredo.
Public report received of streets flooded on the northwest side of Laredo.
Report received through social media of Interstate 35 flooded south of Encinal.

CHP law enforcement reported a wash flowing across CA 177, north-northeast of Desert Center. One of their patrol vehicles sustained damage trying to get through to an accident. No injuries were reported.

At 9:48 am on 9/29, the public reported flooding on Avenida Menendez Blvd and the closure of the Bridge of Lions. due to storm surge and fresh-water rainfall flooding in St. Augustine. At 11:02 am on 9/29, emergency management reported flash flood water was entering homes about 2 miles NW of St. Augustine. At 11:10 am, flood water was over Kings Street in St. Augustine. At 11:13 pm, a public reported of storm total Ian rainfall in Elkton was 9.51 inches.

Flash flooding was reported in Palm Coast around midday on Sept. 29th due to heavy rainfall from Hurricane Ian. Storm surge was also rising along the coast and extended into inland estuaries which caused limited drainage where heavy rainfall occurred. Around 1:30 pm, the gage at Haw Creek Russell Landing rose to 6.56 ft above datum and much of this rise was due to heavy rainfall.
Video showed I-17 southbound at Indian School Road under about a foot of water with law enforcement having to push a stalled vehicle out. No injuries were reported.

The FCDMC streamflow gage along 4th of July Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along Agua Caliente Road. The gage peaked at a depth of 0.74 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.

La Paz County Dispatch reported the following roadways were closed due to flooding from water overflowing from Tyson Wash: Tyson Street, North Washington Avenue from Quail Trail to Kenoyer Streets, and Plymouth Road. at Mockingbird St. No damages or injuries were reported.

Cruff Wash streamflow gauge reached bank full with peak flow of 1000 cfs and a rapid 3.75 foot rise. A low water crossing along Agua Caliente Rd was likely impacted. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gage along East Fork Cave Creek exceeded alarm stage, peaking at a height of 2.15 feet and a flow of 473 cfs and impacting a downstream low water crossing along 7th Avenue. No damage or injuries were reported.
A video showed a wash flowing over a low water crossing along 48th Street, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Salome Hwy between 331st Ave to 355th Ave was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

A video on social media showed a large amount of mud and rock debris across a low water crossing along Onyx Avenue near 42nd Street, indicating high flow in Tatum Wash earlier in the morning had made the road impassable. Further downstream along 40th Street near Mission Lane, another video indicated flow in the wash climbed high enough to overtop a bridge, partially pushing a guardrail over and leaving mud and small debris on the bridge. No injuries were reported.
Reports of Roadways underwater at the intersection of Mill Road and County Line Road. Depth of water unknown.
The Acadian Thruway underpass was closed due to high water.
Water was flowing across several streets in Flora.
Water was 1 to 2 feet deep on some streets in Pana.
US-45 was flooded south of Watson near Salt Creek.
Video of water rushing down Wixon Pond Road and East Lake Blvd in Carmel, NY.
The public reported water, rocks and gravel running across Twin Lakes Road near the Handsome Eddy Road intersection due to culvert being blown out by flood waters.
Multiple reports of vehicles stranded in Wallace were received.
Flash flooding on the Nesowadnehunk Stream flooded the Park Tote Road with 8 to 10 inches of running water. The road was closed for several hours until the flash flooding subsided.
Flooding occurred on Raintree and Gum Branch Roads, with vehicles stranded in water.

Public reported a washout on Goodrich Road near Jackson Brook. Minor washout on Murray Street near McLaughlin Lane. Radar estimated 1 to 3 inches of rain fell across the Bingham Area in the course of an hour and a half.

Heavy rain moved into Cheshire County around 8 PM with rainfall rates peaking around 4 inches an hour. In Walpole, Great Brook came out of banks and flooded Old Keene Road near Mill Road and damaged agricultural property off Watkins Hill Road.

During the afternoon and evening of April 12th, prolific rainfall occurred across southern and central metro Broward County, including the cities of Fort Lauderdale, Hollywood, Dania Beach, and Wilton Manors. Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly training over this urban corridor brought multiple hours with rainfall rates of 3-6 inches/hour, with total rainfall of 15-25 inches between Noon and Midnight. The highest measured rainfall amount was 25.91 at a WeatherSTEM gauge at Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, with 20 inches falling between 4 and 10 PM. This rainfall rate has less than a 0.1% chance of being exceeded in any given year, and the rainfall over most of the Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood areas has an annual exceedance probability of no more than 0.5%. ||This extremely rare rainfall led to devastating impacts and crippled neighborhoods for several days. Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport was closed for nearly 40 hours due to high standing water. Over 1,100 buildings in Fort Lauderdale suffered damage, with 766 having major damage. Fort Lauderdale City Hall sustained major water damage and was considered a complete loss. At least 38,000 cubic yards of debris was collected in Fort Lauderdale. The city of Hollywood Waste Water plant sustained damage. Damage surveys revealed high water marks of over 3 feet inside homes in the Edgewood and Melrose Park neighborhoods of Fort Lauderdale, with 1-2 feet of standing water and high water marks in sections of Dania Beach and Hollywood. About 600 residents were displaced by the flood, with many being rescued from their homes by first responders. 22,000 residents were without power during the peak of the event, with the hardest hit areas remaining without it for days. Port Everglades, which supplies 100% of the fuel for the area (13 million gallons per day), suffered a 50% reduction in distribution due to submerged fuel pumps, with interruptions lasting over 10 days. This led to a fuel shortage across the area, with most South Florida gas stations having to close for days at a time. Nearly one thousand calls were made to local towing companies for abandoned/stranded vehicles in flooded water, with the number of vehicle insurance claims across the area in the thousands.||Damage totals were provided by Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood emergency management officials.

Heavy rain fell across Enchanted Pond just south of Jackman between 5 and 7 PM, bringing a radar estimate of 4 inches, most of which fell between 530 and 6 PM. This torrential rainfall caused a small retention pond in the hills above the lake to collapse. The resultant debris flow included uprooted trees and boulders, along with high flowing water around 3 feet deep. A campground located below the hill sustained significant damage.
Water was over the road in a couple of spots along Route T.

Flash flooding closed several roads in McCracken County. Kentucky 1255 was closed at the 1 to 2 mile marker, just west of the Kentucky 450 intersection. Harris Fork Creek was overflowing and flooding downtown Fulton. Kentucky Highway 94 was closed from the 7 to 11 mile markers in the lower bottomlands between Kentucky 311 and Kentucky 1099 due to water over the road.

Considerable flash flooding occurred in Andover on the morning of the 26th after 3 and 6 inches of rain fell along the south facing slopes of the Wyman Mountain. Abbott Brook was redirected and severely impacted Wyman Hill Road and personal property along it. At one stretch along Wyman Hill Rd, Abbott Brook was diverted and is running directly down the middle of the road. More than a dozen residents were impacted, leaving people without road access. The main bridge at Wyman Hill Rd and Cross Rd was washed out. There was also one water rescue in Andover as a vehicle got stuck in the flood waters. The runoff caused the Ellis River to climb above flood stage cresting at 17.29 feet.||Additional roads in Andover that sustained washouts were East B Hill Road and South Arm Road. The major thruway of Route 120 was closed from Route 5 to Roxbury Pond Road due to flooding out of the Ellis River.
U.S. Highway 62 experienced localized flooding between Calvert City and Possum Trot. Some side roads were covered.
Kentucky Route 1949 was closed at the 7 to 9 mile marker near the I-69 tunnel.

Flooding with severe shoulder washouts on Route 201 near Parlin Pond.
Law Enforcement reports numerous roads and intersections under water in San Angelo.

Flooding in Rockwood causing significant disruptions to travel in and out of the region. Most of the downtown village was impacted. Roads flooded include Misery Gorge and Marston, Cedar, and Village Roads.

Flooding on Route 15 west of Rockwood after heavy rain fell during the afternoon of June 29. The radar estimated rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches, most of which fell in an hour between 3 and 4 pm. Multiple significant washouts occurred.

Miami Beach Public Works reported water entering a parking garage in Mid-Beach. There were other reports of street flooding in South Beach. An estimated two to three inches of rain fell across Miami Beach with the evening thunderstorms.

Water and debris rushed across several areas of Wilson Butte Road resulted in damage and impacts. Water flowed out of the rockier boulder terrain on the east side of the road, crossed the road with water depth being 2 to 3 feet deep at times. Water and debris entered at least two homes. One culvert was completely washed out with drainage pipes unearthed. Some wheat crops were flattened. NWS Employee that lives along the road had water enter their basement. Wilson Butte Road was impassable for approximately an hour.
Law enforcement reported flooding near Rapelje.
Moorhead Road was washed out at Plum Creek.
Red Lodge Creek and Willow Creek were reported flooded.
Carbon County Emergency Manager reported a debris flow on Grove Creek on the Robertson Draw Burn Scar.
Approximately 6 inches of water running over a low spot near the intersection of County Road 75.2 and 25. 3.25 inches of rain were also reported less than 5 miles from this location.

Widespread road closures due to flash flooding in Willoughby, Eastlake, and Willowick. Multiple water rescues conducted due to vehicles driving into flooded roadways. Road closures in this area included US-2 near Stevens Boulevard, Vine Street just east of US-2, Riverside Boulevard and Riverside Drive, and Lake Shore Boulevard near Vine Street. Radar estimated 2.25 to 3 inches of rainfall in a three to four hour period, with 1 to 1.5 inches of rain falling in the hour immediately preceding the flash flooding.

Fergus County Sheriff's Office and Emergency Management reported portions of Casino Creek Road washed out from heavy rain and flooding of the creek. The road was washed out completely in at least two locations, per a later NWS survey. Many cattle fields along the creek were also flooded.
Several roads in Lower Macungie Township became impassable due to flooding. There was a water rescue from a stranded vehicle at Church Lane and Oak Drive.
A little more than 4 miles of state highway 80 was closed between Hon and Anderson due to flash flooding.
Runoff from torrential rainfall caused water to go over the road in a low spot. Depth was approximately six inches.
Social media report of water flowing over Highway 25 near the intersection of County Road Z.
Fergus County Sheriff's Office reported portions of Cottonwood Creek Road washed out from flooding.

Portions of N Creek Road as well as Highway 12 were closed due to debris flows and flash flooding in the Deep Creek Burn Scar area. The Deep Creek Picnic area was closed for over two months as a result of the flooding.
Social media video showing 1-3 feet of flowing water across the road near the intersection of West Rainey Street and West Main Street.

A concentrated area of 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across southern Franklin County during the afternoon of June 29th into the early evening hours. Between 400 pm and 700 pm, a stalled thunderstorm brought 2 to 3 inch per hour rainfall rates which peaked between 430 pm and 600 pm where most of the rain fell. These rains fell across previously saturated soils and hilly terrain. The heaviest rain fell in Jay. An additional 17 roads in surrounding communities of Wilton, Farmington, and Chesterville sustained partially wash-outs or road closures from flooding. In nearby Wilton, ME-156 at Soules Hill Road and Whittier Roads sustained washouts.
Sprague Street in Jamestown was flooded.
Allen Street in Falconer closed due to flooding.

Widespread flash flooding leading to road closures in Willoughby Hills and Waite Hill. Flooded roadways include Milann Drive, River Road near Beech Hills Drive, River Road near Rivera Ridge Road, Chagrin Drive, and Trailard Drive. Radar estimated 2.25 to 3 inches of rainfall in a three to four hour period, with 1 to 1.5 inches of rain falling in the hour immediately preceding the flash flooding.
Law enforcement in Laredo reported a few streets flooded on the north side of Laredo with one car stranded.
Flooding lead to a water rescue on the US Route 30 eastbound ramp onto US Route 202 northbound in West Whiteland Township.
Highway 336 was flooded in Thaxton.

In Newport, stormwater flooded the drainage system on Sand Hill Road, washing away about 150 feet of the dirt road. The washout affected a handful of homeowners who lived on the dead-end portion of the road. A half-dozen other roads, including Fletcher Road and a portion of Maple Street, also were also washed away.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Corser Brook Road in Errol.

Grantham Mountain Road in Meriden, N.H. nearing the intersection with Route 120 was washed out in the afternoon of the 17th. The flood washed out over 300 feet of road material, including asphalt, with crevices of as much as 10-feet deep in some places. Radar estimated about 3 inches of rain fell between 2:30 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. The rain flooded Bloods Brook, which runs parallel to Grantham Mountain Road before entering a large culvert, approximately 4 feet in diameter, that passes underneath the road. The culvert was overwhelmed and the road subsequently damaged.
Vehicular high water rescue on Caddo Street between McNeil Street and Louisiana Avenue in downtown Shreveport.

Vehicular high water rescue near Devaughn Street and Rightway Avenue at the underpass along Hearne Avenue in Shreveport. One person was rescued, but a second person was trapped in the same vehicle and drowned.

Flash flooding in and around Wellington. Lorain County Fairgrounds inundated with more than a foot of standing water, flooding cars and livestock trailers in the fairgrounds parking area, and several barns on the fairground property. Some basement flooding reported in Wellington. OH-18 closed west of Wellington between Oh-511 and Quarry Road and east of Wellington between Hawley Road and West Road. Radar estimated 3 to 4 inches of rainfall in a three hour period.

Numerous roads were flooded throughout the county. Water was over a number of state roads, including Kentucky Routes 1453, 115, 1026, 1663, 1386, 164, and 272. A vehicle carrying five occupants (4 juveniles and an adult female) went into chest high water near the intersection of Buffalo Rd and Gracey Sinking Fork Rd. A rescue operation was performed, removing all of the occupants from the vehicle. The 68-year-old female driver was found to have died as a result of drowning.
Pond Brook surged out of banks and onto Pond Brook Drive near Chamberlain Way.

Heavy rainfall estimated by radar between 2 and 3 inches fell during the early afternoon of June 17. In Croydon several roads were flooding including Brighton Road, Winter Road and Croydon Brook Road. Croydon Brook Road sustained washouts.
Social media image showing water flowing across portions of Lee Boulevard near Interstate 44.
Vehicular high water rescue reported near the Pines Road on-ramp to Interstate 20 westbound in Shreveport.
Vehicular high water rescue reported at Hudson Avenue and Regent Street in Shreveport.
Runoff from torrential rainfall caused water to go over the road in a low spot. Depth was approximately six inches.

Widespread flash flooding across northern Lorain County due to heavy rainfall. Widespread basement and isolated first floor flooding reported in Lorain, Elyria, Amherst, Avon Lake, Avon, and North Ridgeville. Widespread flooded roadways reported. Post event damage assessments reported hundreds of homes and businesses flooded. Radar estimated rainfall of 3 to 4 inches falling in a three hour period, which matched several measured rain gauge reports from the area.

The Newfound River came out of its banks after 4 to 6 inches of rainfall in the early morning hours of the 26th. Pleasant Street in Bristol sustained a washout, with 4 feet of sand and gravel piled into intersection of Lake Street by floodwaters. Numerous roads washed out elsewhere in the community with culverts exposed and pavement collapsed, including Plummer Hill, Matthews Rd, Burns Hill, Foster Pond, and King Rd.

A BNSF Railroad track inspector reported multiple locations of track subgrade material completely washed out along a half mile stretch of railroad in Hinsdale. Subgrade material was washed onto US Highway 2, closing the highway for a time. Train traffic was suspended until repairs could be made.
A trained spotter reported water over gravel roads in several locations west of Hinsdale.
Public reported water running down numerous streets and area roads.
A trained spotter reported 2.3 inches of rainfall in a short period of time. Numerous fields were reported as flooding.
Public reported, via Facebook, water running over Edwards Road.
Flooding was reported in a lower water crossing with two high-water rescues.

Widespread, extensive flash flooding in Cleveland, Lakewood, Rocky River, Westlake, and Bay Village. Interstate 90 flooded with several feet of water with multiple water rescues on both eastbound and westbound lanes near the McKinley Avenue exit. Lakeshore Boulevard and Martin Luther King Boulevard closed due to flooding in Cleveland, with multiple cars stranded in high water. Extensive basement flooding in Rocky River, Lakewood, and Bay Village. Radar estimated 1.5 to 2.25 inches of rainfall in less than three hours, with much of the rainfall falling in less than one hour.

A cluster of thunderstorms moved over Salem between 3 and 430 pm. An unofficial weather station recorded rainfall up to 4.25 inches in the area with instantaneous rates peaking around 4 inches per hour. The rapid runoff over this urban area resulted in a foot of water on Route 28, disrupting the evening commuter traffic.
High water reported on several city streets and four cars submerged in downtown Shreveport.
Report of flooding relayed via mPing.

Flash flooding occurred within the Ocala city limits from about 5-6 inches of rainfall during the morning hours during about a 3 hour accumulation period. The first flash flood report to the NWS was at 9:42 am when Marion county dispatch reported that 3 lanes of traffic were closed on Southeast 17th Street near Southeast Lake Weir Avenue. At 10:15 am, a local newspaper reported that East Silver Springs Blvd, west of South Pine Avenue, was flooding with some portions of the road closed due to flood water. At 10:34 am, the public reported a car was stuck in flood water under bridge on U.S. Highway 441 south of Southeast 3rd Avenue. Around 3 to 4 inches of rainfall was measured in this area around the time of this report since about 8 am. Police and emergency vehicles were on scene. On 6/21 around 9:32 am, law enforcement reported that County Road 475A (SW 27th Avenue) in Ocala was closed due to flood water from SW 66th Street to SW 42nd Street.

The combination of heavy rainfall and mud and debris blocking storm drains resulted in flash flooding across the City of North Adams. Several roadways had to be shut down including Church Street, Mansion Street and River Street. Water and debris also covered portions of Ashland Street, Eagle Street and Elmwood Avenue.

Flash flooding of area creeks/streams due to heavy rainfall. Road closures reported on Fairmount Boulevard near the Chagrin River and Bishop Road near East Branch Euclid Creek due to flooding. Radar estimated 2.25 to 3.25 inches of rainfall in a three hour period, much of which fell in 90 minutes or less.
Flooding occurred on US Route 46 in Dover with sections of the roadway becoming impassable. A vehicle was stranded on NJ Route 10 in Randolph Township.
Law enforcement reported vehicles street flooding with vehicles stranded in Aransas Pass on West Nelson Avenue and Farm to Market Road 1069.
South airport road west becoming impassible due to floodwaters at LaFranier road.
Flash flooding occurred at North Highland Street and Summer Avenue.
Heavy rain over saturated ground resulted in washouts on Martins Brook Road in Wentworth. Shoulder washouts also occurred on Clifford Brook Road.
Severe washouts on Perry Road and Mountain Road in multiple locations near Dead Pond cutting off properties.

Heavy downpours fell over the hilly terrain around Alexandria New Hampshire during the overnight hours of the 26th. The heaviest rain fell around Mt. Cardigan and surrounding hills with radar estimates between 3 and 5 inches. Heavy rainfall caused flooding of several small streams including Bailey, Clark, Brock, Patten, and Bog Brooks. Much of the flood damage was from overflow of the Patten and Bog Brooks. Significant washouts and closures occurred on Bailey Road, Burns Hill Road, Plummer Hill Road, Thissel Road, Bog Road, King Road, and Town Pound Road. In Alexandria shelters were open to house displaced residents as access was cut off for hundreds of residents.

Multiple rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall overwhelmed Manchester storm drainage systems resulting in urban flooding. Flooding was reported on Green Street and Beech Street. Water up to car hoods. A report of water up to people���s knees on the intersection of Lake Avenue and Pine Street.
Flooding on NH Route 123 in Ipswich. Widespread flooding surrounding numerous businesses near Camden Court and Davis Village Road.
The downtown area of Baldwyn was heavily flooded.
High water reported across Airline Drive in Bossier City.
High water reported on Benton Road near Highway 79 in Bossier City.
Law enforcement reported water flowing over the roadway on U.S. Highway 87 at mile marker 22.
Water was observed flowing several inches deep over Woods Gap Road as Dodd Creek flooded out of its banks.
Multiple spotters reported water over road with videos. Water was estimated to be 6 inches over Highway 385 for about 100 yards.

A thunderstorm with torrential rain brought flash flooding to urban areas in southern Nashua. Unofficial weather stations in the area reported instantaneous rainfall rates between 3 and 4 inches per hour, with rainfall totals between 1.75 and 2.25 inches. The rapid runoff overflowed storm water drainage systems which had limited capacity from earlier rainfall. Water up to 2 feet deep was reported on Daniel Webster Highway.
Kings Highway just east of Interstate 49 was flooded with cars stalled out at the intersection of Kings Highway and Barrett Street.
High water reported at the intersection of Stoner Avenue and Centenary Boulevard in Shreveport.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused an area of water approximately six to ten inches deep to run over portions of Tenth Street and Silver Street in Elko. The water covered the road and went over adjacent sidewalks.

Flash flooding impacted several roads of Clarkston. Half an inch of rain fell in 15 minutes from 1330LST to 1345LST. Flooding also impacted on State Highway 129 between Asotin and Clarkston, with mud and debris on the roadway.

Flash flooding impacted several streets and avenues of Lewiston. It stalled vehicles and caused debris build up in the area. A local emergency was declared from damages sustained during the event. Half an inch of rain fell in 15 minutes from 1330LST to 1345LST.
Gaither Station Road was closed due to water over the roadway.

Portions of several roads were flooded and closed. A few vehicles were stranded in flood water.

North Travis Street and U.S. Highway 75 quickly flooded due to prolonged heavy rain. The U.S. 75 service roads also flooded.

Multiple road closures due to flash flooding in eastern Erie County, including in Vermilion and Florence Township. Main Road closed at Chappel Creek due to flooding of the creek. Sperry Road closed between OH-60 and the Erie/Lorain county line. Reports of cars stranded in flooded roadways in Vermilion. Radar estimated 3 to 3.75 inches of rainfall in a three hour period.
In Cranston, Pleasant St was flooded and impassable.
In Providence, the intersection of Francis St and West Exchange St closed due to flooding.
In Providence, Jastram St was flooded with 5 cars stuck in floodwaters.

Hillsborough St at William Moore Dr was closed due to flooding.
In North Attleborough, Chestnut St was closed due to flooding with cars stuck in the road.
In Lynnfield, Durham Dr near Grey Ln had a car stuck in street flooding.
In Greenfield, there was significant street flooding on sections of High St and Hastings Rd.
Radar estimated rainfall amounts of 3-4 inches over northern Macon County during the evening hours. County Road 57 flooded and impassable.
In Hartford, cars were stuck in flood waters on Albany Ave. Water rescues were performed.
In Providence, the corner of Valley St and Atwells Ave was flooded and impassable.
In Providence, Pawtucket Ave was flooded.
In Lincoln, there were cars stuck in flood waters.
Flooding was reported at 563 County Route 24.

Widespread flooding across western and central Erie County, including the cities of Sandusky and Huron, Margaretta Township, Perkins Township, Oxford Township, and Huron Township. Officials estimated hundreds of homes impacted by basement flooding per local media reports. Widespread road closures due to flooding. Some of the roads impacted by flooding include US-6 from the Sandusky city limits to OH-269, Homegardner Road between OH-269 and Bardshar Road, Campbell Street at Pipe Creek, Old Railroad Road at Mills Creek, Bogart Road at Pipe Creek and at Patten Tract Road, Patten Tract Road at Fox Road and Mason Road, Ransom Road at Wood Road, and Hull Avenue at Lawrence Avenue. Huron High School damaged by flooding. Animal shelter needed evacuated due to flooding. Several residents requiring evacuation near Pipe Creek near Columbus Avenue. Cars stranded in underpass on Columbus Avenue. Apartment complex flooded out in the southeast portion of the city of Sandusky. Radar estimated 3 to 4.75 inches of rainfall in a three hour period, with the highest amount along the Lake Erie shoreline from Sandusky to Huron.
Flooding near W Franklin St and Semart Dr led to road closures.
Flash flooding led to flooding along Hillsborough St near Chapel Hill Rd.
In Conway, North Poland Rd at Rt 116 was flooded up to doors of cars.

Brushy Creek overflowed Interstate 30 near FM 1565 and several cars were stuck in high water. The fast moving water swept one car off the road on the north service road and unfortunately the elderly man drowned.
State Highway D at Spencer Creek and Bank Branch was flooded and impassable.

Multiple roads were flooded and impassible by several inches of flowing water across the roadways due to slow moving thunderstorms that produced rainfall rates at 3 to 4 inches per hour. This includes flooding on Rives Road and Memorial Boulevard. The roads were reopened after flooding receded. No damage was reported.
The intersection of Melbourne Rd and Aukland Dr was closed due to flash flooding.
In Attleboro there was significant street flooding at the intersection of Newport Ave and Irving Ave.
In Swansea, there was high water across entire portion of road near the 2000 block of Rt 6.
In Fall River, a section of Country St was flooded and impassable with cars stuck in floodwaters.
In Stafford Springs, 6 to 10 inches of flood waters were observed at the intersection of Furnace Ave and River Rd.
In Stafford Springs, a tree was down on wires and a phone pole was down apparently due to saturated ground due to flooding.
In Williamsburg, Ashfield Rd was flooded up to windows of homes with rescues in progress.
In Worcester, the area of 86 Southwest was flooded with 4 cars stuck in flood waters.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed in southwest Rowan County after 4 to 5 inches fell in just a few hours. The most significant flooding was in the city of Kannapolis. A small stream inundated Mable Ave and Marie Ave near the Cabarrus County line. A tributary og Irish Buffalo Creek overflowed onto Pump Station Rd. Another stream overflowed onto West 22nd St. Farther northwest, East Fork flooded a road at the Iredell County line, while Jackson Rd and Highway 150 were inundated by Sills Creek.
In Hartford, several cars were stuck in flood waters on Scarborough St.
Flash flooding was identified around Riverview Drive and Holland Avenue. There were also flooding issues on US 60 about 1 mile east of Lewisport.
There was a vehicle stranded in flash flood waters.
Water was covering the bridge with debris in the roadway near the intersection of Mangum Dairy Rd and Brayer Hill Path.

Fire dept reported flash flooding developed along Duck Creek after 4 to 6 inches of rain fell in just a few hours along the Caldwell/Alexander County line. Two individuals were swept down the creek when they fled their vehicle after driving into flood water at Duck Creek Dr and Dover Church Rd. A 49-year old woman drowned while the other person was rescued. At least one road was washed out in the area.
Highway E at Louse Creek was flooded and impassable.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding at I-285 and Campbellton Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
Heavy rain from training thunderstorms led to flash flooding near Pennsdale, with a vehicle becoming stuck in water of unknown depth on Pond Road.
Heavy rain from training thunderstorms caused flash flooding in Washington Township, with a stretch of Route 44 near Elimsport becoming covered with water.

Multiple reports of flash flooding two miles Northwest of Winthrop. Mud and debris on road reports for West Chewuch Road, Highway 20, and Wright Road. Methow Valley Airport recorded 0.9 of an inch fell in an hour and half.
Flooding over roadway on State Route 77.
U.S. Highway 2 closed with a debris flow and damage to the asphalt and guardrail at milepost 171.

Brush Creek was flooded out of its banks at several locations by as much as 7 inches of rain falling across its headwaters. This included flooding at Brush Creek Road, Scenic Valley Road and Rich Hill Road. The bridges across Brush Creek along these roads were closed until the flood waters receded. No damage was reported to the roadways.

Building collapsed on Parrish Street extension as foundation eroded away due to flooding. Nobody was inside.

Several intersections along Battlefield Road had cars stalled in high water.

Up to a quarter of a mile of Highway 35 through Siren was covered with 6 to 10 inches of water.
Water was flowing over Highway 30A in Seaside.
Moss Hill Road was reported to be underwater.
Barricades were in place on Steele Field Road due to flooding.

A large portion of Duffy Lane was covered in water.

Bunker road was close due to flooding.
Yerkes Road was impassable due to a large volume of water rushing over the road.
A large volume of water was reported flowing across Cooley Road and Short Road with both roads impassable.
Numerous road closures reported in Canandaigua, including roads near the shoreline of Canandaigua Lake.
Minor flooding occurred along the Neshanic River and its tributaries in Raritan Township.
A member of the public reported impassable streets across Bridge City.
Widespread roadway flooding occurred in Lower Makefield Township. There were numerous road closures and water rescues.

Significant flash flooding occurred in the city of Cape Girardeau. A sport utility vehicle was swept off a roadway and into a creek. The vehicle came to rest against a pile of debris in the creek in Arena Park. The occupants safely escaped with no injuries. Elsewhere in Cape Girardeau, emergency crews responded to a water rescue when a sport utility vehicle became stalled in floodwaters. The driver was safely carried to safety. There was also some flooding in Jackson, but no major impacts were reported there. The co-operative observer at Jackson measured 5.11 inches for the total rainfall on the 18th and 19th. Most of this rainfall occurred during the flash flood on the morning of the 19th.
High water was observed in several spots in Cross Lanes, including along portions of Route 62 and Big Tyler Road.

Heavy rainfall measured around 4.5 inches caused the closure of main thruway Route 10 near Kapper Drive in Winchester on the afternoon of the 9th. An extensive washout on Route 10 required lengthy repairs to a 600 foot section of the road.

Reports from emergency managers, trained spotters, and the public of flash flooding near the US 1/Federal Highway corridor from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport south to Hallandale Beach. Many streets had standing water with vehicles stalled, and water rising into homes in Hollywood along 16th Avenue south of Hollywood Boulevard. County road 30 closed due to flooding. Evacuations occurring at the Happiness House on Independence Lane.

Numerous streets were flooded throughout Princeton. Radar estimates indicated around two inches fell in 45 minutes.

Buffalo street and surrounding streets are impassable due to flooding.
Residents are kayaking on Arlington Park and Dorset Drive in flooded roadways.

Numerous roads were flooded, with some reported as impassable.

Several roads with deep standing water or water flowing through town. A car was stalled on one of the roads.

Washout of Coon Hollow Rd. due to flooding.
Debris and boulders due to flooding on Richburg Hill Road. Additional flooding in Bolivar on Prospect Street, Salt Rising Road and Pleasant Valley Road.

Water covering roads and entering homes near Downtown Huntsville.

Heavy rainfall caused extensive flooding of roadways in the Toledo metro area. Some flooded locations included Secor Road near Sylvania Avenue and also south of Central Avenue, and portions of Interstate 475. NWS Employee reported the disc gold course along Dry Creek was under several feet of moving water. Received numerous public reports that Dry Creek had breached its banks and is overflowing into nearby areas.
Received report via Facebook of numerous dirt roads under water along with overflowing drainage ditches.
Portions of Douglass Road washed out near Pettus Road. Report relayed via media. Time estimated based on radar.
Water over the roadway at Orville Smith Road and English Elm Road. Report relayed via social media. Depth of water estimated at 6-8.
Morrow-Woodville Road was closed west of Ghiels Carroll Road due to rushing water.

State Route 104 closed in Mexico between Emery Road and Standpipe Road due to flooding.

In Springfield, there was 3 feet of water in a basement along El Paso St. Blunt Park Rd was impassable with cars stuck. Carew St was closed with 4 feet of water.
Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches led to the closure of Brush Valley Road between Schock and Tressler roads in Rockefeller Township due to flash flooding.
Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches led to the closure of Route 61 between Highland Avenue in Sunbury and Green Street in Upper Augusta Township due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain led to the washout of a roadway between Tuscarora Township and Mifflintown.
Heavy rainfall estimated around 3 inches caused flash flooding east of Sunbury, with emergency responders conducting a water rescue on Plum Creek Road.
Reports of several streets flooded and impassable in Tiffin. Radar estimated rainfall of 1.25 to 2 inches fell in a 45 to 60 minute period.
Heavy rain flooded a parking lot east of North Broadway Street in Portland, causing one truck to stall.
The intersection of Lorene Street and Junction City Road was flooded in ankle deep water.
The eastbound lane of Strong Highway was flooded.

Moderate to major flooding occurred along the East Branch of the Brandywine Creek in West Bradford Township and East Bradford Township. The flooding resulted in the closure of a section of US Route 322.
At least 6 inches of water was flowing across the 2300 block o Ruth Avenue, with cars unable to drive on the roadway.
Flowing water covered Kent Dairy Road and made it impassable. Radar estimated rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches fell over a short period of time.
Heavy rainfall between 3 and 5 inches caused a washout on Waterford Road in Norway.
Flooding due to a debris filled culvert was impacting two homes in the area.
Heavy Rain.
Roads around Highway 107 near Kolin were flooded from heavy rain.

Heavy rainfall led to flash flooding of roads, a park, and a residential area in Thompsontown. There was also damage to the local fire station that included the kitchen, restroom, a meeting room, and a truck bay.

Heavy rain near Watertown, southeast of Lebanon, caused minor flooding in the area. Flooding began in the Shop Springs area with several roads in the area closed. The heavy rain and flooding then flowed northward closer to I-40, forcing the closure of Bluebird Road at Tuckers Crossroads. No damages are known.

Widespread roadway flooding and road closures occurred in Muhlenberg Township. PA Route 12 was impassable and closed between PA Route 61 and North Fifth Street. US Route 222 was under water at the PA Route 61 underpass. A house collapsed on Mount Laurel Road along Laurel Run due to basement flooding and the eventual failure of the foundation. The residents needed to be rescued as the house was surrounded by flood waters.
Moderate flooding occurred on the Manatawny Creek around Spangsville in Oley Township.

Heavy rain started early in the morning in the Jamestown area, and training thunderstorms through the afternoon hours produced five to eight inches of rain which resulted in significant flash flooding. According to the emergency manager and several other sources, numerous roads were flooded and washed out due to the flooding. Some of these roads included Manson Road, Tollie Lane, and Riverton Road in the Manson community where two small bridges also reportedly had water flowing over them. Highway 52 at Riverton Road was washed out and impassable. Boatland Road and Mill Creek Road were also washed out with a car swept away along Mill Creek Road. Glenobey Road and David Road were also flooded and closed. No reports of injuries or fatalities were received. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain began in the Clarkrange area early in the morning and continued into the afternoon hours, producing an estimated five to eight inches of rain. This produced significant flash flooding in the area with the emergency manager and several other sources reporting that numerous roads were flooded and washed out. These included Highway 127 and Highway 62 as well as Franklin Loop north of Clarkrange. A CoCoRaHS observer northeast of Clarkrange near Roslin Road measured 6.11 inches of rain. No injuries or fatalities were reported, and damages are a rough estimate.
North Point Road was closed to due to water flowing over the road near Wood Avenue.
Lodge Forest Road near North Point Road was closed due to flowing water.
Ruth avenue was closed near Sparrows Point Road due to flowing water.
Rudasill Mill Road was closed due to flowing water over the roadway in several locations.

Portions of Dundon-Widen Road were impassable between the towns of Widen and Dille for a time due to high water. The water approached a few homes near the road and washed out portions of the driveway.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Cates Hill Road.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over southern Utah and far northern Arizona caused flash flooding in the Paria River. The river gauge on the Paria at Lees Ferry (Colorado River) showed a two foot rise between 415 PM and 645 PM.
Flooded streets and yards across garden city were reported.
Law enforcement reported multiple roads flooded across Garden City.
In Leominster, multiple homes had to be evacuated including a trailer park of 30 people on Central St.
In Leominster, Rt 2 near Rt 12 was closed due to flooding.
A NWS Employee reported 1 to 2 feet of flowing water just east of the intersection of Green Meadow Drive and Oak Grove Blvd. at the low water crossing.

Heavy rain in excess of 4 inches lead to several inches of gravel and dirt washing over the Birkie rollerski track along with washouts along the side of the path up to a foot deep in the dirt along with smaller chunks of pavement removed as well.
Several medium to large washouts were reported across Boedecker Road.
A water rescue was needed on Main street at Tatum Branch in Stamps, due to a vehicle that was swept off of the roadway.
A vehicle became trapped in flood waters at the intersection of Mine Lane Road and Division Street in Palmer Township, necessitating a water rescue.
Heavy rain in the Crossville area caused vehicles to stall in flood waters near Old Jamestown Highway and Industrial Drive. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain in the Monterey area caused flooding of several roads and one unknown business. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain in the Sparta area caused flash flooding along Roosevelt Drive near White County High School. Damages are a rough estimate.
Station manager at KNEB reported flooding in and around Bayard.
Emergency manager reported streets flooded in and around Dalton.
Running water from the heavy rainfall led to gravel being washed across the pavement on Highway OO along with the ditch becoming eroded.
Public reported that the low water crossing at the Irving Street Bridge over the Concho River had several inches of fast flowing water over it.
In Leominster, multiple roads was flooded and impassable.
A clogged storm drain resulted in repeated flooding along South Main Street at Townsend Outdoors in Hope.
Significant flooding over County Road 8, with a portion of the roadway washed out.

Flood waters reached the first floor of a house in Washington Township, causing a basement wall to collapse. A bridge on Lower South Main Street in the township was severely damaged due to rushing flood waters.

Catastrophic flash flooding occurred in Upper Makefield Township, resulting in the loss of seven lives. A reliable rain gauge located within the township indicated that 4.64 inches of rain fell during the event which lasted less than 2 hours. Widespread roadway flooding occurred with many roads becoming impassable. Numerous water rescues took place in the township. The worst of the flooding occurred along Hough's Creek. The creek rose rapidly and the rushing water carried away many vehicles, most along Taylorsville Road which parallels the Delaware Canal. Eleven vehicles were reported to have been swept into the creek. Eight individual were rescued from their vehicle and two from the creek. Unfortunately, seven people perished either while trapped in their vehicle or while attempting to escape the flood waters.||The Taylorsville Road Bridge over Hough's Creek was structurally compromised. PA Route 532 between Stonebridge Crossing Road and Wrightstown Road was damaged severely by the raging flood waters from Hough's Creek.

Heavy rain in the Tullahoma area caused flash flooding in numerous areas, including along Wilson Avenue, Ovoca Road, and along North Jackson Street where the O'Reilly's parking lot was flooded. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain in the Normandy area resulted in flash flooding along Rowesville Road. One person had to be rescued from their vehicle which got trapped in the flood waters. No injuries were reported. Damages are a rough estimate.
Roads were impassable due to flooding.
The Walnut Grove Road and Poplar Avenue underpass was flooded.
Received via Facebook of county roads flooded in and around Redington.
Emergency manager reported flash flooding in Lodgepole. Second report from spotter in Sunol of flash flooding as well.
A family was rescued from high water in south Hamilton County. There was widespread water over roadways.

Severe widespread flooding in Swanzey prompted Police to issue a statement Please avoid driving in Swanzey at this time. Numerous roads across the community were flooded and damaged by floodwaters including Route 10, Holbrook Avenue, Old Homestead Highway, East Shore, and Carlton Roads, along with several others.

Reports of impassable roadway flooding in and just north of Fremont, including flowing water over County Road 73 between Oak Harbor Road and Fangboner Road. Community building in the northern portion of Fremont experienced up to 5 feet of water in the basement of the building. Radar estimated rainfall of 3.25 to 4 inches fell in a 3 to 4 hour period, much of which fell in an initial 45 to 60 minute period, when 1.5 to 2 inches of rain fell in the hour leading up to the flash flood event.
Significant flooding across County Road 57, with portions of the roadway and culverts washed out.
Raleigh-Lagrange Road was flooded between Jenkins Road and Highway 194.
Cars were stranded in floodwaters at Semmes Street and McCool Avenue. Floodwaters reached the doorways of the cars.
Peoria Heights Fire Department reported six to eight inches of standing water on Illinois Route 29 near War Memorial Drive.

The Cold River came out of banks on the evening of the 10th following heavy rains. The river had been running high due to multiple rounds of heavy rain over the previous few days. After approximately 1 to 3 inches of additional rain that afternoon, the river spiked to the second highest level on record at the Alstead USGS river gage (period of record 2010-2023). The river crested at 11.67 feet, with a discharge of 10,300 cfs. The flow recorded has an annual exceedance probability between 1% and 0.2% levels. The high flowing water came out of banks along Route-123A in South Acworth and Acworth Road in Alstead. Acworth Fire Chief rescued 12 people from their homes on Route 123A. He said several cars were swept by water but there were no injuries in those incidents. The floodwaters caused damage to the southbound lane on Acworth Road. In Lempster South Road and River Road were flooded.

Flooding caused by the significant rainfall over two days damaged property and roads in the Marlow area. Most roads were closed due to flooding and residents were advised to stay home. The flooding produced on the 10-11th of July occurred over areas that were already dealing with previous flooding. The North Fork of the already flooded Ashuelot River flooded portions of Marlow. Another source of flooding came when the Stoddard Lake overflowed totally surounding homes.
Multiple road closures were reported in Newfane due to flooding.
Multiple road closures were reported in Wilson due to flooding.
Multiple road closures were reported in the Somerset area due to flooding.
Kendrick Road closed due to flooding.
In Fitchburg, cars were stuck in flood waters by the bridge on River St.
Multiple roads flooded in Pell City. Water entered eight residential homes on Fox Run Circle.

Significant flooding occurred during the early morning hours on July 13th across southern Sumter County. Vehicles were swept off roadways and a portion of I-20 was closed for several hours. Water entered many homes in the city of York and people were trapped in their homes and had to be rescued by swift water boats. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
In Hampton, there were flooded basements on Main St and Brook St.

Heavy rain generated flash flooding near the community of Burbank. Northbound lanes of Highway 170 were flooded.

Several portions of Route 9 were closed east of Paxton due to flooding. Winter Street was blockaded. A photo shared on social media showed a rain gauge near Paxton with a storm total of 6.50 inches of rain.

Law Enforcement reported inundation of Milwood Road due to floodwaters from a nearby pond. In addition to the 1.5 inches of rain that fell the previous day, radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches, with isolated amounts of up to 8 inches, fell on March 26, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Morgan Road closed due to flash flooding. This area also experienced flooding the day prior. In the 36-hours prior to the event, 6 to 8 inches of rainfall had fallen, with another 1.5 to 2 inches occurring on March 27, resulting in the flash flooding.
