State Route 58 and County Road 281 closed due to flooding of East Branch Black River in Sullivan Township in northeast Ashland County. Radar estimated 3 to 3.5 inches of rainfall in a 2 to 3 hours period.

Reports of widespread road closures due to flooded and impassable roadways in northeast Sandusky County. Radar estimated 3 to 3.25 inches of rain fell in a 2 to 3 hour period preceding the flash flood event. Total rainfall of 4 to 4.5 inches fell over a 5 hour period.

Major flash flooding occurred throughout Death Valley National Park. Four hundred miles of NPS roads were damaged or destroyed, in addition to other roads maintained by the county and state. Lake Washington, Core, and Lubeck Roads were closed due to high water in and around the Parkersburg area.

Widespread roadway and basement flooding across Catawba Island. One water rescue was reported at a campground in Catawba Island. Radar estimated 5.5 to 6 inches of rainfall in a four hour period ending around 400 AM EDT on August 24, 2023, with a bulk of the rain falling in roughly 2.5 hours.

Over 2 inches of rain fell in a 3 hour period in American Falls resulting in flash flooding. Pocatello Avenue flooded with water coming halfway up tires. The construction site at American Falls High School flooded with sandbags required. Multiple houses flooded as storm drains could not catch up with the heavy rainfall.

The Emergency Manager reported multiple roads closed due to flash flooding on Potato Creek, including E County Road, Cobbtown Road, and Del Ray Road at North Delray Road. |In the 36-hours prior to the event, these areas had received 6 to 8 inches of rainfall, with another 1.5 to 2 inches occurring on March 27, resulting in the flash flooding.

Multiple road closures due to flooding in Cass and Plymouth Townships. Flooding of Bear Run and Marsh Run caused flowing water over roadways leading to their closure. Near the community of Azusa, a couple feet of mud covered the lanes of Highway 39.
Flash flooding occurred throughout the Mojave National Preserve. All roads, facilities, trails, etc in the preserve were closed. Exact start and end times unknown.
Heavy flooding pushed debris across Highway 62 between Cactus Jack and Godwin.
Mud and debris washed onto Highway 62 just east of Olympic Rd.
Several roads in Twentynine Palms were closed due to flooding.
A boulder washed onto Highway 62 at Hess Rd.
The public reported flooding of the on ramp for I-75, stalling one vehicle. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The public reported a flooded residential driveway near the Ocmulgee River in Juliette. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 2.5 inches fell in the previous 24-hours, and 3 to 4 inches accumulated on March 27, resulting in high runoff rates and rises on the Ocmulgee River.
Debris flow from heavy rainfall required the state emergency operations center to deliver sandbags to protect homes in and around Rociada. No damage was reported.
A trained spotter reported flash flooding over the road, stranding some motorcyclists on the main road in Featherville, ID.

One to two inches of rain fell in Chubbuck in a 3 hour time frame and caused some flash flooding on roads and a few basements. The interstate 86 underpass on Hawthorne Road flooded. Interstate 86 flooded with 2 feet of water standing in an active construction zone. Water was pumped off of road but traffic significantly impaired. Garage and basement flooding in the Chubbuck and Galena Road area.
Heavy rains caused flash flooding in Clovis, Texico, and Cannon Air Force Base. There were multiple reports of roads becoming closed and impassable with vehicles being stranded.
Near the community of Palmdale, several homes reported significant flood damage.
Near the community of Alhambra, flooding was reported at the connector of Interstate 10 and Interstate 710.
Mud and debris flows were reported on Piuma Road near Malibu Canyon Road.
Flash flooding in Baker was up to vehicle hoods.
Highway 95 was flooded near mile marker 17.
The intersection of Highway 178 and Trona Rd was flooded with multiple vehicles stuck, and 178 was also possibly washed out at Pinnacle Rd.
Water and mud covered La Contenta and Alta Loma Rds.
Four feet of rushing water trapped people in their cars on Highway 127. The road was severely damaged.
Mud and debris covered the intersection of Amboy Rd and Cactus Jack.

Several strong to severe cells produced very heavy rain over north-central portions of Knox County, where 2.50 to 4.50 inches fell, with 4.13 measured from the same maximum rain axis at the Plainville 1.3 S CoCoRaHS site in northwestern Daviess County. Standing water was widespread along and near Indiana Route 67 between Bruceville and Edwardsport, with water in several basements.

A clogged culvert resulted in minor flooding issues of two houses residing along Little Creek Road. Slaughters Creek rose above its banks and caused high water issues along Slaughters Creek Road and Westwood Drive.

In Danville, Drawdy Creek rose out of its banks and inflicted water to spill onto the roadway at Arvle Lane. A water rescue was conducted to help a citizen trapped in their home. Two other water rescues occurred along Coal River Road in the town of Seth. Sections of Three Fork Road were washed out along with several culverts in the Hopkins Fork area. At least 7 homes were impacted by high water issues in the county, with two of those homes deemed to have observed major flooding impacts.
High water was observed along Honeyfork Road in the Foster township.

Nebo Walker Road observed high water issues along several spots as a result of Dawson Fork Creek and Stinson Creek rising out of its banks. Near the town of Big Otter, Murphy Fork also rose out of its banks and caused flooding along Clinic Road and Big Otter Road.

Two rounds of thunderstorms produced heavy rain over the highlighted area that resulted in several reports of flash flooding impacts. Flash flooding forced debris over the roadway at the intersection Montgomery and Carlisle with rocks greater than 5 inches in diameter, and street flooding also observed at Moon and Menaul. High water rises were observed on area arroyos resulting in swift water rescue being deployed with two people able to self-rescue. I-40 westbound also saw two lanes close near San Pedro for emergency repairs. There was also 6 inches of standing water on the bridge over the Hahn Arroyo, with water also reaching the base of a pedestrian bridge over I-40 near San Mateo.

Rock slide reported on Highway 82 just west of Mountain Park near the Tunnel Vista observation site due to the heavy rain that fell the previous afternoon/evening. The road remained closed for approximately 2 days.
The intersection of Highway 395 and Randsburg Cutoff Rd was flooded.
Fast-moving water covered the intersection of I-15 and Fort Irwin Rd.
Highway 247 was flooded and closed at Pipes Canyon Rd.
A vehicle was covered in mud and sinking at the intersection of Covington Dr and East Dr.
Two feet of rock and debris covered Highway 62 near Valley View Rd, and small boulders were on the highway from Senilis Ave to east of Valley View Rd.

Persistent showers and thunderstorms affected the southern portions of St. Lawrence County, NY during the late afternoon and evening hours on August 4, 2023. Radar estimates of between two and five inches of rain fell in this area, particularly in the Town of Pitcairn where emergency management reported multiple road washouts, including along Edwards Rd.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding on I-75/85 at 10th Street, stalling three vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The public reported flooding of the exit ramp at I-20 and Hill Street. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported more than a dozen roads closed due to flooding across the city of LaGrange, including Orchard Hill Road. Road flooding prompted school closures due to the number of impacted bus routes. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area the day prior, with an additional 3 to 6 inches accumulating on March 27, resulting in the flash flooding.

The public reported flooding at the intersection of Cook Road and Lower Big Springs Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area the day prior, with an additional 3 to 6 inches accumulating on March 27, resulting in the flash flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported flooding and debris in roadway completely covering the intersection of Oak Creek Rd. and CalPortland Access Rd.
California Highway Patrol reported heavy flooding on Redrock-Randsburg Rd. between US 395 and SR 14 which required the road to be closed.
California Highway Patrol reported several large rocks as least 1 foot in diameter washed up on northbound Interstate 5 just south of Grapevine Rd..
The Kern County Emergency Manager reported Copus Rd. was closed between Old River Rd. and Basic School Rd. due to heavy flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported large rocks across the roadway at the intersection of SR 58 and SR 223. near Bealville.

The Ridgecrest Fire Department reported heavy flooding in a portion of Ridgecrest that resulted in an evacuation for areas bounded by West Ridgecrest Blvd, North Alvord St. West Las Flores Ave. and North China Lake Blvd. Other portions of Ridgecrest were impacted by soil erosion and instability resulting in heavy runoff.

Multiple road closures due to flooding, including the U.S. 20/Main Street underpass east of Broad Street, North Street, Buckeye Street, and High Street. A report of a car stranded in water in Bellevue. Radar estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rain fell in one hour.

Fast flowing water, rock, and debris covered Whitney Portal Rd, the Whitney Portal parking lots, and the road to Lone Pine Campground. Whitney Portal Rd was destroyed by high flows in Lone Pine Creek.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon. It was closed for a day to remove the flood debris.

Fossil Creek Road (Forest Road 708) closed for several days due to damage from heavy rain and flooding that occurred on August 16th and 17th. Closure began morning of August 18th and remain closed for several week or more.
Heavy rain over the Schultz (2010) and Pipeline (2022) fire scars brought debris flowing over Copland Lane. A road grader was needed to clear the road.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms moving south over the Paria River basin (including in Utah) caused flash flooding. The river gauge on the Paria River near the Colorado River (Lees Ferry) measured a rise in water the level 4.8 feet at 8:15 PM MST to 6.6 feet at 11:00 PM.
East Bellefonte Road was around the 10 block closed due to high water and vehicles stranded.
Russell Road around Mount Vernon Avenue was closed due to high water and vehicles stranded.
In Boston, on Columbia Rd at Hamilton St a car was stuck in flooding and the driver needed to be rescued.
In Dedham, the intersection of Milton and River St was flooded.

Reports of widespread flash flooding in Port Clinton. Multiple flooded and impassable roadways reported along with widespread basement flooding. Radar estimated around 4 inches of rainfall in just under a 3 hour period ending 300 AM EDT on August 24, 2023, with total rainfall of 5 to 5.5 inches ending 500 AM EDT on August 24, 2023.

Minor flooding occurred along Rocky Branch Creek in downtown Columbia. The USGS gage at the intersection of Whaley Street and Main Street crested at 7.50 feet at 747 pm. Flood stage at this location is 7.2 feet.
Flooding and debris on the Cameron overpass on SR 58 caused a closure in both directions as SR 58 became impassible.
California Highway Patrol reported a large rock blocking lanes on Interstate 5 south of Wheeler Ridge Rd.
California Highway Patrol reported large rocks in the roadway on Sand Canyon Rd. 3 miles north of Tehachapi Blvd. which required clearing with a plow.
California Highway Patrol reported flooding causing erosion and running over the roadway at the intersection of Elm Trail and Mount Pinos Way in Frazier Park.
California Highway Patrol reported large rocks on SR 178 southwest of Lake Isabella.
Kern County officials reported a closure of Tehachapi Blvd. east of Tehachapi Willow Springs Rd. due to heavy flooding.
Kern County officials reported a road closure of South Kelso Valley Rd. and Birch Springs Pass due to heavy flooding.

Law Enforcement reported flooding and closure of New Road due to high water on a small creek. In addition to the 1.5 inches of rain that fell the previous day, radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches, with isolated amounts of up to 8 inches, fell on March 26, resulting in the flash flooding.

Multiple road closures reported across the southern portion of Norwalk, including Christie Avenue, Shady Lane Drive, Water Street, and Benedict Avenue. Sewer backups reported in Norwood Avenue. Radar estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rain fell in one hour.
The NM Department of Transportation reported State Highway 108 was closed to flooding north of Pleasant Hill.

Multiple reports of flash flooding were received via social media during the evening of May 25, 2023. Streets throughout town were flooded, closed, or impassable with vehicles being stranded in some spots. Water was also reported to have reached up to business entrances.

The Emergency Manager reported Covered Bridge Road near Red Oak Creek flooded. In addition to the 1.5 inches of rain that fell the previous day, radar estimates indicate that an additional 6 to 8 inches fell on March 26, resulting in the flash flooding.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms produced localized flooding at the intersections of 5th and Fir Streets. Photos from the public show water 3-6 inches deep over the roadway, with some folks taking to using Kayaks for their amusement.
There was a water rescue involving multiple vehicles on Mount Olivet Road NE.
Emergency manager reported flooded roads in downtown Cheyenne. Lincoln Avenue flooded as well as Ames underpass. Crow Creek flooded out of it's banks.
Reports of flash flooding in Sidney on many city roads. One vehicle stuck in high water.
Several county roads flooded around Sidney. Includes county roads 16, 99, and 18.
Flash flooding led to the closure of several roads across Bald Eagle, Woodward, and Dunnstable townships in due to water and/or rock slides across roadways.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported multiple flooded and impassable roads in and around Holly Hill. 6 inches of water covering roadways.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported multiple roads impassable due to flooding in and around Santee.

Throughout much of central Cook County including Chicago and nearby suburbs, very heavy rainfall caused widespread flash flooding of roadways and structures. During a 12-hour period from 3 AM to 3 PM CST, storm total rainfall in Cook County ranged from 1-9 inches, with the highest amounts in central Cook County near the border of Chicago, Cicero, and Oak Park. The magnitude of this rainfall ranged from typical to extreme, with the peak rainfall estimated to have less than a 0.2% chance of occurring in a given year. Two distinct waves of heavy rainfall occurred in the Chicago area during this event, with each period of heavy rainfall corresponding to significant flooding.||The first wave of heavy rainfall impacted the Chicago area from 4:30 AM to 11 AM CST. Within a few hours numerous residential streets were flooded and I-290 (Eisenhower Expressway) was blocked in multiple locations, as well as a stretch of I-55 (Stevenson Expressway) near Pulaski Road. Multiple water rescues were reported, most of which occurred at underpasses in Chicago and the immediate western suburbs. Runoff quickly entered the deep tunnel system and mostly filled McCook Reservoir, greatly reducing storage capacity for additional rainfall.||After a brief period with lighter rainfall intensities from 11 AM to 12:30 PM CST, the second wave of heavy began, which occurred until 3:30 PM CST. This additional rainfall brought renewed flooding of numerous roadways as well as portions of CTA's blue and pink El train lines. The storage capacity of the deep tunnel and McCook Reservoir were exceeded, with most rainfall flowing into the Chicago River system as part of a combined sewer overflow event. The Chicago River quickly rose to minor flood stage, flooding the Chicago Riverwalk. MWRD opened gates at Chicago Lock to reverse the flow of the river into Lake Michigan, causing a mixture of rainfall and untreated sewage to enter the lake. The lack of capacity to store combined rain water and sewage caused rainfall to back up into 10s of thousands of basements. As of November 29th, 2023, FEMA had received nearly 75,000 claims for flooded homes, the majority of which are assumed to be basement flooding. Approximately $285 million in FEMA individual assistance grants were provided, along with $96.5 million in low-interest SBA loans. These federal disaster assistance programs only cover a portion of uninsured losses. Few claims, less than $1 million in total, were made to the National Flood Insurance program due to the low percentage of residents paying for such polices and the cause of most instances of flooding being related to sewer backup. The estimated total damage costs from this flash flood event are likely in excess of $500 million.

Flash flooding was reported upstream from this location along Arrowhead Road where 3 to 6 inches of water was flowing over the road where Chester Creek passed under the road. As the surge of water flowed downstream, it damaged walkways along the creek and sent 2 to 5 inches of water onto side streets and Kenwood Avenue. Chester Creek runs through tunnels for much of its trip down the Duluth hillside and this volume of water overwhelmed the tunnels sending a large stream of rapidly flowing water 3 to 10 inches deep down the hill. This affected a few apartment buildings in the vicinity of 7th Avenue and 3rd Street which required a few rescues/evacuations of lower level residents and pets in the buildings by the fire department. Interstate 35 runs through tunnels underground at the base of the hill and the water surging down the hillside began to collect in the tunnels. Standing and flowing water in the tunnels resulted in the closure of the tunnels for a period. Water of at least 4 to 6 inches in depth was covering the southbound lanes in spots. Rainfall amounts of 5 to 7 inches were recorded across the Schmidt Creek basin on the 23rd and 24th with the vast majority of the rainfall occurring on the 24th. This amount of water was significantly more than the creek could handle and issues began near the headwaters. A small culvert carrying the creek under Pioneer Junction Road failed starting with a sinkhole in the road before the fast moving waters completely scoured a channel through the road. Further downstream just after passing under Minnesota Highway 61, the rapidly flowing water encountered another too small culvert that carried the creek under the tracks of the North Shore Scenic Railroad. The water proceeded to scour out this culvert as well exposing a bridge that was originally built by the railroad at this location over 100 years prior. An NSSR train had passed over the bridge about an hour before the culvert failed and noted the developing washout. The train was then stranded in Two Harbors until the washout could be repaired a few days later.

The Mercer County Sheriff's Office received numerous reports of flash flooding across the City of Bluefield WV due to 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain falling between 5 AM and 7 AM EDT, on top of 1.5 to 2.25 inches that had fallen since the evening of the 28th. The most concentrated number of reports occurred near the intersection of Bland Street and College Avenue, where 2 inches of rainfall occurred in one hour. Both Bland Street and College Avenue were flooded by over a foot of rushing water in places. At least one vehicle was stranded in the flood waters, with three occupants requiring help by a swift water rescue team. Several basements in the area were also flooded by several feet of water, including in homes on Bland Street, Union Street, Jefferson Street and College Avenue. Portions of Lynn Street and Walters Avenue were flooded and impassible until the water receded. One swift water rescue was required for the occupant of a vehicle that became stranded by flooding along Grassy Branch Road as Grassy Branch rose out of its banks over a foot deep across the road. Another swift water rescue occurred when a vehicle traveling on Airport Road became stranded in flood waters when a tributary of Brush Creek rose out of its banks over a foot deep.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along the 3900 block of Abbotts Bridge Road, and at the intersection of Duluth Highway and Buford Highway where floodwaters stalled vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along and between Douglas Boulevard and Parkway Drive, due to highwater on a tributary of Anneewakee Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Interstate 25 became flooded at the peak of the event, and was closed for until well after rainfall ended. Low-lying tunnels on the south side of Casper had as much as 5 feet of water in them at the height of the storm. Damage values have been updated as of Oct 2023 and are from the FEMA presidential disaster declaration, FEMA-4739-DR-WY. No injuries or fatalities were reported to the NWS.

The Austin Stream set a record stage of 13.2 feet on December 18th based on records from the USGS river gage established from 1932-1969 and 2009-today. The streamflows reached 14,000 cfs which is greater than a 0.2% annual chance exceedance event, otherwise referred to as a 500-year storm. The stream washed out a 134 foot bridge on Dead Water Road in Moscow and overtook Stream Road washing out a mile long section. The flooding was the result of heavy rainfall falling over frozen ground and melting snow. The rainfall estimates were around 5 inches and the snow melt contributed around an inch or less of additional runoff.

Major flooding occurred on the Wild River in Gilead with the USGS river gage marked the 2nd highest crest on record of 16.4 feet. The gage was established in 1960 and the only flood of higher flows was that following Irene in 2011. The streamflow was near 34 kcfs, which falls between a 0.5 and 0.2% annual chance exceedance level, otherwise referred to as a 200 to 500 year flood. The flooding was the result of 5 to 6 inches of rainfall and 3 to 4 inches of snowmelt running off within an 18-hour timeframe. The steep slopes of the Wild River combined with frozen ground resulted in a fast rise of 13 feet in 12 hours. The fast-moving water overtook Route 113 and washed out a 80-foot section. The flows from the Wild River contributed to the Androscoggin River major flooding in downstream Bethel.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt combined with steep terrain to produce rapid runoff. The resulting runoff over frozen ground caused numerous washouts and sinkholes along the Kancamagus Highway/NH Route 112. Flooding from the adjacent Swift River also eroded a 100 foot section just west of Conway.
Water was across Route 11 between Hallstead and New Milford.
Heavy produced flash flooding in and around Milliken to west of Windsor. Storm totals in these areas ranged from 2.5 to 5.0 inches. Several road closures were in place due to standing water.

Major flooding of the Bear River between Grafton Notch and Newry with an estimated rain and snowmelt combination of 8 and 9 inches. Washouts occurred on Route 26 near Horseshoe Falls in the Grafton Notch Campground area and near Poplar Road, in Newry. Wheeler Road and Branch Roads in North Newry were hard hit with severe washouts running for 2 miles. Major flooding of the Sunday River occurred on the 18th after an estimated 7 to 9 inches of rain and snowmelt ran off into the river. The resultant flow was estimated to be over a 0.2% recurrence interval with flows between 10 and 12 kcfs. The most severe damages were in the Sunday River resort region where a landslide caused damage to a recreational building and several roads were washout out. The flooding continued downstream to Bethel where a Route 2 bridge was flooded and access in and out of the region was cut off for days. Homes were flooded on Sunday River Road including several townhomes off Cherry Lane. Sunday River flooded a bridge and numerous other spots on Vista Road, Roderick Road, Bear River Road, and Sunday River Road, in Newry. Several roads were deemed inaccessible including Summit Road which was completely washout out with the loss of a large metal culvert. Bear River, a tributary to Sunday River also came out of its banks, washing away multiple parked vehicles, in Newry. Multiple water rescue was conducted for occupants of vehicles in flood waters on Vista Road.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused flooding and partial wash-outs of numerous roads in the Blue Mountain region, particularly in Weld. The roads include Edes Brook Road, Intervale Road, and Day Mountain Road.
Multiple reports of streets flooded across metro New Orleans, with most reports in the Mid City and Uptown areas. A few reports of underpasses closed at Carrolton and Canal.

Flooding on Route 232 near Gore Road from the Bakers Brook in Milton.

An unnamed tributary to the Alder Stream washed out the entire length of Tufts Pond Road to the sub-base. The flooding was the result of 5 inches of rain and another 2 to 3 inches of snowmelt running off frozen terrain.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt combined with steep terrain to produce rapid runoff. The resulting runoff over frozen ground caused flooding from the Rocky Branch River in Glen New Hampshire. The Stilling's Road became inundated and was closed due to the flooding.

Video evidence showed significant flow along Fortuna Wash near I-8. It is likely the water flowed across East Masterson Avenue and Foothills Boulevard, located about 0.5 mile downstream of I-8, making those roadways impassable. Between 1-1.5 inches of rain was estimated to have fallen in the general area based on doppler radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Bridge washed away on Milton Road after the Concord River overflowed its banks following heavy rain and snowmelt.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused flooding of numerous roads in Carthage along the Webb River including Grover Bridge Road, Storer Hill Road, and River Road. With additional flooding being reported on Goodwin Road.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt combined with steep terrain to produce rapid runoff into the Ellis River. The small stream became a raging river after 6 inches of rain and 3 inches of snowmelt overwhelmed the stream system. Downstream in Jackson, properties along the river were inundated, along with several roads being damaged. The main thruway, NH Route 16, closed at mile marker 92.6, and adjacent NH 16B also flooded. Washouts were also reported in many local roads like Green Hill Road.
A video shared via social media showed water entering a business along South Market Street. Saltwater flooding approximately 18 inches deep was also reported in a business inside the City Market.

Fire rescue personnel reported at least one home flooded on Mercury Road, requiring a homeowner to be rescued. The entire area along the roads of Mercury, Hamlin, and Atlanta Drive were flooded with a combination of salt and fresh water. An estimated 30-40 homes were surrounded by flood waters with the occupants sheltering in place.
A video relayed via social media showed water inside a building along Drake Street.

US-17 closed from Highmarket Street to Sampit River Bridge due to flooding.
Water rescues conducted between North Watkins Road near East 6th Ave south of Watkins. Occupant in one of the vehicles drowned.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused extreme flooding in the Sugarloaf Mountain region. Numerous small streams became raging rivers with washouts on most local and state roads, cutting off access to the region.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt produced around 9 inches of combined runoff. All small streams in the Presidential Range region exceeded their banks. This was true in Jefferson, New Hampshire where numerous small streams flooded Route 115 and Route 2, causing these roads to be closed.
A NWS employee reported water approximately 6 inches deep entering several businesses at South Windermere Shopping Center.

Major flooding of the Moose River with an estimated rain and snowmelt between 8 and 9 inches of liquid runoff. The resultant flow was estimated around 6500 CFS, which is greater than the 0.2% annual exceedance level, or 500 year flood. The river overflowed its banks surrounding homes and flooding basements off Bellevue Place near the Gorham Airport. Additional flooding occurred on Water Street and Broadway Avenue. Flood waters topped the Route 2 bridge shutting down a major throughway in the region.
A few roads were flooded around Salisbury.

Extreme flooding across the Bethel area resulted in swift water rescues of several motorists and residents. The Bethel Fire Department performed numerous rescues starting around 11:30 am and continued through the afternoon as flood waters cut the community off. Officials estimate at least a dozen water rescues were conducted with a few dozen people being rescued. One area were numerous rescues were occurring was Mill Brook along Lovers Lane.

Valley Brook, a tributary to the Sandy River washed out the abutment on the Route 149 Bridge in Strong. The flooding was the result of 5 inches of rain and another 2 to 3 inches of snowmelt running off frozen terrain.

Major flooding of the Moose Brook with an estimated rain and snowmelt between 8 and 9 inches in runoff. The resultant flow is estimated over a 0.2% recurrence interval with flows between 3 and 4 kcfs. The most severe damages were near Pike Industries in Gorham, which suffered a washed-out bridge and floodwaters compromised a building. The nearby storage facility was inundated with unknown damages. Jimtown Road flooded but no reported homes where damaged. The flows overwhelmed the Moose Brook bridge overtopping onto Route 2. A large truck was picked up by the flood waters and wedged under the bridge, along with significant amounts of rocks and debris.
A combination of torrential rain and hail caused flash flooding. Multiple road closures were in effect due to washed out county roads, including County Road 17 south of CO 14.

Number 3 and 4 lanes of I-10W near and east of Date Palm Drive blocked with mud and debris. The nearby Thousand Palms mesonet recorded 0.83 inch of rain since 3 AM that morning, though no rain was occurring when the flooding was reported.

Heavy rain and snowmelt runoff caused flooding of Otter Brook onto Interval Road near the confluence with the Androscoggin River in Hanover. Vehicles were trapped in the flood waters with occupants needing to be rescued.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt combined with steep terrain to produce rapid runoff. The resulting runoff over frozen ground caused flash flooding on the Ammonoosuc River causing a closure of the Tunnel Brook Bridge in Easton.

Significant damage occurred on the Peabody River on December 18th following a heavy rain and rapid snowmelt event. The USGS river gage in Gorham went from under 100 cfs around midnight, to over 13,000 cfs by noon. The streamflows were estimated to be around the 1% annual exceedance or 100-year flood level. Rainfall amounts where estimated around 5 inches with an additional 3 inches of rapid snowmelt runoff. The ground conditions were frozen, supporting complete runoff. One home off Route 16 was deemed unlivable and a complete loss after floodwaters eroded the foundation. Property was also damaged at Great Glen Trails Outdoor Center near the headwaters. Downstream in Gorham the damage was most prevalent along Bell Street and after the confluence with the Androscoggin River. Major damage occurred downstream to the town of Shelburne.
Prentice Road is closed by flooding.
Numerous roads are flooded around the West Burlington area.

Rushing water observed overtopping CO-63 north of Elba. A trained spotter near Elba measured a total of 4.2 inches of rainfall.

Heavy rain and rapid snowmelt combined with hilly terrain to produce rapid runoff. This was 1.5 feet less than that reached following Irene in 2011.
A video from social media shows fast moving water rushing down roads in the area.
Rising water in Sauquoit Creek is affecting the bridge on Main Street. Flooding is occurring at properites downstream of this location.
Jennings Creek is out of bank and flooding nearby properties. There is also extensive yard and basement flooding in the area.
Swift water rescues evacuated 12 people from near the Sauquoit Creek. All 12 people were successfully rescued with no injuries.
Urban flooding is blocking roads in the area.
All lanes of MS Highway 3 between Phoenix Road and Germania Road were flooded.

Torrential rainfall led to near zero visibilities along US Highway 84 in northeastern Hockley County as reported by local law enforcement and from public reports. Storms slowly trained over the area from central Hockley County from north of Levelland to near Anton. Water was reportedly over the roadway along US Highway 385 between Whitharral and Levelland.
The Buckhorn Road, County Road 44H, was closed west of Stove Prairie Road due to flood damage. Water was also observed crossing County Road 43 at Streamside Drive.
Dogwood Road was flooded.
Highway Dept. and EM reported flash flooding with road closures and a few culvert washouts on Route 14 in and south of Williamstown, VT during the late afternoon hours on the 7th.

Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall impacted the affected area during the late morning hours of July 16. Radar estimates and ground observations showed between two and three inches of rain fell, leading to a few areas of flash flooding, most notably in the Morrisville area where a few roads were closed.
Floodwaters of unknown depth caused a single vehicle crash along U.S Highway 287 east of Boyero.
A roadway was flooded near the Memphis International Airport.
NH Route 11 had 2 to 3 feet of water over the road.
Heavy rain caused the Tuttle Brook to come out of banks and cause some minor damage to the Recreational Area off Lake Road.

Forest Service reported up to two dozen culverts washed out and six county roads that were partially or fully washed out. Large trees were washed into fields and there was significant damage to farm fields in several areas in the counties. There are significant areas of crop fields that likely lost in excess of 100 tons per acre from that one heavy rain event. The county estimated the damage to be approximately $400,000-$600,000.
Heavy rain on the evening of July 8th caused Western Avenue to close due to flooding near New England College. Additional flooding was observed along Hall and Gould Street.

The public reported deep, swiftly moving water in areas around the Garnett MARTA station, flooding roadways and carrying multiple vehicles in the flow. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.

Slow moving storms with intense rain rates moved over Parmer County dropping as much as one inch of rainfall in less than 20 minutes. The Friona Police Department reported that US Highway 60 in Friona was flooded. Additionally, portions of US Highway 60 outside of Friona had water over the roadway.

Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall became anchored over Lynn County during the mid-morning hours. The Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near O'Donnell measured 7.02 inches of rainfall. The intense rain rates and amount of rainfall resulted in the closure of a portion of US Highway 87 between O'Donnell and Tahoka. Numerous water rescues were completed and many vehicles became stranded in the flood waters.
Report received of street flooding on Walnut Avenue with a water depth of 3 feet. Time duration is radar estimated.

The public reported Snider Road, between Gibson and Mitchell, was washed out due to highwater on a local creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.
The lower floor of a home was flooded in Quito. A roadway was flooded in Quito.
Deep flood waters came off North Shore Road onto W Shore Road near the intersection with N Shore Road adjacent to Pleasant Pond. The debris was over a foot deep.
Flash flooding on Highway 80 just east of intersection with Lynch Street.

Danville volunteer fire department reported Parker Rd. washed out due to flash flooding at the Whiteman Brook crossing. Other later reports of flooding were received in the town, but details remain unclear.
Local post office reported pavement and culvert washout on Middle Rd. in Weston, VT.
MDOT reported flooding on US 80 between Hawkins Crossing Drive and Jimmie Rodgers Parkway. Road was closed off both directions due to flooding.

An estimated three to four inches of rain from training thunderstorms over Starkville caused scattered flooding of roads especially in the northwest part of the city. Three feet of standing water flooded cars in the Chandler Park area, a car was stranded due to flooding at the intersection of MS Highway 12 and Spring Street, a portion of Nelson Street was closed due to flooding at its intersection with Yellow Jacket Drive, and flooding at the intersection of Washington and Gillespie Streets threatened a home.
Kit Carson county dispatch passed along a report of flooding in the basement of a residential home in Burlington, CO.
Several roads were flooded near the Canal Place Cinema.
Flash flooding along Standing Pine Drive surrounded 4 mobile homes and required water rescues by boat. Other nearby areas were flooded as well.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain produced localized flash flooding north of Wellington. Up to 3.50 inches of rain fell in several hours. Multiple gravel roads were washed out or damaged due to the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager relayed more than 40 reports of water rescues, dozens of stalled vehicles, and several flooded buildings and student dorms at Clark Atlanta University. These reports were concentrated around Peoplestown, Vine City and Atlanta University Center Consortium as well as downtown Atlanta south of 10th street. Vehicles parked near Northside Drive and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive were washed into a parking lot near Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Cars could be seen in piles along streets, covered in mud. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.

The public reported street flooding near and inundation of the Georgia Aquarium and World of Coca-Cola, forcing their temporary closure. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.
Highway 309 near Oak Street closed due to flooding in Byhalia.
Flooding was reported along NV 338, which closed the highway from Wellington to the CA/NV border. Location is approximate based on radar.
NV-359 closed in Mineral County near mile post 25 due to flooding. Reported by NDOT.

The same slow moving storms that brought intense rainfall and flash flooding to Parmer County also moved over Swisher County. Similarly, the intense rainfall brought over an inch of rainfall in less than 20 minutes. The Tulia Police Department reported that several roads in town were flooded along with a few County Roads along US Highway 87.

Thunderstorms that became anchored over Lynn County bringing extensive flash flooding slowly moved into central and northern Garza County spreading intense rain rates along with it. Widespread flash flooding was reported throughout central and northern Garza County. Additionally, a tractor trailer rolled over on US Highway 84 near Farm to Market Road 399 also causing a multiple vehicle wreck.
The torrential rainfall, which added up to over two inches of rainfall, caused water to flow into a resident's basement and a business downtown.

Report received of flash flooding with photos and videos at 9.5 miles north of Bird City, KS by Big Timber Creek. 1.86 inches of rainfall reported. Reporter stated they could not make it home due to the flooding. Flooding started around sundown and waters did not recede enough to cross until sunrise the following day.
Water and tree debris was flowing across Ball Park Road.
Flooding was ongoing on Miami St in South Bend with water of 6 to 8 inches deep.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain led to flash flooding. Up to 3.50 inches of rain fell over several hours. Garland Road was partially blocked and washed out due to overwhelmed culverts. In addition multiple culverts were washed out on Mill Road along the Garland/Charleston town line. Washouts were also reported on Corinth Road and Fernald Road in Garland...with water across other roads. Water was also reported over Kenduskeag Road and Sawyer Road near the Levant/Kenduskeag town line. Puddledock Road...in the area of Paine Road...was flooded and impassible. A road washout was reported on Bradford Road...between Main Road and Puddledock Road. In Charleston...Harris Road was closed and impassible due to flash flooding.
A few cars were submerged in the Teresa Street underpass in Laurel.

Emergency Management in Waseca County reported that street and small stream flooding was occurring in and about three miles north of New Richland, MN. There were also reports of numerous structures and homes with flooded basements. Approximately two miles north of New Richland, a trained spotter reported that heavy rains were allowing Boot Creek to flow about six feet out of its banks and it started to run over 120th Street (Paved elevated road). Approximately three miles north of New Richland, MN, heavy rainfall caused flooding of a roadway which cut off access to a household's driveway. New Richland City Administration confirmed that flash flood waters receded within 24 hours and no longer posed a threat to public safety.
Kentucky 307 was closed at the 14 to 16 mile markers at Little Joe Creek south of Kentucky 1748 and Beulah.
In the Rock Springs Hollow Road area, a roadway culvert was washed out.
Water was over roads in Wingo. Water was over Kentucky 339 in downtown Wingo.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding near the community of Atascadero in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported mud and rocks across Highway 41.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in Santa Barbara county. Highway 135 was closed from Bell Street to the Harris Grade, due to significant mud and water flowing across the roadway.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported road closures between Avila Beach Drive and San Luis Bay drive, due to flooding.
Route 50 was covered with 3 feet of water.
Flood waters starting to run across US Highway 285.
State Highway 137 is closed at the Junction with US Highway 285 due to flooding. Rocky Arroyo is also flooding at the bridge on US Highway 285.
Loop bypass road on the west side of Carlsbad is closed due to flooding.
A car was flooded on State Highway 524 on the west side of Carlsbad.
Multiple road closures in the city of Lovington.
A trained spotter reported 1.7 inches of rain in 35 minutes.

Water covered Route 130 about a mile north of Albion. A semi truck driver believed the water was attempting to sweep the semi off the road. The storm total rainfall as reported by a spotter in Albion was 5.71 inches.
Street flooding was reported along Main Street in Murray. Water was over Highway 121 near the intersection with Highway 1497 southeast of Murray.
Highway H north of Zalma was closed due to flooding. The two-day rainfall totals for the 3rd and 4th were 9.15 inches at the Marble Hill co-op site and 8.77 inches at a station just south of Grassy.

Torrential rains of nearly 4 inches in an hour (2 to 3 PM CST; 3 to 4 PM CDT) fell across west Brownsville as a strong cluster of thunderstorms eased through the city. More than 3 feet of water piled up near the B&M Bridge along Mexico Blvd. near the bridge (and in the C and D street vicinity. Several cars were submerged up to the hoods. A CoCoRaHS observer in the Los Ebanos community, 2 miles northeast of the worst flooding, recorded 3.7 inches of rain.
U.S. Highway 67 was flooded near Coldwater.
Several roadways were flooded across northern parts of the county. Water was over roads and up to houses between Chaffee and Oran.
There was flooding of city streets in parts of Henderson.
Washout on Deer Run Road near Collins Road, caused by runoff from nearby hills and Jock Stream.

Widespread flash flooding occurring in Hickman. Numerous roads were closed or impassable. Five homes in Hickman were evacuated due to flash flooding. Numerous streets remained closed through the morning. An area along Kentucky 94 in the downtown Hickman area was blocked for several days where a mudslide occurred, taking trees with it. Kentucky 125 was blocked near the Hickman city limits. The Fulton County mesonet site located two miles east of Hickman observed 11.28 of rain in 33 hours from 3 AM August 3rd through 12 noon August 4th. This broke the previous 2-day rainfall record for Fulton County, which was 9.80 back on January 1-2, 1966. The 24-hour record also was shattered, with 9.69 occurring between 8 AM August 3rd and 8 AM August 4th. The previous 24-hour record for the county was 7.24 set back on September 23, 2006.
Numerous main roads were closed around Boonville. Cars stalled due to flash flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported Chimney Rock Road was completely washed out, due to heavy rain and flash flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported significant flooding in the community of Cambria in San Luis Obispo county. At a gas station, water rose to a depth up to half of the gas pumps.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris completely blocking York Mountain Road and Shadow Canyon Road.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris blocking the offramp of Highway 154.
Grand Traverse County Emergency Management reports flooding at several spots in and around downtown Traverse City.

Heavy rain between 3 and 5 inches caused a sinkhole along Babbidge Road near Spoondrift Road. The sinkhole damaged the shoulder and part of one lane. The road continued to collapse into the afternoon resulting in a full closure, but the flooding that undermined the road occurred during the morning hours.
Water was over a portion of U.S. Highway 45 north of Jeffersonville. The road was eventually closed north of Cisne.
Roads were closed in Xenia due to flash flooding.
A car was flooded on Coon Creek Road with water up to the hood.

Persistent shower and thunderstorm activity affected portions of eastern Essex County, NY during the afternoon of August 16, 2023. Radar estimates and observational reports showed that between one and three inches of rain affected this area leading to a few reports of flash flooding, mainly in the towns of Moriah and Westport.

State officials reported nearly one mile of Route 17 between Byron and Rangeley Plantation in Franklin County was damaged by flash flooding. Route 4 was also washed out and closed near Sandy River Plantation around the same time.
Water from Mill Stream came over Embden Pond Road in Embden. Flooding also occurred on nearby Slipp and Fahi Pond Road.

Road flooding was reported near the senior center in Hickman. The Kentucky state highway department worked through the morning to remove debris that washed onto roadways. A Kentucky mesonet station near Hickman reported 4.75 inches between midnight and mid-afternoon on the 3rd.
Heavy rain on the 8th caused washouts on Davis and Mason Roads in Vienna near Eaton Mountain, resulting in the closure of Davis Road and 2 spots on Mason Road.
Shoulder washout on Hovey Road near US RT 2 in Farmington with water surrounding a home and flooding an outbuilding.
Several roads on the north and west side of Springfield were closed due to high water. A few vehicles stalled out in the water.
Streets were flooded, and there were homes with flooded basements in Advance. A personal weather station in Advance measured 5.86 inches from midnight to late afternoon on the 3rd.
U.S. 51 was closed between the 9 and 10 mile markers at the Cane Creek bridge north of Hickman. Kentucky Highway 123 was closed at Obion Creek, between mile markers 14 and 16.
A trained spotter reported flash flooding with water running over Highway 71 east of Gering.

Significant flash flooding was reported from the Marble Hill area west-southwest along Highway 34 to the county line. Between 40 and 50 homes and businesses were damaged by flooding in the county. Highway 34 was shut down as a nearby creek flowed over it. At one point, 22 county highways and roads were flooded. Several county roadways were washed out, including bridges. Some of the washouts were 8 to 10 feet deep. Flooding occurred at the main bridge in Marble Hill. Sixteen individuals were rescued from floodwaters throughout the county. Up to 6 feet of water was flowing in some locations. Water flowing 3 to 4 feet deep was observed in Marble Hill. Water was in buildings in Glenallen. Close to the Wayne County line, water was into numerous campers at Twin Bridges Park. Significant flooding occurred near the intersection of Highway Y and Highway 34. Water rescues occurred at the Castor River Campground west of Grassy. The two-day rainfall total at the Marble Hill co-op observation site was 5.73 inches, which occurred on the 13th and 14th. Total flood damage to public infrastructure in the county was conservatively estimated at 18.2 million dollars. Some of this total may have occurred in other flash flood events earlier in the month.

Multiple areas in downtown Plaistow including Town Green, Main Street, and Congressional Avenue were flooded with flowing water across streets and feet of standing water up to knee depth in parts. South of town the main thruway Route 108 or Newton Road was closed due to flooding.
There was at least a foot of water reported over the road by a trained spotter.
Highway 23 north and south of beaver became impassable late Saturday night due to heavy rainfall leading to water flowing over the road.
Law enforcement reported on B street in Colorado Springs.
A car was stranded on Interstate 70 below Federal Blvd overpass, with approximately 1 foot of water covering several lanes.
Clay fire department was en route for a report of a vehicle in water.
Water rescues located on Hiawatha Drive in Colorado Springs.
Three feet of flowing water reported on roadway.

Showers and thunderstorms persisted across the affected area during the evening hours dropping one to three inches of rain and leading to a few areas of flash flooding. A CoCoRaHS observer reported local flash flooding at their residence in the Craftsbury Common area.

EMs and local fire departments reported scattered to numerous areas of high water and road washouts in Caledonia and Orleans Counties on the evening of the 16th after two to four inches of rain affected the area. Hardest hit were the towns of Lyndon, East Haven, Orleans and Egypt. Areal Flood Warnings were issued for this area instead of Flash Flood Warnings.
Widespread running water behind NWS employees house and on street in front of employees house.
Flooding along 9th street.
Heavy rain produced up to a foot of standing water at 23rd Avenue and I-25.

County | road D northwest of Booker and FM 377 also | had water flowing over the road with cars | becoming stranded. Time estimated based on | MRMS FLASH guidance.
Highway 36 was closed due to flooding between Watkins and Schumaker Road. At least 6 vehicles were stranded with reports of roads washed out and active water rescues in progress.
Report from mPing of street flooding, road closures, or vehicles stranded.
Reported by emergency management. There was around a foot of accumulated hail, as well.
There was 10 inches of water flowing across the streets an dup on houses.
Extensive street flooding with water depth estimated at 1 to 2 feet, covering the entire intersection and sidewalks.
Both lanes of traffic were flooded on Michigan Route 139 in Niles at Lincoln Ave.
Emergency management had reported around 6 of rapidly flowing water across Highway 270 between Forgan and Beaver.
Video from NWS employee of road completely overflowing with deep water and flowing very quickly.

Heavy rain and thunderstorms impacted the Halfway Hill Fire burn scar area during the afternoon hours. Subsequently, the Millard County Emergency Manager reported that there were heavy flows out of Copleys Canyon within the burn scar, with flows and debris across the main canyon road and into a campground. This required rock and debris removal.

Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding associated with thunderstorms in the area, which necessitated the closure of several roads in the park, including portions of the Scenic Drive, The Capitol Gorge Road, and Pleasant Creek.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported a debris flow across state Route 24, making it impassable just east of the Visitor Center between Hickman Bridge and Grand Wash. Additionally, flash flooding was observed in Sulphur Creek, and high flows were reported in Grand Wash. This flooding was associated with a cluster of showers and thunderstorms which produced heavy rain over portions of the park, with Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of approximately 0.75 to 1.25.
Water overflowed Four Mile Road just east of AL 188, trapping several vehicles in the flood waters.

Paria Contact Station personnel relayed a pubic report with photos of active flash flooding ongoing in Buckskin Gulch at House Rock Valley Road. This was the result of several hours of rain and thunderstorms, with Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor system rainfall estimates of approximately 0.50 to 1.50 around much of the area.
A portion of Rangeline Road at Laurendine Road was flooded.
Portions of Bellingrath Road and Fowl River Road were flooded.
Water was rapidly flowing over roadways and approaching homes in Barnwell, AL.
Water was covering the road on Henderson Camp Road at Oakdale Avenue.
County Road 49 was impassable between Laurent Road and County Road 12 due to flooding.

Significant flooding was observed impacting Hurricane Boulevard next to Alma Bryant School. Tue vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.
Heavy rain caused flooding along N Davis Highway from Creighton to Olive Road.
Heavy rain caused numerous reports of flooding across southern Escambia County.

As a result of heavy rain nearby, fairly substantial flash flooding was observed along Short Creek through the Hilldale area, with flood waters and debris crossing streets and overflowing culverts. A subsequent rise in flow from approximately 25 CFS to a peak of 1300 CFS was observed at the Fort Pearce Wash gauge downstream as the flood wave propegated.
Heavy rain caused creek to overflow and flood a basement.
Heavy rain caused water to overflow roadway on Highway 21S.
Water was reported in basements and across roadways in Magnolia Springs.
Two to three feet of water was covering US 90 in Theodore.
Flood waters entered buildings along Dauphin Island Parkway.
Heavy rain caused flooding of numerous structures and ongoing highwater rescues ongoing.
A portion of AL 188 at Oakdale was impassable due to water overflowing the roadway.
Quartzsite Fire and Police performed a swift water rescue of two juveniles trapped on a small island in Tyson Wash. No injuries were reported.
Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to heavy rain, park rangers at Zion National Park reported several canyons around the park were flooding.
Heavy rain caused flooding and closed Gulf Breeze Parkway.
Portions of US 90, between AL 17 and McDonald Road were closed in both directions due to flash flooding.
Portions of US 98, near the Foley Beach Express, was closed in both directions due to flash flooding.
Portions of AL 193 near AL 163 were closed due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain caused flooding in the Pensacola area with reports of residents evacuating in Brent along Carpenters creek due to water rapidly rising.
Heavy rain caused flooding of numerous roads around the Pensacola area.
Two to three feet of water was reported over US 90 In Irvington, AL.
Old Pascagoula Road near Peach Terrace Drive was impassable due to water covering the road.
Water rescues occurred on Highway 98 near the Fish River Grill in Foley, AL due to significant flash flooding.
Several portions of Bellingrtah Road was flooded between Half Mile Road and Deakle Road.
Heavy rain over northeast Monroe county with up around 5 inches of rain reported caused flash flooding. Residential streets were submerged in water in and around Monroe.

Late on August 3, the city of Draper declared a state of emergency as flash flooding and mudslides led to road closures on Highland Drive, Bangerter Parkway, and Minuteman Drive. A portion of Bangerter Parkway, near 14200 South, was damaged on the uphill lanes. A number of homes sustained water damage. According to the City of Draper, there were 428 residential damage report forms submitted, with estimated damages of $11,255,765. There were 11 business damage report forms submitted, with estimated damages of $844,235. City infrastructure estimated damage totaled $4,000,000.

Significant flow off of the Jacob City burn scar into Soldier Canyon and Soldier Creek. The road going up Soldier Canyon was closed. SR-36 was closed south of Stockton due to debris and flood waters starting to top the culvert on to SR-36.
Large debris flow through Soldier Canyon off the Jacob City burn scar. Water and debris is flowing across SR-36.
Heavy rain closed Texas at 16th avenue due to flooding.

Numerous road closures occurred across the city due to flash flooding. Playa lakes were overflowing onto roads and water rescues occurred with dive teams deployed. Several reports were relayed from Amarillo police department and Amarillo fire department.

Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to at times heavy rain, local law enforcement reported flash flooding in Snow Canyon State Park, including water moving over Snow Canyon Road which made the road impassable. The flooding also necessitated the closure of the south entrance to the park.
Water began to enter the garage of a home in Theodore, AL.
Heavy rain closed Langley Avenue from Davis highway to Hermitage drive due to flooding.
Heavy rain with reported rainfall amounts around 5 inches across far eastern Washtenaw county lead to flooding. Tyler road near Willow Run Airport was washed out.
Multiple road closures occurred in Canyon due to fast flowing water over roads. Reports were relayed from emergency management and canyon police department.
Heavy rain caused a road washout along Tom Call Road.
Portions of County Road 12 was impassable due to flash flooding.

Heavy rain of 4-7 inches caused flooding across much of Western Wayne County. Areas in and around Detroit Metro Airport were particulary hard hit, with flooding limiting the acess to McNamara Terminal. Vehicles were stranded in several feet of water and parts of I-275 and I-94 were closed due to flooding. Numerous reports of roadway flooding in Canton Township, some of which required water rescues. Many businesses throughout Canton Township were damaged by flooding. Several inches of water covering residential street in Woodhaven. Flooding reported at Five Mile Rd and Northville Rd. Finally, after the 8/24 flooding, the Western Township Utilities Authority system could not keep up with the capacity and was forced to release partially treated effluent into the Lower Rouge River creating a public health issue.

Fairly persistent showers moved over Sulphur Creek during the morning hours, with thunderstorms moving over the Capitol Reef National Park area during the early afternoon. The storms resulted in quick bursts of heavy rain, with radar estimates showing around 0.4 to 0.6 inches of rainfall over the affected area. Subsequently, Capitol Reef National Park officials reported approximately 8 to 10 inches of water flowing through Sulphur Creek near the Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center. A visitor report of knee- to thigh-deep water within Spring Canyon was also relayed from a Park Ranger.

Scattered thunderstorms moved across the area from late morning through the afternoon hours. Radar estimates indicated 1.25 inches to 2.5 inches of total rainfall near the affected area. A Park Ranger with the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument subsequently reported and sent pictures of Hole-in-the-Rock road near the 25 Mile Wash area, where floodwaters associated with the rain overtopped road culverts and resulted in a minor road washout.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across southern Utah on Saturday, moving across the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument towards the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. Locally heavy rainfall was associated with these thunderstorms, with radar estimated rainfall from around 0.75 inches to 1.5 inches noted across the Buckskin Gulch area. Two flood waves resulted, as noted on the Paria River at Lees Ferry gauge, downstream of the canyon. This gauge showed an initial gradual increase to around 50 cfs over the course of 2 hours, followed by a rapid increase to approximately 150 cfs over 15 minutes. The second bump would correlate to roughly a 1 foot rise at Lees Ferry, which would be much higher in the narrow slot canyon area of Buckskin Gulch. During the time of flood waves propagation through the slot canyon, at least 2 permitted hikers were hiking through the canyon. They were reported to be planning on hiking approximately 5 miles into Wire Pass and the Buckskin Gulch slot canyon areas. Kane County Sherriff's department received word of a deceased person within the trail, and subsequently recovered the bodies of two deceased individuals. It is believed that the men drowned in the initial flood wave, and were then washed 7 to 10 miles downstream.
Multiple reports of several roads came in for having water over the road.
Three high water rescues occurred at the US Highways 87 and 60 interchange in Canyon. Hospital Drive, Hunsley Hills Boulevard, and Country Club Drive were all closed as well.
At Alta Lodge, along state Route 210, flooding left mud and debris on the road, with cars stuck and some homes flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Cedar City, impacting the Cedar City Hospital, Iron County Jail, and homes.
The Escalante River at Escalante gauge was at 583 cfs.
Zion National Park reported flash flooding at Refrigerator and Echo Canyons.
There was a 798 cfs rise on the East Fork of the Virgin River on gauge ESTU1.
Flooding was reported in the town of Bicknell, with water flowing across streets.
Debris with mud was reported in Huntington Creek resulting from flow from the Trail Mountain Burn Scar.

A cluster of thunderstorms produced heavy rain during the early afternoon hours through portions of Capitol Reef National Park, with Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor estimates of around 0.50 to 0.75 inches of rain. Subsequently, Capitol Reef National Park reported that state Route 24 east of the visitor center was impassable due to high water and debris. Additionally, minor flooding was reported in the campground.

An emergency manager reported 4 manhole covers removed along state Route 36 between 200N and 600N, with heavy rain and thunderstorms noted in the area. As a result, there were multiple reports of residential flooding in the area.

Flash flooding was reported on Short Creek and its tributaries through the Hilldale and Colorado City area. All creek road crossings were closed for 2 to 3 hours, and the Hilldale Street Creek crossing was heavily damaged and subsequently closed indefinitely until repairs could be made. This flooding is the result of strong thunderstorms which per Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor, produced approximately 3.00 to 4.00 of rainfall, largely within the span of 2 hours, though some of this can likely be attributed to hail contamination. At 6:25 am MST on the 14th, the downstream Fort Pearce Wash gauge recorded a spike in flow to 124 CFS associated with the flood water propagation.
There were reports of flooding at a campground in Cedar Canyon. The Cedar Canyon stream gauge reported a significant rise.
A flash flood was reported in Capitol Gorge and Grand Wash.
Diamond Fork Road was closed between the Diamond Campground and Three Forks Trailhead due to water and mud on the road.

A 64-year-old woman was reported overdue from a hike on the Fairyland Loop Trail. A search of the area was conducted, with the woman being found deceased. Details are unclear, but showers and thunderstorms were in the area. A news release from Bryce Canyon National Park stated dry washes had higher flows because of precipitation. Though not conclusive, a medical examiner report stated the cause of death was likely due to drowning.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported multiple flows and waterfalls associated with heavy rain and thunderstorms moving through the park. At approximately 11:46 am MST, multiple waterfalls were noted on cliffs. By 11:55 am MST, water was reported to be coming over state Route 24, and by 11:59 am MST, debris, in addition to water, was noted. At approximately 12:30 pm MST, the wash south of Hickman Bridge through Neil Johnson Bridge was reported to be flowing high, and the Hickman Bridge area was reported to be flooded.
The Dirty Devil Gauge near Hanksville reported a rise over 700 cfs.
Videos and reports of flooding and mudslides in Indian Canyon near mile post 278.

Moderate rain during the morning hours, with Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor estimates of around 0.50 to 0.75 inches of rainfall, resulted in Flash Flooding across portions of Zion National Park in addition to river flooding. Park officials reported that multiple drainages were flashing, with the North Fork Virgin River near Springdale gauge peaking at 605 CFS and the East Fork Virgin River near Springdale gauge peaking at 320 CFS.
Zion National Park reported multiple waterfalls through southern portion of the park, the biggest of which was noted near Twin Brothers.

As a result of heavy rain in the area, the East Fork Virgin - Springdale, guage recorded a rapid rise in flow from its initial general flow level of around 68 CFS. An initial peak of 1228 CFS was observed at approximately 4:00 pm MST. The river then fell to 359 CFS at approximately 7:00 pm MST, before rising again to a secondary peak of 858 CFS at approximately 11:00 pm MST.
Flash flooding caused a closure of state Route 24 due to water covering the road from mileposts 81 to 85. The flooding led to an evacuation of the Fruita Campground and Gifford House.
A flash flood was observed on Wahweap Creek.
Park rangers reported flooding on Sulphur Creek and adjacent drainages. Floooding in Capitol Gorge resulted in a multiday road closure of the Scenic Drive.
Flash flooding forced the closure of St George Regional Airport, with flights diverted. Fort Pearce Wash Gauge reported a flood wave peaking at more than 400 cfs.

Zion National Park rangers reported multiple large waterfalls throughout the park. Additionally, the river gage on the Virgin River at Virgin recorded an increase in flows from 77 cfs to 1604 cfs between 12:00 and 1:00 p.m. MDT.

Bryce Canyon National Park Rangers reported rock slides and deep mud along the Navajo Loop trail as a result of heavy rain in the area. This resulted in damage to retaining walls along the trail, and as such, the temporary closure of the trail.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a spike to just over 400 cfs.

The Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument Big Water Visitor Center reported a flash flood wave along Wahweap Creek that was audible from the town of Big Water until around 8 pm MST. A survey of the creek at the Smokey Mountain Road low-water crossing the following morning revealed the flood wave was approximately 60 to 75 feet wide at some point overnight, which would roughly equate to around 3 to 4 feet of depth at this particular point. This flooding was associated with heavy rain that fell within the far headwaters from approximately 3 pm MST to 5 pm MST.

Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument Kanab Visitor Center officials reported flash flooding in the town, with local streets flooded and covered with mud and debris, resulting in closure of a few streets. Creeks through town were overflowing across roads at culverts, and in one spot, Kanab Creek was overflowing across the road with water approximately 9 to 12 deep. Dirt roads on the outskirts of town were impassable. Additionally, Kane County Sheriff's office officials reported that several homes had some minor basement flooding. This flooding is the result of strong thunderstorms in the area, with Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor estimates of approximately 0.75 to 1.50 of rainfall in around 3 hours.
Zion National Park reported flash flooding near Twin Brothers Mountain, just north of SR-9.
There were reports of street flooding, road closures, and vehicles stranded.
Running washes lead to the closure of North Vulture Mine Road in Wickenburg. No damages or injuries were reported.
Zion National Park reported multiple waterfalls and high flows at various locations throughout the park associated with ongoing rainfall.
Social media pictures and video indicated fast moving water flowing down a residential street. Emergency management reported an estimated three feet of water in some spots on the southside of Pampa.
