Widespread flooding on State Road 67 with numerous road closures across the county. Total rainfall ranged from 2.8 to 4.4 inches.
Several roads closed due to water flowing over them within the town of Rockville. Total rainfall was around 2.1 inches.
Many sections of Rushville were impassable due to flooding. Several streams nearby had near record flooding. Total rainfall ranged from 2.7 to 3.1 inches.
Water surrounded residences on 5th St South in Phenix City.

Heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches in Loretto caused flash flooding across Lambs Ferry Road, likely caused by heavy rainfall rates causing the nearby Bluewater Creek to overfill its banks. Extent of damages is unknown.
Heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches near St. Joseph caused flash flooding along Fairview Road east of South Old Miliary Road with a tree and mud covering part of the roadway. Damages are a rough estimate.
Route 251 closed due to water over the roadway.
NYS Thruway/I-90 at exit 46 flooded.
Water rescues occurred between Avon and Lima.

Flash flooding due to heavy rain occurred over Texas State Highway 70 between Girard and Jayton. Several severe thunderstorms moved over the same area producing multiple rounds of heavy precipitation.
Heavy rain from severe thunderstorms repeatedly trained over central Garza County resulting in flash flooding in and around Post. Numerous streets in and around Post were inundated with water.

Heavy rain across Hickman County caused flash flooding, particularly along waterways and across low-lying areas. By the end of this event, observations and radar estimates showed 5 to 8 inches of rain had fallen across Hickman County. Extent of damages is unknown.

Heavy rain across Williamson County resulted in widespread flash flooding, especially along waterways and across other low-lying areas. By the end of this event, observations and radar estimates showed 5 to 8 inches of rain had fallen across Williamson County. Extent of damages is unknown.
City officials reported flash flooding near Lomas Blvd. and Central Ave. with several roadways in the area under high water.

Emergency manager and stream gauges reported flash flooding developed in south Charlotte, mainly along Little Sugar Creek and Little Hope Creek after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in just a couple of hours. Little Hope Creek overflowed its banks and inundated part of Mockingbird Lane. Little Sugar Creek flooded a portion of Wakefield Dr, covered a part of Reece Rd with a couple of feet of water, and approached some homes south of Archdale Dr. Emergency manager reported multiple swift water rescues of motorists in south Charlotte. Media reported multiple cars stranded in floodwater in the Pineville area.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed across central and southern York County after 3.5 to 5.5 inches of rain fell in just a few hours. Inundation of Wilson Chapel Rd occurred in the Sharon area, likely due to Bullock Creek overflowing its banks. One lane of Bookout Rd in McConnells was flooded by water from South Fork Fishing Creek. A tributary of Stony Fork flooded Stallcup Rd just southwest of Rock Hill. Phil Grant Rd was washed out near Strait Rd near the Chester County line due to a small drainage. Additionally, extensive yard flooding was reported in a neighborhood on the north side of Rock Hill due to Big Dutchman Creek overflowing its banks. However, other than water entering a couple of outbuildings, no structures or roads were impacted in this area.
Emergency management reported significant flooding in a Fairfield neighborhood with at 1-2 feet of water running across yards and streets.
Anderson County Emergency Management reported flooding of low lying areas across the county with 4.55 inches of rain measured in Tennessee Colony.
Emergency management reported that Luella Road at the Choctaw Creek bridge, about midway between Luella and Sherman, was flooded by one foot of water.
Emergency management reported that multiple streets in Bridgeport were flooded. Pioneer Road in New Fairview was also closed due to high water..
Broadcast media reported a home flooded on Dynasty Drive in Glenn Heights.
Widespread flooding across Hempstead County, with multiple roads covered in high water and closed, with others washed out. Flash flooding damaged the Ozan Creek Bridge on Hempstead Road 26.

During the late afternoon hours of April 24, 2025, a supercell tracked over the Omaha metropolitan area, with rainfall totals of 2.5 to 3.5 inches along a swath from Ralston in SW Omaha through northwestern Pottawattamie County led to flash flooding in portions of Omaha. Considerable flooding was reported in the Saddle Creek area with water up to the windows of vehicles and dumpsters floating.
The intersection of FM 2493 and FM 2813 was flooded.
Near record flooding occurred on the Big Blue River near Shelbyville with numerous roads closed during the overnight hours due to flash flooding. Total rainfall ranged from 3.1 to 3.6 inches.

Intense rainfall from a slow moving storm occurred in and around Happy. A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Happy measured 1.62 inches of rainfall in less than one hour. An mPing report was received of flooded roads in Happy.
Rapidly rising water from Rock Run impacted Rock Run Road and approached nearby homes.
Water was flowing across Cook Street between Eastdale Drive and Dirksen Parkway.
East Van Buren Street was closed due to high water under the viaduct.

On the morning of August 9, 2025, flash flooding struck the Blair, Nebraska area, particularly Southern Washington County, following a storm that delivered 3 to 4 inches of rain. Rainfall rates peaked at 2.5 to 3 inches per hour. Public reports confirmed significant impacts, including 6 to 10 inches of fast-moving water flowing through an apartment complex parking lot, and striking photos of residential backyards inundated with 3 to 5 feet of standing water. Minor flooding was also observed along Cauble Creek.

Heavy rain caused Jacobs Station Road near Towers Road to flood. Neighborhood yards also had about 1 foot of water in them. 2 miles west of Harvester, there was maybe a foot of water over an unnamed road. A small 2 door car stalled in these waters. Dardenne Creek rose onto St. Peters Howell Road. Up to 1 foot deep water was reported in nearby homes from the creek.
Broadcast media reported that McKinney Street at Ennis Avenue was flooded, and a car was stalled in flood waters on Ennis Avenue at Clay Street in the city of Ennis.
Street and road flooding was reported via mPING in Holland.
High water was rushing across Decoursey Pike.
Mud Lick Branch Creek came out of its banks. Old Sweet Owen Road was closed due to mud and debris on the roadway from the flowing water.
Several roads were flooded in and around Moccasin.

On the morning of August 10, 2025, heavy thunderstorms pushed through the Lincoln, Nebraska metropolitan area, triggering flash flooding across northwest Lincoln and north-central Lancaster County. Measured rainfall totaled 3.12 to 3.69 inches, with radar estimates confirming a similar 3 to 4-inch range. The intensity of the storm was the primary factor, with rainfall rates peaking at a severe 1.5 to 2.5 inches per hour. Public reports included major travel disruption, with Cornhusker Highway completely covered in water between Interstate 180 and Highway 77 at 1:55 AM CST.
Several roads were flooded including the intersection of MS Highway 9 and MS Highway 182, the intersection of MS Highway 9 and Fox Avenue, and parts of Waterworks Road.
The I-30 Westbound right hand lane was closed due to flooding.
High water covered Shiloh Road between Broadway Avenue and New Copeland Road.
High water covered South Georgia Street in Troup.

An estimated 9 inches of water was flowing across 15th Street in Lawrenceville, prompting the closure of the road in a few spots. In addition, water was flowing across parts of 12th Street and James Street.
North Point Road closed between Willow Road and German Hill Road for 6 inches or more of flowing water over the bridge at Bread and Cheese Creek.
Coakley Town Road near Bank Church Road closed due to at least 6 inches of water flowing over the road. Debris in road from washouts.
Old Chesterbrook Road closed at Pimmit Run due to at least six inches of water flowing across the road.
Reports of several roads closed in Dundalk due to high water. This includes North Point Boulevard near I-695, German Hill Road, Broening Highway, and Merrit Boulevard.
Joppa Farm Road closed near Philadelphia Road due to at least six inches of water flowing over the roadway.
A picture was posted to social media of high water covering Highway 19 between Delight and Prescott.
Multiple county roads were washed out, including CR 31 and 16.
Portions of FM 747 southwest of Jacksonville were flooded.
The intersection of Canada Street and Beaumont Street in Jacksonville was closed due to flooding.

A water rescue took place on Illinois Highway 13 near Lenzburg due to a vehicle being stranded in flood water. Heavy rain of up to 5.25 to 6.1 inches fell in St. Clair County during the duration of the event.

Numerous roadways across Washington County were deemed impassable due to floodwater. Nearby communities to these roadways include Nashville, Okawville, Lively Grove, Saint Libory, Addieville, Hoyleton, Covington, New Minden, Venedy, Beaucoup, and Wamac. Over the duration of the event, up to 7 inches of rain fell. At times, rain rates were in excess of 2 inches per hour.

Flash flooding reported in North Randall, Bedford, and Solon. Flooding reported on US-422 between Miles Road and Cannon Road in Solon, with up to a foot of water inundating the roadway. Brainard Road under US-422 was closed due to flooding. Northfield Road southbound was closed in North Randall between Emery Road and Miles Road due to flooding. Rainfall amounts estimated from 1.5 to 2.5 inches in a 1 to 2 hour period, which equates to a roughly 1 in 20 annual recurrence interval.

Flash flooding in northern Trumbull County. 12 to 18 inches of water completely covering Painesville Warren State Road between Leiby Osborne Road and Doty East Road from an overflowing creek. Berm and part of road washed out at Hoffman Norton Road near County Line Turnpike Road in Southington Township. Radar estimated 2 to 3 inches of rainfall in 2 to 3 hours, which equates to a 1 in 100 to 200 year annual recurrence interval.
South Main Street on the south side of Bridgeport just south of the railroad tracks was closed due to flooding from Indian Creek.
Numerous roads flooded near Cade.
High water covered County Road 25 in Northern Lafayette County.
A section of Highway 275 just north of Strong was closed due to high water.

Emergency Manager reported flash flooding throughout the city of Barnwell. EM observed 4.8 inches of rain at their home and stated that many city streets flooded as storm drains could not handle that amount. Time estimated by EM.
A car was stalled in high water adjacent to an insurance office along Highway 110 on the north side of Whitehouse.
FM 449 near Franklin Road was closed due to flooding.

Multiple instances of flash flooding were reported in St. Louis County due to heavy rain. Reports of flash flooding varied across the county. One report stated there was 2 to 3 feet of standing water on a road adjacent to Wildhorse Creek near Chesterfield. Another was of a stranded vehicle at the intersection of I-70 and I-270. Cold Water Creek also rose out of its banks in Hazelwood and entered the parking garage of the Hazelwood Civic Center on Dunn Road. The same creek came about 1 foot from reaching businesses on Bypasse Drive in Hazelwood. There was also a public report of roads closed due to flooding in Oakville. Rainfall amounts across the county vary from 2.5 to 6.3 inches ending on April 6th.
A report from mPING was received of street/road flooding or closures in Fort Stockton. Urban flooding was likely due to a slow-moving supercell thunderstorm. Time is estimated from radar.

Heavy rain produced flooding across sections of Lafayette, Carencro, Youngsville, and Milton. Numerous streets were flooded with many impassable with cars stranded. Water entered businesses in downtown Lafayette and some homes in Youngsville had 3 to 4 inches of water inside. Amounts up to 8.59 was reported in Lafayette Parish.
Numerous roads flooded around New Iberia and Loreauville. Amounts up to 6.84 was reported during the event in Iberia Parish.

Numerous reports from the public on social media showing water flowing over several roads from Lake Orion to east of Lakeville, and areas south into the Oakland township. One video in particular shows water flowing over 32 Mile east of Lakeville, with active runoff flowing towards and over the road from the higher terrain south of 32 Mile. Oakland Township also had a number of road closures due to flooded roads.
Public reported flash flooding across streets with a few vehicles stranded.
High water was rushing across a portion of Garner Road.
Highway 80 near Lansing Switch Road was closed due to flooding.
Multiple county roads across Harrison County were flooded and closed.

Heavy rain caused Joachim Creek to rise out of its banks near Crystal City and Valles Mill and caused Saline Creek to rise out of its banks in Jefferson County west of Fults, IL. Up to 7 inches of rain fell in portions of Jefferson County between April 4th and the evening of April 5th.

Heavy rain caused a few road closures in Jefferson County. One road closure was near Regina on Missouri BB and Regina Road. Here, downed power poles were reported. The other was near Imperial around US Highway 61/67 and Scott Lane/Mill Creek Drive/Montebello Road.

Multiple water rescues were reported in St. Francois County, one in Blackwell and another in an unnamed location in northern St. Francois County. Near Libertyville, an estimated 3 feet of water was running swiftly across Highway DD into a small lake across the street. The lake was reportedly spilling onto the road.

A report of street/road flooding or closures was received from mPING on the northeast side of Fort Stockton. This was likely the result of a slow-moving supercell thunderstorm. Time is estimated from radar.
A social media post showed an oil field road closed due to flooding of a low-water crossing near the Pecos River in far southern Eddy County. The time was estimated from radar.

At 2:53 AM MDT, a swift water rescue was conducted near a low-water crossing at Black River near Black River Road. A vehicle was reported to have been swept downstream. No injuries were reported. The time is radar estimated. Property damage is an estimation.

Flash flooding in the Albuquerque arroyo channel system resulted in a fatality. The body was first spotted in the Hahn Arroyo near Pennsylvania Ave. in northeast Albuquerque before the deceased body was retrieved in the arroyo washout pond at the end of the North Diversion Channel near 4th Street and Edith Blvd. in the North Valley.
High water covered Butler Avenue near the Zaxby's in West Monroe.
Various roadways in the Claiborne community in West Monroe were covered in high water.
Public reported a creek overflowing due to flash flooding.
High water covered Mansfield Road just south of Barron Road beneath the railroad overpass.
Widespread flash flooding ongoing across Marion county. Several cars stranded in flowing water. Rainfall amounts varied from 2 to 3.25 inches.

An NWS storm survey revealed significant flooding south of Crosbyton along several roadways. A slow moving supercell thunderstorm produced very heavy rainfall over an extended period of time over areas of rural Crosby County. Farm to Market 40 was covered in mud in several areas east of Texas Highway 207 indicative of water over the roadway on the night of the 24th. Most of the county roads were muddy and impassable at the time of the storm survey.

An emergency manager reported multiple vehicles trapped in high water on I-70 eastbound under the East Carrie Street overpass. This is a low area. A vehicle was also trapped in flood waters in St. Louis at Lindell Boulevard and Vandeventer Avenue. These areas received between 2 and 4 inches of rain.

Heavy rain resulted in lots of running water over Highway 94 near Terri Road. This made the road completely impassable. Near St. Paul, there were reports of heavy flooding north of Dalbow Road, though the extent of the flooding is unknown. Otherwise, there was a report of Dardenne Creek overflowing in St. Peters. This area received anywhere from 3 to 6.5 inches of rain over the duration of the event.

The Department of Highways and the public reported multiple inaccessible roads in Franklin County due to flooding. These include parts of Highway A and Highway YY due to side ditches overflowing and Highway CC due to Big Creek flooding over the road and onto the other side. Notably, this is a low point on the highway. On April 5th, the Missouri Department of Transportation reported that Route W just past Sand Ford Road at the entrance to Meramec Caverns was closing due to flooding of the Meramec River. Franklin County received up to 6.2 inches of rain during this event.

Several road closures were reported mainly in the Ellington area has rainwater flooded roadways and areal creeks overflowed. Examples of road closures include: MO 106 1 mile west of Route F, Route B between CR 785 and CR 784, and CR 838 at its intersection with CR 837. Logan Creek overflowed, making its bridge on Route B impassable and causing extensive damage to the bridge.

At 4:41 AM MDT, a swift water rescue was conducted at a low water crossing over the Black River along Higby Hole Road. No injuries were reported. The time is estimated using radar. The property damage is an estimation.
Social media video shows flooding on Boothe Road near Twin Beech Road.
Roadways in the Grundy Cooper Neighborhood of Alexandria were flooded and some were impassable.
Social media reports and county 911 dispatch reported that Indian Creek washed out Belfast Mills Rd at the intersection of US 19.

Flooding along Woodland Hills Road in Abingdon. Additional pictures received at 11:45 PM EDT via X show water running over neighborhood road, and water pooling in low spots to a depth of several inches, inundating the lower portions of mailbox posts. Standing water was also visible in front yards. A total of 2.5 inches of rain had fallen at the time of the second report.
Phone call report of Fall Hill Road being completely flooded, causing damage to the road.
Pictures were posted to social media of significant street flooding in Lindale.
Portions of Caples Road was flooded, forcing a vehicle off the roadway.
Portions of Cypress Street was flooded, with water reportedly entering a restaurant.
Public report of street flooding due to flash flooding and a few vehicles stranded.
Public reported road flooding due to flash flooding and a few vehicles stranded.
Multiple streets were covered in high water throughout Shreveport, requiring several high water rescues.
Water was flowing over Layhigh Road near Chapel Road. Water was overtopping the road at the location of a culvert.

An NWS storm survey revealed significant flooding northeast of Post along several roadways. A slow moving supercell thunderstorm produced very heavy rainfall over an extended period of time over areas of rural Garza County. Water was flowing over Farm to Market Road 2008 three miles south of Farm to Market Road 651 along McDonald Creek. Most of the county roads were muddy and impassable at the time of the storm survey.

The Missouri Department of Transportation has reported multiple road closures in Iron County due to flooding that began on April 3rd. Some of these closures continued into May. Road closures include: Route F from CR 160 to CR 135, Route 40 at Route BB, and Route F from Missouri 49 to CR 165. Over the duration of the event, portions of Iron County received up to 7.5 inches of rain.

Fourche a Du Clos flooded over Highway Y at Jackson School Road deeming it impassable through the first low bottom bridge headed eastbound. A water rescue was reported at this location. On April 5th, water was reported over the roadway near Missouri 32. During the event, portions of Ste. Genevieve County received 3.75 to 6.25 inches of rainfall.
The Dent Branch of the Big River was reportedly swiftly running over Highway C where a bridge crosses the road. Rainfall totals through the event were on the order of 2.5 to 4.3 inches.

The 911 Call Center reported numerous events in Fredericktown including water over the roadway at Morley St and Villar St, City Lake Road, Buford Boulevard, Highway Z and North Chamber Drive, the 200 block of East College, and North Main Street. Southeast of town, Route F was closed where it meets Route V due to flooding. During the event, up to 7.75 inches of rain fell in Madison County.
A report from mPING of street/road flooding or closures near I-20 was received. Time is estimated from radar.
South Texas Street was flooded.
High water covered Highway 37 just south of Bogata.
Widespread flooding across the city of Monroe, including the residential areas. High water blocked the entrance of the Monroe Civic Center, and high water covered portions of Louisville Avenue.
A report of street/road flooding or closures was received from mPING.

Several roads were flooded and closed around Warren including 1943 East and West, CR 4475, FM 1013 CR 4478. Multiple other roads had water covering them, but were not closed including CR 4470 and CR 1450.
At least four to five inches of flowing water occurred across the intersection of FM2391 and County Line Road.
Heavy rainfall resulted in up to eight inches of standing water along 23rd and 25th avenues on the north side of Pampa.
Several inches of water were flowing across the roadway near the intersection of Wilfred and St Charles Avenues.
Several inches of water were flowing across Carlisle Avenue and Tacoma Street.
Reports of flash flooding were received in Keansburg on Belleview and Center Avenues.
A vehicle became stuck in flood water under the railroad underpass on Gibraltar Road.
Multiple flooded roadways reported around Nazareth due to flash flooding.

A slow moving supercell thunderstorm trained over areas of Motley County producing very heavy rainfall and flash flooding. An NWS cooperative weather observer reported flash flooding within the city of Roaring Springs as well as flooding over Texas State Highway 70 between Matador and Roaring Springs.

Town Creek in Salem rose rapidly due to heavy rain and was level with Eastlawn Cemetery and Tully Park. The emergency manager in Salem issued a voluntary evacuation of Starlight Mobile Home Park, which occurs anytime flooding conditions of this scale are present. A majority of main routes in and out of Salem were inundated with water and closed with cars floating in the floodwater down West Main Street. The reservoir overflow channel was topped and water flowed into the town park and inundated homes to its south. In Centralia, 4 to 5 fete of water covered Locust Street near a major production facility. Heavy rains of up to 8.5 inches fell during the event.

Heavy rain caused several feet of water over County Road 18, leading to a vehicle becoming submerged. The occupant was safe. Route 4 north of Sparta also had water over the roadway. During the event, up to 4.5 inches of rain fell in Randolph County.
A storm chaser reported that a large stretch of FM 2400 was under approximately 6 inches of rushing water. The entire road is flooded. Time is estimated from radar.
High water covered portions of Highway 49 in low lying areas. A local tow operator estimated water 6-8 feet deep in some areas.
High water covered multiple roads in Gilmer.
Flash flooding throughout the Texas side of Texarkana. High water covered Exit 220 on I-30 West.
A picture was posted to social media of flooding near businesses along Highway 110 South.
Flash flooding was reported along Marietta and Thornton Roads.
Water was rushing over Walnut Creek Road.

Several inches of water were flowing across Westfall and Bush Mill Roads near State Route 207.
Multiple streets were flooded in Beaumont with one water level gage reported water just under 2 feet over the roadway near downtown.
A part of FM 2400 was reported flooded out by at least a foot of water. A few vehicles were unable to cross the road at either end. The time is estimated from radar.
A report was received from mPING of street/road flooding or closures in portions of Snyder. The time is estimated from radar.
Heavy rain across Stewart County caused flash flooding, especially along waterways and within low-lying areas. Extent of damages is unknown.

Heavy rain across Stewart County caused flash flooding, especially along waterways and within low-lying areas. By the end of this event, observations and radar estimates showed 8 to 11 inches of rain had fallen across Stewart County. Extent of damages is unknown.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Houston County, especially along waterways and across low-lying areas. Extent of damages is unknown.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Houston County, especially along waterways and across low-lying areas. Extent of damages is unknown.

Flash flooding was reported along Taylor Canyon on the afternoon of June 4h. This flooding eroded a six food embankment along White Rim Road in Canyonlands National Park, and carried sediment all the way to the Green River. Additionally, several washes along Taylor Canyon Road ran and washed out sections of Taylor Canyon Road. No other damages, and no injuries or fatalities, were received.
High water was observed on Oil Creek Road.
West of the town of Danville, flooding was observed along Lick Creek Road.
Multiple reports of flooded roadways and water impacting residences in Centre. Hardwood Hills Dr was flooded, with homes surrounded.

Numerous roadways were flooded or washed out in southern and southeastern Cherokee County, including the Spring Garden area. Street flooding was occurring in Willow Springs.
State Highway T was closed due to flooding.

USGS stream gage at Rocky Branch at the intersection of Main and Whaley exceeded flood stage, reaching a maximum height of 9.6 feet. Webcam from this intersection showed a stranded vehicle in flood waters as the creek flooded the road.
Columbia Fire Dept reports a flooded vehicle with water rescue operations on Key Rd at Market Rd.

Heavy rain from severe thunderstorms resulted in five inches of water on 8th Street near Eddy Avenue and 6 inches of water on Park Lake Drive in Santa Rosa, NM.
Flooded roadways around 18th Street and Kilgore Avenue from heavy rainfall.

Water reported over 1st Ave and 40th. Vehicles were unable to pass through due to water depth. Time was provided by Law Enforcement.

Whitewater creek completely out of its banks at Timberline golf course. Low areas of golf course flooded. Most creeks full or overflowing in southern Dubuque county. State Highway EE was closed due to flooding.

Hwy 109 closed between Wells and Alden due to water over the roadway. Two county roads west of Alden were damaged due to flooding (CR 61 and CR 51). One Carlston Township road (630th Av north of Hwy 109) was also damaged due to flooding.
Flash flooding reported across the highway with a high water rescue that occurred.
Flash flooding reported in downtown Tyler.

There was water over the roadway with debris at Knickerbocker Road.

Columbia Fire Dept reports a flooded vehicle with water rescue operations at the 900 block of Gadsden St.

In the town of Volga, high water was observed around a few homes.

Slow moving thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and rushing water across NM Highway 117 near El Malpais National Monument. The highway was temporarily closed during this time until flood waters fully receded.

Heavy rain from a slow-moving thunderstorm produced flash flooding in Waynesboro, with high water rising over roadways. Locations impacted included North Welty Road on the east side of town along the East Branch of Antietam Creek. Vehicles were stranded due to flash flooding.

These winds were accompanied by a torrential downpour in Colorado City, resulting in rapid flooding in the immediate area. The initial downpour lasted approximately 45 minutes and produced street and highway flooding, with standing and moving water measured at approximately 3-5 inches in most areas, generally still traversable by passenger vehicles. Approximately 15 minutes after the rain began to lessen, reports of flooding were received for Interstate 25 at Milepost 77 and Milepost 70. Milepost 70: Flooding slowed traffic but did not result in any reported traffic accidents. Milepost 77: Flooding rendered the interstate temporarily impassable to most vehicles, with large debris present on the roadway and several traffic accidents reported. Within approximately two hours after the storm passed, water had fully receded from all roadways, and no further significant closures or incidents were reported.

An estimated 3 or more feet of water was on the frontage roads.||The rain in this area came in multiple rounds. A first round occurred between 430 and 6 PM, with additional rounds between 7 and 8 PM and again fro 930 to around 11 PM,and a final windy round around midnight March 28th CST (1 AM CDT). Water rescues were first reported in Mercedes at around 7 PM CST (8 PM CDT). As of this writing, damage was unknown but hundreds of structures likely had varying degrees, ranging from affected to major damage. ||High water would continue well into March 28th and beyond; the flood control system (floodway) had up to 20% capacity due to spillage and pumping of urban flood areas into it. ||Full damage statistics will be available later in 2025.

The highest water was at least four feet in spots along the frontage south of the McAllen Convention Center. Rainfall rates were historic for the season, ranging from 1/100 to 1/200 probability events (annual return frequency) over a 2-hour period. McAllen/Miller Airport, located just south of IH-2 and just west of 10th Street, recorded 6.25 in two hours. ||Additional reports of 2 to 3 feet of water were received from the City of Pharr, with two to three feet of water depth at the intersection of N. Cage Blvd. and E. Ferguson Ave., along/near the IH-69C frontage. Residual urban flooding and high water would continue into March 28th and beyond in some areas.||As of early July, a county-wide estimate of Public Assistance (PA) and Individual Assistance (IA) damage was $52 million in Hidalgo County. Thunderstorms developed over the Redlands area of Grand Junction late in the afternoon of September 4th, and remained there for 2-3 hours. Impacts began to be noticed around 6:45 PM MDT, with an LSR in the area of 1 ESE Redlands indicating Water out of the banks of nearby wash and running over Redlands Parkway in several areas. Approximately half an hour later, another LSR indicated that water running over the roadway in many areas along South Camp Road in the Redlands (Redlands 1SSE). Debris was also reported as having to be removed from Monument Road (Redlands 3SSE). In addition to the LSR'd events, properties were flooded, normally dry washes were overfilled, and water and debris inundated several roadways in the area. Additionally, social media reports indicated flooding along No Thoroughfare Canyon, Monument Road, and in the Devil's Kitchen area of Colorado National Monument. Once the rain stopped and the storms dissipated, a local spotter provided the total precipitation from this storm, which was a 2.33 inches.

Widespread and numerous reports of flash flooding in streets, in addition to rivers, creeks, and streams across the southern two thirds of Milwaukee County. 1800 homes were classified as major damage or destroyed due to flash flooding of the Lincoln and Honey Creeks. Many instances of flooded basements across the impacted area. Six foundations collapsed into basements of homes in the 60th street neighborhood near Lincoln Creek, with two homes being condemned. At 16 feet, flood water is approximately 1 foot over the top of the concrete-lined channel of the Kinnickinnic River at Milwaukee, affecting homes in the residential neighborhood next to the river. Widespread flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods and homes occurred especially in New Berlin, Brookfield, Menomonee Falls, Waukesha, Pewaukee, Merton, and Muskego. Some of the more notable creeks or rivers that flooded were the Fox River, Jewel Creek, and their tributaries, as well as some lake flooding. Some flood damage occurred to homes especially near Linnie Lac Lake toward Little Muskego Lake. These damages were from a variety of 1st floor flooding, basement flooding, and foundation collapse. Residential sewage backups, and raw sewage released into rivers by many municipalities were common. A small number of complete road washouts and swift water rescues occurred, in addition to dozens of people stranded in their vehicles in deep, still water in low lying areas. More specifically, one lane of Gold Dr. washed out due to the flash flooding of Jewel Creek in Muskego. Large sections of Barker Road in Brookfield and other nearby roads were closed due to the flash flooding of the Fox River, including the Fox River overtopping the Barker Rd. bridge. Dozens of people were evacuated or relocated from their flooded homes and neighborhoods, which included the Deer Path Subdivision near Minooka Park. A sidewall of the Merton Millpond Dam was damaged but quickly repaired. Many other dams in eastern Waukesha County were at or exceeding their maximum flow capacity, but no dam failures occurred.

Flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in West Bend and other communities over northern Washington County. Some vehicles were stranded in relatively deep, still water. Widespread flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods and homes occurred especially in New Berlin, Brookfield, Butler, Menomonee Falls, Elm Grove, and Muskego. Some of the more notable creeks or rivers that flooded were the Fox and Menomonee Rivers and their tributaries. The Butler Ditch, Jewel Creek, Root River, and other unnamed creeks also flash flooded. For all of Waukesha County, 3 homes were classified as destroyed, 310 homes and businesses sustained major damage, 221 with minor damage and 119 with affected damage. These damages were from a variety of 1st floor flooding, basement flooding, and foundation collapse. Residential sewage backups, and raw sewage released into rivers by many municipalities were common. A small number of complete road washouts and swift water rescues occurred, in addition to dozens of people stranded in their vehicles in deep, still water in low lying areas. More specifically, a partial road washout occurred on Lily Road in Menomonee Falls due to the flash flooding of a tributary of the Menomonee River. The large collapse of a Y-shaped intersection at Campbell Dr. and Campbell Ct. in Menomonee Falls also occurred due to the flash flooding of Butler Ditch. A car was swept away at this intersection but the occupant escaped with minor injuries. 130 St. in New Berlin was partially washed out from the flash flooding of a tributary of the Root River. A swift water rescue occurred on Beres Rd. in New Berlin when a car was swept off the road by floodwaters. Dozens of people were evacuated or relocated from their flooded homes and neighborhoods. Rain amounts of 0.2-0.3 inches in an hour caused a debris flow that trapped cars near MP 103 of Hwy 21. This surprisingly small amount of water produced a mudslide because of two important reasons. First, the Wapiti burn scar last year burned very intensely in the flood location, leaving lots of ash and debris on the ground. Second, this portion of Hwy 21 is notorious for avalanches because of it's steep, fairly sparse forest. The very steep open slopes that were primed with ash allowed the small amounts of water to run off almost immediately, carrying debris and mud with it.

Slow-moving thunderstorms brought heavy rain for several hours to Burnet on the morning of July 5. Burnet Municipal Airport reported 8.67 inches of rain. An LCRA gauge in Burnet reported 11.67 inches. The torrential rainfall caused the rapid rise of Hamilton Creek. Additional inundation also occurred along Daugherty Branch and Haynie Branch in Burnet. Homes, businesses, and other buildings along Hamilton Creek experienced up to 7 ft of inundation. Oak St. in the northwestern part of the city was especially hard hit by the swollen Hamilton Creek. Around a dozen homes along the road were damaged, primarily near 7th and 8th Street. One house was torn off its foundation and was carried by floodwaters onto the opposite side of the street. Several businesses were flooded along South Water St. A 57 year old man was swept by floodwaters while commuting through Burnet along US 281. His body was recovered about a quarter mile away from his vehicle along Hamilton Creek. Most of the units at the Hamilton Creek Manor housing complex were impacted by floodwaters. Fields at YMCA of the Highland Lakes on the south side of Burnet were damaged by flooding with fences washed out and dugouts damaged. Pafford Place Assisted Living was heavily damaged. An 85 year old man at the facility drowned in the flooding. Seven others were successfully evacuated from Pafford Place. Parts of Burnet Municipal Airport experienced 5 to 7 ft of inundation, resulting in damage to PAPI lighting and the runway. Several homes were inundated along Delaware Creek to the west and southwest of Burnet with washouts on roads. Across the county first responders rescued at least 63 people. The county Emergency Manager estimated more than 400 homes were affected and the damages were at least $6 million.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Jackrabbit Wash recorded a water level above the alarm stage level of 2.9 feet, with a peak stage of 3.78 feet. Exceeding alarm stage corresponds to likely flooding of Wickenburg Road located approximately 5.1 miles downstream of the gauge. There was an extended period of greater than 900 cfs with flow peaking at 1560 cfs, resulting in likely greater than 1.5 feet of flowing water over the road. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach Wickenburg Road. Catastrophic and deadly flash flooding occurred in the Globe area following strong to severe thunderstorms that produced very high rainfall rates. Observed gauge reports and doppler radar rainfall estimates measured approximately 2 inches of rain within 30 minutes in the Globe area. A stream gauge along the typically dry Pinal Creek, just south of Downtown Globe, recorded a dramatic 6-foot rise in water in 30 minutes between 1825MST and 1855MST. This flood wave quickly moved through downtown Globe, overtopping bridges, inundating businesses, and sweeping away dozens of vehicles. Many sloped streets also became raging currents. Additionally, around 800 propane tanks were swept into the floodwaters from a distribution center along the creek. Several dozen homes and businesses were inundated with water, with some experiencing water levels of two to three feet deep. Floodwaters traveled over 15 miles north of Globe, within Pinal Creek, all the way to the Salt River and Roosevelt Lake with additional flooding impacts experienced in the Wheatfields area. A USGS gauge on Pinal Creek just south of the Salt River recorded an 8 ft water level rise and came within half a foot of reaching the gauge's historical peak. In the aftermath of the flooding, approximately 288 tons of trash and debris as well as 800 cubic yards of dirt were cleared. There were also over 60 vehicles damaged or destroyed, with some of them wedged under bridges. The flooding resulted in three fatalities, all from vehicles swept away. In response to the catastrophic flash flooding, Globe's Mayor, Al Gameros, declared a State of Emergency for Globe on the afternoon of the 27th followed shortly by an Arizona State of Emergency declaration from Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs. Preliminary damage assessments performed in the subsequent days had estimated damage costs of approximately $25 million.
